metadata.description: Full raw proverb corpus (5000 Proverbs source), auto-tagged by theme.

entries.luganda: Ababiri babibira ebigambo : naye abasatu babisattula.
entries.english: Two make plans : but three frustrate them.
entries.meaning: A secret is better kept by two than by three. Engl. "Two is company, three is a crowd". Notice the play on words!

entries.english: He was in a whirlwind (under the influence of a sudden fancy, not his usual self).

entries.luganda: Abafugibwa ngabo : atannagikwatamu ye agitenda obwangu.
entries.english: Those who are ruled are like the shield : who never got hold of it, thinks it light.
entries.meaning: Those who don't rule think ruling is easy.

entries.english: Those who love each other need only a small place.
entries.meaning: Although the but may be small, they live happily together. Engl. "Home is home, be it over so homely".

entries.luganda: Abaganda bakaabira ekitali kyabwe : amaziga ne gajja.
entries.english: The Baganda quarrel about a thing that does.not belong to them : and then the tears come: Don't worry about other people's business!

entries.luganda: "Abaganda baakalya olumanyo" : buli ajja nti Nkonge wuuyo.
entries.english: "The Baganda just had an intuition (felt it instinctively)" : because everyone coming said: "There is Nkonge".
entries.meaning: So the Banyoro said once during the wars between the Baganda and the Banyoro : A Munyoro with the name Nkonge happened to hide himself from the passing army of the Baganda, near the road, just where there was a stump of a tree in the path. So every warrior passing warned his followers: look out! here is a stump (nkonge). The poor man in hiding thought they had seen him, came out and was killed. - Okulya olumanyo = to feel instinctively.

entries.english: The Baganda are like the stinging nettle : they sting themselves on it with open eyes.
entries.meaning: Giving hospitality to thieves, marrying a mulogo, having bad friends.

entries.english: (If you tell the Baganda) "You go round the miyagi-bushes" (i.e.
entries.meaning: you are evasive, dishonest in talk) : (they answer you) "We only get rid of the kafumbe-smell". The ffumbe (civet-cat) has an offensive smell which it leaves on the grass and on the bushes where it has been passing and which remains also on the clothing of the passers-by. To get rid of that smell the old Baganda walked round miyagi-bushes.

entries.luganda: Abaganda nswa engabo bazisuuliranga ku mabega.
entries.english: The Baganda are like flying ants : they put their shields on their backs.
entries.meaning: With the shields on their backs they look like flying ants with their wings folded.

entries.english: The Baganda are like flying ants : they cover themselves superficially.
entries.meaning: Outwardly kind, inwardly angry.

entries.english: The Baganda are useless fellows (lit.
entries.meaning: poor, homeless) : the kasukusuku-mushroom has no termites. The kasukusuku-mushroom grows on dry banana-leaves rotting on the ground and has no long root (as the ggudu-mushroom has) which the other mushrooms drive through channels built by the nkuyege (termites), i.e. the Baganda are said to have no roots (foundation, firmness); "tibeesigwa".

entries.english: Visitors are like banana-stumps : they make room for others that follow.
entries.meaning: The old banana-stumps rot away and make room for the new shoots. Germ. "Sie reichen sich die Klinke".

entries.luganda: "Abakadde ka batabaale" : nga talina wuwe; naye obanga alma, "Abakadde bayinze".
entries.english: "Let the old men fight" (one might say) whose father is not there; but if his father is there, he says: "Ah, no, the old people are beyond that".
The trumpeters (horn-blowers) : blow in harmony.
entries.meaning: They work together, although they might be of different character. Community spirit.

entries.english: Peasants are like crickets : they establish themselves where the soil is prepared.
entries.meaning: They settle down where the chief has occupied his land.

entries.english: Peasants are like millet : where you break up the soil (on which millet has been growing), new millet grows.
entries.meaning: The people who have been killed by the king, are followed by others. - "Sanguis martyrum semen christianorum".

entries.english: "The parents eat good food" (says the greedy child) : and falls with the packet of food (hanging from the roof).
entries.meaning: The child could hardly reach it. Prompt punishment for greediness!

entries.luganda: Abakulu n'abakulu tibaleekaana : 1) singa Nnamasole ayitiriza Mulere; 2) ekigere we kifuluma kiwakanya kinnaakyo.
entries.english: Big people don't quarrel with each other : 1) otherwise the mother of the king would interrupt the Mulere.
entries.meaning: The Mulere is a "mwami wa kabaka" and the head of the king's flutists. His position is so high that even the Nnamasole won't interrupt his business, but waits till he has finished. Big people don't quarrel with each other : 2) otherwise one foot would inter-fere with the other.

entries.luganda: Abakulu n'abakulu tibaseerana mukubi (nva) : nga za mazzi (= nga si za munnyu).
entries.english: Grown-ups don't quarrel about vegetables (little things) : if they are watery (if they are tasteless).
"The people here don't like me" : (so says) who has only rags to dress himself.
entries.meaning: He expects them to clothe him better.

entries.english: The Balemeezi are like the root-stocks of banana-plants : they are left in the cooking pot.
entries.meaning: Such root-stocks are only famine food and not appreciated.

entries.english: The Balemeezi are daring : they prevent even their ssaza-chief from passing.
entries.meaning: When they are busy catching enswa on the road, everybody has to go round them, they won't budge.

entries.english: (One who remarks) "The boys help themselves to matooke and are chewing (heartily)" : is giving a hint to the woman.
entries.meaning: He is afraid that he won't get enough to eat.

entries.english: "Boys, put them (the matooke) into your claws (fingers), dive into it" : (one who says so) has only a narrow place where he could put (more food).
entries.meaning: No more room. He has had enough.

entries.english: People living together won't fail to quarrel (now and then).

entries.luganda: Abalirira ekigula (= ekyagala) enkumbi : tawa munne ssooli ddene.
entries.english: One who counts in a miserly fashion the price of a hoe : does not give his neighbour much maize.
entries.meaning: A stingy fellow does not profit the community.

entries.english: Those present here fight for their places (for precedence).
entries.meaning: An expression used as a riddle (ekikokko): Nnina mukazi wange, erinnya lye "Abali wano balwanira ebifo". Answer: ensanafu.

entries.luganda: Abalungi mbwa ya nnamaaso : bw'etebba n'eyigga.
entries.english: The beautiful are like a dog with big (beautiful, strange) eyes : it might turn out to be a thieving dog or a good hunter.
entries.meaning: "All that glistens is not gold".

entries.luganda: Abalungi ndagala nnamu : teziggwa mu lusuku.
entries.english: Beautiful women are like fresh banana-leaves : they never come to an end in the bananary.
entries.meaning: There will always be beautiful people.

entries.english: Those who have ugly teeth : God gives them their meat.
entries.meaning: Blessings of God are not dependent on good looks.

entries.english: Three chiefs : but one throne.
entries.meaning: Katikkiro, omuwanika, omulamuzi, all three are governed by the Kabaka. Or: The three cooking-stones form one seat for the cooking pot (entarnu).

entries.english: The children of the poor man : make fat those of the rich one.

entries.luganda: Abaana ba Kintu : tibaggweerawo ddala (= tibaggwawo kufa).
entries.english: The children of Kintu (legendary ancestor of the Baganda) never die out.
entries.meaning: Mankind is constantly renewed. - Narrower sense: there will always be Baganda in the world. - "Baana-ba-Kintu" is also a propei name.

entries.english: "The children have not enough yet" (says he) : but he thinks of his own stomach.

entries.luganda: Aba n'ebingi ng'abimma : aba n'ebitono ng'abigaba.
entries.english: The person who has many things is mean (refuses to give) : he who has few things gives them away.
entries.meaning: Riches harden the heart; poverty softens it.

entries.luganda: Abangi babi kulya : naye ku mirimo balungi.
entries.english: A crowd is bad for eating : but good for work.
entries.meaning: Both are finished quickly.

entries.english: If many help, they will catch the "nsonzi" (small fish).
entries.meaning: Many hands make light work. Germ. "Viele Hunde sind des Hasen Tod".

entries.luganda: Abangi bwe bakusiima (= bakwebaza) : ng'olubimbi luweze.
entries.english: If many congratulate you on your work : your day's cultivation is at its end.
entries.meaning: You have worked long and well.

entries.english: A whole crowd does not obey : but rain makes them listen.
entries.meaning: They run away and take shelter. It takes a powerful personality to rule a crowd.

entries.english: Where there are many, they won't agree entirely.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Quot capita, tot sententiae".

entries.english: Where there are many : somebody will be offended.
entries.meaning: Some will surely be grousing.

entries.luganda: Abangi we basimba olunwe : we kyabikira.
entries.english: If many people touch the boil (put their finger on it) : it will burst.
entries.meaning: Power of public opinion. Lat. "Vox populi, vox Dei".

entries.english: People are like cleaned banana-stems : one cannot hide in them.
entries.meaning: Bad reputation follows one everywhere. Germ. "Nichts ist so fein gesponnen, es kommt doch an die Sonnen".

entries.english: People are like the stinging nettle : they get stung by it whilst seeing it.
entries.meaning: They run into trouble with open eyes.

entries.english: People are grateful as long as they are eating.

entries.luganda: Abasajja ssubi : erimu lisiba linnaalyo (= buli erifuluma lisiba linnaalyo).
entries.english: Men are like grass : one stalk is used to tie the rest.
entries.meaning: As grass is tied into bundles with other grass, so outstanding people dominate others.

entries.luganda: Abatabaazi (or: ababaka) basula ku luba (= basula kumpi).
entries.english: The warriors camp on our side (i.e.
entries.meaning: quite near, on this mutala).

entries.english: Farmers who like each other : dig up the lumbugu (grass).
entries.meaning: They do not quarrel about digging up the weeds on their common boundary.

entries.english: Farmers are like pigs : they eat properly at night.
entries.meaning: When the others have gone, they indulge in a proper feed. - Also the wild pigs feed at night.

entries.luganda: Abataka nkwenge : gw'olya naye ye akutta.
entries.english: Landowners are like parrots : the one with whom you eat, kills you.
entries.meaning: One is the enemy of the other. "Abalabe b'omuntu banaabanga ba mu nnyumba ye" (Matt.10.36).

entries.luganda: Abataka tebeesigwa : omuntu enviiri z'azaalibwa nazo, bw'afa nga zivaako, ng'asigaza amannyo agaamera obukulu.
entries.english: Farmers are not trustworthy : man loses the hair he was born with, when he dies and retains the teeth which he had grown in later age.
entries.meaning: Good things of old are forgotten soon.

entries.luganda: Abatongole bikya bya mbuzi : tibyegaana mugwa.
entries.english: The citizens are like the necks of goats : they don't refuse the rope.
entries.meaning: They might murmur behind the chief's back, but they have to obey.

entries.luganda: Abayita ababiri bajjukanya (= bejjukanya) : enviiri zikulaga (= zikutegeeza) engo, bwe weesisiwala.
entries.english: Two who walk together warn each other : your hair, bristling, gives you warning of the leopard.
entries.meaning: Your hair always goes with you and, when the presence of a leopard is sensed, the fright makes your hair stand on end. - Mutual help of friends.

entries.luganda: Abaziika abafu okumpi : be babaleetera okululuma.
entries.english: Those who bury the dead in a shallow grave (or: near the house) : cause them to haunt the living.
entries.meaning: Only the near-related are buried near and then in a deep grave.

entries.luganda: Abeegeyera ku nsiko : be bawa abataka empoza.
entries.english: Those who take a counsel (plot together) on the uncultivated land (i.e.
entries.meaning: before they come near the chief) : give the citizens a chance of defence. Prepared and concerted action.

entries.english: If two men fight for a stick (with equal force) : neither will get it.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Duobus certantibus tertius gaudet". Dutch "Als twee honden vechten om een been, loopt een derde er mee heen".

entries.luganda: Abeera awawe tabulako ky'akola : ekirevu kizina kirabye emmere.
entries.english: The man who is at his own home has always something to do : the beard dances, when it spots food.
entries.meaning: The mouth behind the beard is the proper home for the food and gets busy when food is in view.

entries.luganda: Abika atali wuwe : abika ayanjala engalo.
entries.english: One who brings the death-notice of a person who is not his relation : spreads out his hands.
entries.meaning: One who is personally grieved, looks depressed.

entries.english: (ebiswa) The person who covers two anthills (at the same time) : does not pick up flying ants.
entries.meaning: Whilst he is busy on one, the ants fly away from the other. Splitting of energy! Concentration! Lat. "Age quod agis".

entries.luganda: Ab'oluganda baagalana : nga bombi bali mu ngoye (= nga bonna bali mu mwera).
entries.english: Relations love each other : as long as both parties are rich (or: as long as they are all in funds).
entries.meaning: "Okubeera mu ngoye" or "okubeera mu mwera" stands for "being rich". "Lwera" = copper; "mwera" = cents. - Selfishness. French "Ami jusqu'd la bourse".

entries.english: "My relations will revenge me" (says the man who has been wounded to death) : but perhaps he perishes unrevenged.
Relations are like beer-calabashes : they bump against each other, but don't break.
When relations quarrel : don't put your oar in!
entries.meaning: Don't meddle in other people's business. Both parties will attack you.

entries.luganda: Ab'oluganda n'oluganda tibaagalana : essanja lyokya ebitooke.
entries.english: Relations do not love each other : the dry banana-leaves burn the green banana-plants.
entries.meaning: If the banana-stems are not freed from the dry leaves (ssanja), a grass-fire can destroy the whole bananary. Leaf burns leaf. - Perhaps it is also taken from the custom of singeing a green banana-leaf with burning ssanja, to make a luwombo.

entries.luganda: Ab'oluganda olaba nga basuulana embazzi : nga banaagikumma.
entries.english: If you see that brothers (relations) blame each other for having mislaid the axe (which you came to borrow) : they intend to refuse it to you.
entries.meaning: They only pretend to blame each other.

entries.english: One who talks, thinks : but one who keeps silent, thinks more.
One who explains things to an intelligent person : need not tire himself out talking.
entries.meaning: Not much explanation is necessary. Lat. "Sapienti sat" (Terentius, Phormio 3.3.8). "A word to the wise is enough" (B.Franklin).

entries.english: One who moulds a bad (water) pot : adds a bowl to it (in order to attract the buyer).
One who eats often (in many places) cold food (left over) : also gets his fill.
entries.meaning: One who tries perseveringly, will succeed. - Lat. "Nulla dies sine linea" (Pliny).

entries.english: The man who often comes to see (whether) the mushroom (has broken through) will take it.
entries.meaning: He can pick it at the right time. Certain mushrooms always grow in the same place.

entries.english: He died in absolute helplessness (with no possibility of resistance) like the bananas (in the beer-vat).
One who possesses makes fun (of others who have nothing).

entries.luganda: Afuuye eŋŋombe : nga talagaanye na bayizzi.
entries.english: He has blown the horn : without making arrangements with the hunters.
entries.meaning: If the hunters do not know by whom the horn has been blown, they do not come. Organisation is necessary, wherever people are supposed to work together.

entries.english: He who distributes (things, food) among many : satisfies no one.
Big birds (aganyonyi) that don't fly in formation : knock each others' wings.
entries.meaning: No public spirit, no esprit de corps. Unplanned work!

entries.english: (amenvu) "What is the news?" (so one asks) : (but they intentionally misunderstand him and pretend to hear "the ripe beer-bananas, what do you do with them", and they answer) "We throw them into the bananary; those which ooze out mubisi, we use for drinking".
If the teeth get discoloured : they blame the tobacco for it.
entries.meaning: If one writes a bad hand, the pen is at fault. If the food is not ready, the fire-wood was wet.

entries.english: If the water (in a river) decreases : it concentrates in the middle (from where it started spreading).
entries.meaning: In need one returns to the original sources.

entries.english: Eyes that look into each other : respect each other as those of Mbajja and Mugema.
entries.meaning: "Mbajja" and "Mugema" are titles of two outstanding personalities in Buganda. Mbajja was "mwami omukulu wa Kabaka", Mugema is the title of the ssaza-chief of Busiro, the "kojja wa Kabaka, amusumika olubugo".

entries.english: One who lies in ambush : will no doubt kill somebody.
One who reminds the orphan of his misery : makes him cry (even if it is done with kind compassion).
What tires out the one who sets the trap : also tires the animal (when it is caught).
entries.meaning: Lat. "Nil sine magno labore vita dedit mortalibus" (Horace).

entries.english: The eyes (of those) who will eat and (of those) who will not eat : are all looking at the cow (being slaughtered).
entries.meaning: All who plant expect results; but not all will obtain them.

entries.english: Dances that promise entertainment : do not wait for the drum to start.
entries.meaning: Pleasant things need no command.

entries.english: (amata) The milk that is drunk by the little one : the mother throws away.
entries.meaning: If the little child has drunk too much from the mother's breast, it vomits (= abooga, azza amabeere) and the mother has to clean it up.

entries.luganda: Agatali maawule : gookya ngalo (or: gookya emimiro).
entries.english: Undivided lumps of matooke : burn the fingers (or: the throat).
entries.meaning: Lat. "Divide et impera". French "Diviser pour regner" (Louis XI).

entries.english: (amatu) Ears that don't listen to their master : cover (= are thrown on) the young banana plantation.
entries.meaning: Cutting off the ears was in olden times punishment for disobedience.

entries.english: Carelessness in small things : leads little by little to ruin.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Principiis obsta : sero medicina paratur" (Ovid). Ecclesiasticus 19.1. 0122 "Ag'emitala gajja?" : "situgawulira". (amawulire) "Does the news of the other side of the water arrive?" : (answer) "we don't hear it". P. 0123 Ag'emputtu : gakubya nnyinigo. The ears of an obstinate child : cause their owner to be boxed. Germ. "Wer nicht horen will, muss Millen".

entries.english: (The fact that) one goes away weeping : does not prevent you from sending kindest regards.
entries.meaning: Said of newly married wife taking leave of her parents, or children leaving. The tears will dry.

entries.english: A man who goes to a place where they eat nkolo (root-stock of banana, famine-food) : does not leave his knife at home.
entries.meaning: "Bulya-nkolo" is the name of a village. To prepare that food he needs a knife. One who is going to do a special job, takes the necessary tools along.

entries.english: One who goes back to his home : does not consider the night too dark.
If a man goes to a place he knows : he is not overtaken by the night.
entries.meaning: He finds his way even in the dark.

entries.english: If a person goes away from home with a good friend : he does not mind being in foreign lands.
entries.meaning: Even if his own people despise him, he fares well with his friend. Lat. "Ubi bene, ibi patria".

entries.english: (A suspicious husband, asked, when he intended to come back, answers) "One who travels, sees (what will happen)", i.e.
entries.meaning: "I can't tell you now". He does not tell in how many days he will return. - He wants his wife to be in uncertainty.

entries.english: The man who washes out the salt (into the lusoggo, the funnel made with a green banana-leaf) : gives orders to the one who grinds the pulp.
entries.meaning: The latter does the heavier work. - Ordering is easier than obeying. 12.14. 0132 Agenze butasiibula : nga njala. (cf. Okugenda kiserebetu: 3698) 65.6.

entries.english: He went away without saying good-bye : like a soldier (7th army) going to war.
He went away in a great hurry like the mpawu-termites (when swarming).
The person .who speaks evil about someone who loves you : makes you report the slander (to the offended person).
One who speaks evil of another who calls herself "a bad cook" : won't listen to objections from her, because she does not claim to be a good one.
entries.meaning: Or: He who speaks evil of "Nnanfumbambi" : can do so with impunity. Nnanfumbambi, a chief at Mpumu (Kyaggwe) used to tie bells to his feet, so that everybody was warned of his coming. One talking evil of him could stop in time. Or: He who speaks evil of "Nnanfumbambi" : does so at his own risk. Nnanfumbambi, as Ssabaddu of the Ssekiboobo, was the latter's intimate friend and therefore it was very risky to arouse his indignation. 21.107, Munno 1921 p.129. 0138 Agitta : tagiwoomya? Does the one who kills the cow (or the chicken) which he got as a present : not make it sweet (to the one who gave it)? Should the one who got such a present not let the donor participate in the meal? Custom of "kuddiza".

entries.luganda: Agoberera : y'asamba; nga si gwe balese.
entries.english: One who follows (others) : hurries (to catch up with them); unless they have left him purposely.
He fell and got up quickly : like a hunchback (omuntu w'ebbango).
entries.meaning: A hunchback is short and therefore he has not much trouble in getting up again.

entries.english: (One who complains) "He refused it (the beer) and very decidedly" : goes (in search for beer) in the evening (when they have finished it all).

entries.luganda: Agya amangi : ye agamanya kye geddira.
entries.english: He who has many fetishes : knows the taboos of each one (e.g.
entries.meaning: that some might not be touched after eating certain food; or, that certain fetishes may only be used with peculiar ceremonies). Men are like these fetishes: each one has to be treated according to his character and peculiarities. A ruler ought to know his subjects personally and intimately.

entries.english: (eddagala, ejjembe) He who has obtained his food through the medium of the fetishes, should not be annoyed, if visitors come to eat with him.
entries.meaning: Christian version: We should let others partake of the gifts God has bestowed on us.

entries.luganda: Ajaganya ng'akimezezza okw'enjala : bwe siikoze nnaawuuta.
entries.english: He is dancing for joy like one who has managed to grow a big mushroom in famine time (and exclaims) : if I have no food to dip into the sauce I can sip the sauce.

entries.luganda: Ajja ekisana : tasooka mukeeze kukyusa buwufu.
entries.english: He who arrives when it is already hot : does not turn back before the one who came early in the morning (to put up again the grass which is trodden down).
entries.meaning: "First come, first served". Germ. "Wer nicht kommt zur. rechten Zeit, muss haben was ubrig bleibt". - Okukyusa (= okuweeta) obuwufu: to turn back.

entries.english: The one who draws the attention to "Busemba" : will beat it.
entries.meaning: "Busemba" was the name of the drum of death in the lubiri, up to the time of king Mwanga. After the inthronisation of the king all the drums were carried out, except Busemba, which was left as if inadvertently. One who drew the attention to the apparent oversight, was immediately seized and put to death, and his armbones were prepared as drumsticks for this drum. Custom abolished by Mwanga II. at the request of the Europeans.

entries.english: One who reminds (somebody) of an offence suffered : gets a whole army to fight.
(The mutongole-chief) who bullies the landowner : starts by breaking his sugar-canes.
entries.meaning: Then he confiscates a goat, etc.

entries.english: (I am like) an edible rat : I am left with the remnants of the food (in the field).
entries.meaning: Wailing of one who has lost all his relations.

entries.english: (The poor man) laments among his people (relations) : seeing (feeling) that they will give him something.
entries.meaning: Other people will only have excuses.

entries.luganda: Akabi kaliva gy'oli : ng'omuntu akuba n'omusota omukago.
entries.english: The evil comes from yourself (you have only yourself to blame for) : like one who makes blood brotherhood with a snake.
A day's work, though small : is better than a holiday (doing nothing).

entries.luganda: Akabi nga kanajja : lubaale akwata mukyawe.
entries.english: If evil is to come : the evil spirit gets hold of a woman who is despised and prophesies through her.
entries.meaning: They will not take notice of her and will take no precautions.

entries.english: An evil does not hide itself.
entries.meaning: If you have heard of a calamity, you won't fail to tell others about it.

entries.luganda: "Akabuzi akato tekeevumbulira ggenekere lyako?" : ng'oli avuvuba omuto ku bibye.
entries.english: "Do you think the little goat will not find its tasty bits by itself?" : (this is what one asks his neighbour) if he interferes with a little child's business (interests).

entries.luganda: Akabwa ke weeyolera : ke kakuluma enteega.
entries.english: The little dog that you have brought up for yourself : is the one that bites your calves (lit.
entries.meaning: the hollow of the knee). Ingratitude. Dutch "Ondank is s'wereld's loon". 11.14. 0161 Akaddiya akajwina ke : y'amanya bw'akatunga. One who has grown old with his rags : knows how to mend them.

entries.english: The animal that dies from over-eating : will not haunt (the living).
entries.meaning: They fed it well and therefore it bears no grudge.

entries.english: What travels with food : does not see trouble (does not suffer hunger).

entries.luganda: Akaggo akakuba muka balo : w'akalaba akakasuka.
entries.english: If one of the wives sees the stick that beats her fellow-wife : she throws it into the wilds (or: into the fire).
entries.meaning: The husband might one day beat her as well. - Interested charity.

entries.luganda: Akagoma akatono : kakutuusa ku ggoma ddene.
entries.english: A small drum (chieftainship) : leads you to a big one.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Natura non facit saltum".

entries.luganda: Akajabangu ak'omubumbi : 1) g'azimba g'ayokya; 2) w'asula watonnya, essubi n'alissa omuliro.
entries.english: The stupidity of the potter : 1) the houses he builds (with sticks and grass to burn his pots) he burns again; 2) the rain comes in where he sleeps and yet he destroys with fire the grass (which could be used for thatching).
Thoughtlessness makes an unmarried fellow dig a well.
entries.meaning: Formerly the bachelors were not supposed to live by themselves and had there-fore not to care about a personal household.

entries.english: Lack of reserve that makes one, who does not drink beer, dance.

entries.luganda: Akakadde ak'obuggya : amaggwa gakafumita emirundi ebiri.
entries.english: The old fellow full of envy : the thorns (on the road) pierce him twice.
entries.meaning: After the first time he does not remove the thorns from the path, because he wishes others to step on them; the second time he forgets that he left them there and steps on them again.

entries.luganda: Akakuli mu linnyo : tikaganya lulimi kutereera (= kwebaka).
entries.english: The little morsel between your teeth : gives your tongue no rest.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Ein schlechtes Gewissen ist kein sanftes Ruhekissen".

entries.luganda: Akaakyama amamera : tekagololekeka; bw'ogolola omenya bumenyi.
entries.english: (akati) What grew crooked when young : cannot be straightened (later).
entries.meaning: "Just as the twig is bent, the tree is inclined". A child must be taught (corrected) when young. Germ. "Frith kriimmt sich, was ein Haken werden will".

entries.english: What is according to agreement : does not bring special interest.
entries.meaning: If one has done what he promised (e.g. to pay back his debt at a certain date), he cannot be fined.

entries.english: What will become a proper calabash : you can judge by its stalk (pedicel).
entries.meaning: The qualities of the boy often predict the man of the future. "The child is the father of the man" (Wordsworth). Germ. "Frith krummt sich, was ein Harkchen werden will".

entries.english: The tongue of a borrower : is smooth in its approach.

entries.luganda: Akalina abiri : otega kalaba (or: olonda ejjinja kalaba).
entries.english: (akasolo or akanyonyi) An animal that has two eyes : sees where you put the trap (sees when you look for a stone to hit it).
A thing that causes an elephant to fall : how small may it be!
entries.meaning: It is not strength (bulk), but cleverness that beats the mighty.

entries.luganda: Akamira eyiye : 1) taginyoola; agamba, nti "nnakiyumba" gireke egejje; 2) tagiseera mata (= tagimma mata).
entries.english: The milker : 1) does not turn away the calf's mouth (from the udder); but he says: let nnakiyumba (name of the calf) suck and get fat!
entries.meaning: The milker : 2) does not cheat his own calf out of its milk (leaves always suffi-cient milk for the calf in the udder). Care for one's own children! Personal interest.

entries.english: A hasty tongue : makes you answer your creditor.
entries.meaning: If you were aware that it was your creditor, you would keep quiet in your house and he thinking that you are not at home, would leave again.

entries.english: Too quick a retort : kills the one who has made it.
A man's mouth : is not a cow's mouth (which ruminates).
(akaswa) As soon as the little nswa appears : I shall pick it.
entries.meaning: Applied to a person who claims everything for himself, leaving nothing to others.

entries.luganda: Akaana k'obulenzi : tokaweera mpindi mu ngalo.
entries.english: You don't give a little boy beans with a bare hand.
entries.meaning: You should use a basket or a banana leaf, because he will one day be a man, a ruler, leading the way for women folk.

entries.english: The agreement binds the trapper (the man of the nets) and the one who roasts the meat.
entries.meaning: All who have worked together deserve a reward.

entries.english: What can spoil a bargain : is (often) a small thing (amount).

entries.luganda: Akaneene bwe kaluma omuya : nga tekalumye ngalo.
entries.english: If the "kaneene" (an otter-like animal) has bitten through the net (basket) : it has not bitten your fingers.
entries.meaning: It could have been worse.

entries.english: He (the mukopi) is trying hard to keep the wild animal away from the chief's place.
entries.meaning: Said of a tenant who stands by his chief, warns him of approaching danger etc.

entries.english: The hunter does not know how disappointed the dog is.
entries.meaning: The dog has to do all the hunting and gets only bones and entrails.

entries.luganda: Akasibe akabi : ke kaleesa ettambiro okumpi.
entries.english: A little prisoner (led away to be killed) who is obstreperous : brings the killing place much nearer.
entries.meaning: The king or the executioner might give orders to kill him on the spot.

entries.english: Silence : 1) makes the lizards fight (they feel safe); 2) causes hurry.
entries.meaning: Seeing that the conversation stops, when you come near, makes you pass quickly. Ominous silence!

entries.english: (Which is) the animal that even the king skins himself?
entries.meaning: : the forest-onion. A riddle: everybody eating a forest-onion (Sassa tisselata) skins it himself, even the king. - There are things which are not done by proxy. Rub.C.1598, Ebiko-kko 66.

entries.luganda: Akasolo tekannafa : nti "Omukira gwa jjembe lyange".
entries.english: The animal is not dead yet : (and you say) "I add its tail to my charms".
entries.meaning: "Don't count your chickens before they are hatched!" - Dutch "Verkoop de huid niet, voordat de beer geschoten is". Dhop. "Ikir gen bwoyo ngor ni magira".

entries.luganda: Akasubi kamu : bwe kava mu nju, tetonnya.
entries.english: If one grass-stalk falls from (the roof) of the house : it won't leak.
entries.meaning: A small loss is negligible. No reason for alarm. Lat. "Parum pro nihilo putatur".

entries.english: A man who throws the spear he has : is no coward.
entries.meaning: Use the gifts that God has given you. Lat. "Ut desint vires, tamen est laudanda voluntas" (Ovid).

entries.luganda: Akasukka (= akasusse) omumiro : nga tikakyabalibwa (= tekabalwa).
entries.english: What has passed the gullet : is not counted any longer (if one is not satisfied yet) Charity is soon forgotten.
A market with many wares and moderate prices : sells out.

entries.luganda: Akatale ka mmese : katunda keekuba ensiko.
entries.english: The market place of the rat : sells when it (the rat) has gone to the wilds.
entries.meaning: The rat carries foodstuff from the house into the holes outside.

entries.luganda: Akatali kabbe : eggumba osuula mu mulyango.
entries.english: What is not stolen : its bone you throw through the doorway.
entries.meaning: You are not afraid, that you will be noticed eating it.

entries.english: (akasajja) The little man who won't build a house : is the one who carries the reeds cross-wise.
An animal that mistrusts itself : does not bring forth twins.
entries.meaning: The one which trusts its breasts (udder) risks it.

entries.english: If a mushroom just breaks through the soil (in your courtyard) : will you dig it out at once?
entries.meaning: Better wait and let it grow fully.

entries.english: "The little matooke did not taste good (to me)" : (so you say) if you have not cooked it (yourself).
entries.meaning: To blame others is easier than doing it better.

entries.english: A little thing that is there : is worth more than a big thing that only has been promised.
entries.meaning: "Half a loaf is better than no bread". "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush".

entries.english: (akantu, akalabo) A little service out of friendship : is worth more than a great service which is forced.
(akalabo) A small gift (service) received : makes you give a big one.
entries.meaning: You don't want to be outdone in generosity.

entries.english: Even a small thing is taboo in the eye.
entries.meaning: The eye tries at once to wash it out with the tears. - A tender conscience is disturbed even by small faults. - A small grain of sand can put a big machine out of order. 88.65. 0230 Akatono kazza omukwano. (akantu, akakolwa) A little thing restores friendship. To give a little thing to an old friend reminds him of the old friendship. 63.51, Ssal.p.6. 0231 Akatono okalya ne munno : bw'akwata enkukunyi, anyigira ku kinkumu. A little thing that you eat with your friend : (comical illustration) when he gets hold of a flea he crushes it on his thumbnail. Cooperation between the two thumbs. Friends help each other in everything.

entries.english: (akazaana) The slave girl sent to king Kyabaggu for fire (light).
entries.meaning: She had given birth to a child and could risk asking the king directly for it, as he was the father of the baby.

entries.english: A gift (okuwa) is not equally appreciated by two different persons.
entries.meaning: "There is no accounting for tastes".

entries.luganda: Akawundo k'emputtu : 1) bakasalira mu muzinnoonyo gwa lulagala; 2) kage-ndera mu ndagala.
entries.english: The (insect-eating) bat is a silly thing : 1) they cut it up in the rolled-up banana-leaf; 2) it enters the banana-leaves (and is caught therein).
entries.meaning: It is too slow and too silly to fly away.

entries.english: In an instant, quickly : as the lubaale priest disappears between the sugar-canes.
One who is keen to restore friendship : does not pay damages.
entries.meaning: He is likely to be forgiven. Germ. "Ein gutes Wort findet einen guten Ort".

entries.english: A little grass-fire : is the cause of a big compensation.
entries.meaning: It can cause a big conflagration. The one who caused it, will have to pay for the damages.

entries.english: Clouds of black smoke : will kill a whole army.
entries.meaning: Behind those clouds it is easy to prepare for battle and to surprise the enemy.

entries.luganda: Akendo we kawoomeza amazzi : we kaatikira.
entries.english: When the ladle makes the water sweet : it breaks.
entries.meaning: Often just those things get lost or broken to which we are most attached. - Loss of one's dearest friends.

entries.english: He who attends the chief's court : is informed on current affairs.
He is looking alarmed : like a big bushbuck at which the knife is being thrown.
He is not telling the truth, saying "the good (nice) people have all gone".
entries.meaning: Superficial judgement! If he would observe more people and not for a moment only, he would see that even now there are many good ones. - Lat. "Laudator temporis acti" (Horace). 89.95. 0253 Akivaamu : y'akiyita ekyato. After stepping out of the canoe : he calls it names ("that blessed canoe"). "Ekyato kino kintobezza". Before it was "kaato akalungi". Discarded things (old people etc.) are despised, although they have done good service once. - "Speak well of the bridge that carries you over".

entries.english: You purchase a thing quickly : if you have its price in your pocket.
He does what is done already : like one who takes the water pot off the head of the one who comes from the well.
entries.meaning: The "kutikkula" is nothing, compared with the fetching of the water.

entries.luganda: Akola (= akoze) bya mbyone : ow'obusa by'akola ewaabwe.
entries.english: He (she) acts in a "the devil may care-manner" : as an unmarried girl does at home.
entries.meaning: She thinks: I won't remain here very long. Leisure and carelessness make her do those things.

entries.luganda: Akombye mu (kikuta) kya kkobe : eky'ettungulu kiwoomerera.
entries.english: He has licked the skin of the kkobe (aerial fruit of yam-species) : that of the ttungulu (blood-red fruit of the forest-onion) is sweet.
entries.meaning: Used as an absolute refusal (= nnanidde ddala). Rather let me lick the kkobe than the ttungulu. I'll give nothing to him. I'll be damned - -.

entries.luganda: Ako nno katiiro : akatiiza embwa n'eggumba.
entries.english: That is now fidgeting about (nervousness, suspicious restlessness, jealousy) : that causes a dog with a bone to take it from one place to another (lest another dog should find it).
(ente) He is tired : (the others) raid.
entries.meaning: If a raider gets tired too soon, his fellow-raiders take all. - Losing one's chances by giving up too soon.

entries.english: He who beats the children : beats all of them.
entries.meaning: They all become afraid and suffer with the beaten one. Compare the riddle: "Bakazi bange bwe mbakuba, bonna bakaabira kumu" (Ebikokko No.47) i.e. enkuyege!

entries.english: He is warning you (with a discreet wink) : do you want one from a wrestler?
entries.meaning: The wrestler gets hold of you and forces you. Germ. "Ein Wink mit dem Zaun-pfahl!" M.45, Ssal.p.3.

entries.english: One who beats his own child : beats with half-closed hands (fingers).
entries.meaning: Not to hurt it too much.

entries.english: He is overdoing it (is importune) : like a dog wooing.
One who comments on your song : does not make it sweeter (better).
entries.meaning: A spiteful person will interpret your song (or any of your words) in a criticising slandering way.

entries.luganda: Akugoba ye akuwa ekkubo (= ye akuwa amagezi) : nti "Ab'emmanga, mbawee-rezza".
entries.english: The one who pursues you shows you the way (of escape) : (he shouts) "You down there!
entries.meaning: I am driving him towards you!" Hearing that you naturally branch off. Said about a thief running away.

entries.english: One who reminds you : serves you better than one who abuses you.

entries.luganda: Akukanga : tabula ky'akusuuza; bw'atakusuuza malusu n'akusuuza eminyira.
entries.english: One who frightens you : is sure to make you drop (what you are holding); if he does not make you lose your spittle, he makes you lose snot.
If one is your superior at home, he is your superior even in the forest.
entries.meaning: Give honour to your elders wherever you are.

entries.english: One who does evil to you : you repay him by doing good.
He has defrauded you (robbed you of your goods) : (as) leprosy does to the fingers.
One who makes faces at you behind your back : respects you.
entries.meaning: He is afraid to do that to your face.

entries.english: One who makes faces at you in front of you : eats the gum of your eye.
One who hits your stick : incites you to a fight.

entries.luganda: Akukuba mu liiso : omukuba mu kutu; bw'agamba nti ondabye, naawe omu-ddamu nti ompulidde?
entries.english: The man who hits you in the eye : you hit on the ear; if he says: "Have you seen me?", you answer back: "Have you heard me?" Rub .C.331.
If your enemy accompanies your creditor (and you see them) : you will have a sleepless night.
He who pays you a short visit : does better than one who sends you greetings.
One who sees you at the cross-roads : considers you a traveller (stranger).
He who makes you herd his goats : you make him herd your cows (or: sheep).
entries.meaning: "Eriiso ligattwa liiso n'erinnyo ligattwa linnyo" (Matt.5.38). Ssal.p.52. 0295 Akuliira omuwemba : akunywesa gwa nkenku. One who eats your millet : makes you drink weak beer. One who deprives you of necessary things, does not allow you to do your work properly.

entries.english: The guardian of the chief : surpasses the guardian of his cows.
entries.meaning: The courtier gets a cow which the herdsman has to provide.

entries.english: One who gives you exhaustive information : tells you about somebody living far away (e.g.
entries.meaning: he lives there, bbati-house, he is blind in one eye, he has a growth on his forehead etc.).

entries.english: One who throws you in wrestling : has no pity on you.
entries.meaning: It is simply a matter of greater strength and skill.

entries.english: One who refuses you beans : saves you from bellyache (indigestion).
He shakes his head : like a goat complaining about the rain.
If a man cheats you in the day time : you cheat him at night.
entries.meaning: Paying back in his own coin.

entries.english: One who involves you in a law suit : does not pay your fine.
entries.meaning: You will have to pay yourself for your mistakes.

entries.english: He who urges you to plead in court : sends "Muwanga" (a traditional deity) with you.
entries.meaning: It was customary to wish well by saying "Muwanga awerekere". But he sends his wishes only; he himself does not come along. Words, not deeds. 41.49. 0308 Akusinga (amaanyi) : akukubya gw'okutte (= gw'oli nagwo). (omuggo) A man who is stronger than you : beats you with your own stick.

entries.english: A person who bombards you with questions : makes you speak about some-thing you wanted to hide.
The man who washes (his hands) first : also eats first.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Wer zuerst kommt, mahlt zuerst".

entries.english: He who promises you (a thing) : is better than one who refuses (it).
entries.meaning: A promise is better than a refusal.

entries.luganda: Akutwala enkild : takusiibuza wa muliraano (= takuganya kuslibula wa muliraano).
entries.english: One who frightens you : does not make you accompany him as far as the neighbour's place.

entries.luganda: Akutwala ettwe (= olutwe) : taba wa wala.
entries.english: He who betrays you : is not one from afar.
entries.meaning: "Abalabe b'omuntu banaabanga ba mu nnyumba ye" (Matt.10.36). Duta 1216, M.47, Dict.1064, Ssal.p.42, L.323. 0320 Akuvuma obuto : tassaako magufa. He who calls you "a little baby" : need not add worse insults (because it seems to include them).

entries.luganda: Akuwa akatono : 1) akira akumma; 2) akulobera okugeya; 3) akulobera okwe-gaana.
entries.english: One who gives you little : 1) is better than one who refuses to give; 2) prevents you from speaking evil about him (you cannot say: "tampadde"); 3) prevents you from saying: "I got nothing".
One who gives you something : you give him something.
entries.meaning: One good turn deserves another. Give and take. Lat. "Manus manum lavat".

entries.luganda: Akuwaaniriza (= akuwaliriza, = akusuutasuuta) okulinnya : bw'ogwa (= bw'o-menyeka), ye akuyita "Kadduwannema".
entries.english: He who praises you for climbing well : calls you a cripple when you fall.
entries.meaning: Don't trust the praise of men! See the fable "Wakibe ne Wambuzi" (Munno 1912 p.106).

entries.english: He who asks you to slaughter an animal : gives you also something to eat from it.
entries.meaning: A good piece of it is the butcher's fee. "Kuba omukozi asaanira empeera ye" (Luk.10.7).

entries.english: He who feeds you : makes you become his tenant.
entries.meaning: You like a chief under whom you get good food, who helps you.

entries.english: One who gives something to your child : shows more love to you than one who merely says: "I love you" (or: who gives you a bicycle).
One who supplies you valuable advice (when you go to court as a defendant) is more useful to you than one who gives you a (female) slave.
entries.meaning: Because that slave is not allowed to enter the court and cannot help you there.

entries.english: One who teaches you how to set a trap : won't you give him of the meat you catch?
One who calls you quietly : answer him quietly !
entries.meaning: Take a hint so that nobody is aware of it!

entries.english: He who loves you : warns you.
One who loves you : makes you build (your house) on rock (unfertile land).
entries.meaning: You want to be near him, in spite of the disadvantage.

entries.english: One who loves you and one who hates you : it's all the same.
entries.meaning: Either will talk constantly about you.

entries.luganda: Akwagala n'atakwagala : tebuziba nga tewannabula akwogerako.
entries.english: If there is one who loves you and one who hates you : it will not be evening, before either of them talks about you.
(= Ayeekwanira - -) One who is friendly (to you) : is better than one who (habitually) finds fault (with you).

entries.luganda: Akwata empola : atuuka wala; nnawolovu ow'e Bulemeezi omusanga mu Kyaddondo (= nnawolovu atuuka ku kibuga).
entries.english: One who takes things slowly, goes far; the chameleon from Bulemeezi you find in Kyaddondo (or: the chameleon arrives in town).
entries.meaning: Recommending dignity, gravity! Lat. "Festina lente!" Ital. "Chi va piano, va nano e va lontano". French "De la douceur pluttot que de la violence". "Softly, softly catches the monkey". "More haste, less speed".

entries.english: (effumu) He is holding his master's spear : and his own.
entries.meaning: Whilst the master is using his spear, the bearer is not left helpless.

entries.english: He who attacks his neighbour : will be killed himself.
entries.meaning: "Harm watch, harm catch". Germ. "Wer andern eine Grube grabt, fallt selbst hinein". Dutch "Wie een kuil graaft voor een ander, valt er self in". Compare the fable of the snake and the frog.

entries.english: One who speaks openly to you : is better than one who speaks behind your back.
He is relying on you : as a child relies on its mother.

entries.luganda: Akwonoonera : naawe omwonoonera; omuvubi ensonzi emusiiga ttosi, naye agisiiga vvu.
entries.english: One who does harm to you : you also do harm to him; the nsonzi (small mud-fish) besmears the fisherman with mud, and he, in turn, besmears the nsonzi with ashes (when roasting it).
entries.meaning: Vengeance! Germ. "Wie du mir, so ich dir!"

entries.english: One who visits (travels) : brings news (about others and others,have news about him).
One who hates advice : hates knowledge.
He still eats beans, one by one (as one takes up pins), i.e.
entries.meaning: peacefully, quietly, slowly. The same as "eradde".

entries.english: He still keeps silent (looks amazed, speechless) : like one who eats with a warrior.
entries.meaning: The interesting stories of the warrior make him forget the food.

entries.luganda: Akyogerako si ye akireeta : omukazi tayita njala kugwa (or: si ye akiyita : omukazi omunafu tayita njala kujja).
entries.english: One who speaks about it, does not bring it : a lazy woman does not tell of the famine to come.
entries.meaning: Women often talk about a possible famine. A warning is not causing the evil. Might be used, if somebody takes a warning as a curse.

entries.english: He who sees many things : distracts his mind.
entries.meaning: Splitting one's energy. Lat. "Age quod agis!" Munno 1926 p.75.

entries.english: One who sees a good thing : speaks about it.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Bonum est diffusivum sui".

entries.english: He who looks into the blue : is like a skin bag (made of goat-skin, stiff and always open).

entries.luganda: Alabye malinnya : amakka tagalaba (= amakka gabula).
entries.english: He has seen the way to climb up : but the way to come down he does not see.
entries.meaning: Used for: He can make statements, but cannot prove them.

entries.english: One who orders only one thing on the market : does not eat any relish.
entries.meaning: He should reckon with the possibility that this certain article (e.g. ssemutundu) is sold out, and that he should order an alternative kind of relish.

entries.english: If one (who is used to eating slowly) suddenly has to hurry up : he won't get enough.
entries.meaning: If one relinquishes his ordinary ways of eating, he goes hungry all day.

entries.luganda: Alembalemba : ng'omukulu anaasala ku njovu; nti "Awagwa ekinene watuuki-bwa"; nti "Kabaka bwe yafa tewagenda".
entries.english: He is strolling leisurely : like an old man who is going to cut some elephant meat, saying: "Where something big falls, there people gather"; (reply) "But when the king died, you did not go there!" Then there was no meat to be had!
The one who starts a fashion : abolishes it.
"Wherever will she go?" : (one saying so) is building a house for his mother.
entries.meaning: One is sure that his mother will not leave him.

entries.english: (amaato) One who has missed the boats : looks at the distant prows.
entries.meaning: That is all what he can still see. "Aliba-tasaabadde" is a proper name.

entries.english: He has eaten the egg : (that means) depriving oneself of the meat (of the chicken that could have been hatched).
entries.meaning: "You cannot eat your cake and have it".

entries.luganda: Alidde kya mukama we nga tasenguse : taba mubbi.
entries.english: He who eats something belonging to his master, provided he has not left his service, is not a thief.
entries.meaning: Hence the petty thefts of the servants.

entries.english: (ekkubo) The one who blocks the path and the one who forces it open again : are both equally angry.
entries.meaning: It takes two to make a quarrel.

entries.english: One who cultivates a big (ever increasing) stretch of (uncultivated) land : does not sow well.
entries.meaning: He won't be able to keep it in order.

entries.english: If the wife cultivates with the husband (i.e.
entries.meaning: if the husband helps her) : she won't be lazy.

entries.english: A child that cries for sheer impertinence : is like a jackal that howls after dark.
entries.meaning: People hearing the "kibe" crying at that time curse it.

entries.luganda: All mu bwato : annyulula banne be gasaanyawo.
entries.english: (amayengo, amazzi) He who is in the boat (canoe) : pulls out his friends whom the water is going to drown Those in safety must help those in danger.
He whose house has been burnt in the grass fire : is not called up for community labour, as long as he has not yet built a grass but for himself.

entries.luganda: Alina effubitizi eriyuliza omufu olubugo : nti emagombe agenda na mpiso?
entries.english: He is so spiteful that he would tear the barkcloth from a dead man : does the dead man go to the underworld with a needle?
entries.meaning: He won't be able to mend the damage done.

entries.english: One who has a dog : does not throw away bones.
entries.meaning: Take care of things which might be useful!

entries.luganda: Alina kasiikuuzi : akakubya emmomboze eyajja n'ebigere byayo.
entries.english: He has got an exasperating manner : such that he would even hit a stranger who came on foot (so that he can't even walk any longer).
entries.meaning: He should have accepted him as guest or sent him away, without doing harm to him. Ssal.p.39. 0378 Alina nnyina omuto : tabula kitaawe (= tabulwako kitaawe). One who has got a maternal aunt : has also a father. Her husband calls that child "mwana wange".

entries.luganda: Ali w'ali : w'alabira ebirungi n'ebibi (= w'alabira enjuba n'omwezi).
entries.english: He is here and there (and everywhere) : and sees good and bad things (sun and moon).
He talks (pleads) incessantly : like (the warrior) who has only one cow (on the raid).
entries.meaning: The chief who sent them on the raid, claims from each one his tribute. Those who managed to get more than one cow can easily give up the part claimed. But one who has only one wants to keep it.

entries.english: He has denounced the favourite in the dark (i.e.
entries.meaning: with no effect). The denunciation is not believed.

entries.english: One who reflects on what a hen eats (worms, caterpillars etc.) : loses the appetite to finish it (on his plate) with the ttooke.
One who is worried : opens the door (in the morning).
entries.meaning: He wants to dispel his worries. - Or: One who is interested (in an undertaking), begins.

entries.luganda: Alwa ku katale : y'alaba ssentala bw'agwa (= bw'agenda).
entries.english: One who has visited the market for many years : sees the tax-gatherer pass away (die).
entries.meaning: Said to one who is slow and lazy when some misfortune happens to him.

entries.english: (If somebody inquires about) a sick person whom you don't like : (you answer) "I don't know anything about it".
entries.meaning: If you were concerned about it, you would inquire yourself.

entries.english: He eats like one who makes his stomach drop.
He who eats : gets an appetite.
entries.meaning: Said of one who gets more stingy the richer he becomes. - Engl. "The appetite is concealed under the teeth". French "L'appetit vient en mangeant". Germ. "Mit dem Essen kommt der Appetit".

entries.english: Breasts are like a beard : even a barren woman has them.
entries.meaning: A beard can be worn by one who has got a family, and by one who has not.

entries.english: Butter does not fight with the sun.
entries.meaning: Said of people or nations refusing to fight. Yielding, complaisance. Germ. "Der Klugere gibt nach".

entries.english: Two places for visiting (obtaining presents) : killed the pigeon.
entries.meaning: First the pigeon alighted on the top-branches; then it spotted "misogasoga" (castor-oil-plant-fruits) on the lower branches, where it was caught in the trap. "Curiosity killed the cat".

entries.luganda: Amagere ga nkoko : tegatta baana baayo.
entries.english: The feet of the hen : do not kill the little chicks.
entries.meaning: Punishment does not kill the children. "Spare the rod and spoil the child". "Atakwata muggo gwe : akyawa omwana we" (Prov.13.24).

entries.english: Wisdom is given to you by your friend.
entries.meaning: "Two heads are better than one". "Ow'amagezi awulira okuweererwa ebigambo" (Prov.12.15). Dhop. "Ryeko iomo pa wat".

entries.luganda: Amagezi gakuweddeko : 1) okubongoota nga tonneeyalira; 2) okufuluma n'oggalawo; 3) ng'ayombera gy'asaka.
entries.english: You have no sense left : 1) if you go to sleep before spreading the mat; 2) if you (are in danger from wild animals or enemies and) go out of your house, locking it behind you (you deprive yourself of the possibility of safe retreat); 3) like the man who quarrels, where he works for food (they will not engage him again).
entries.meaning: Don't undertake a thing without making sure that you will be able to see it through.

entries.luganda: Amagezi gandi ku mwoyo : ng'omufuuwi w'eŋŋombe.
entries.english: The idea is in my mind : as the tune in the head of the hornblower.
entries.meaning: As long as it is not spoken, you cannot know it.

entries.luganda: Amagezi muliro : bwe gakubulako okima ewa munno (= bwe guzikira oguggya wa munno).
entries.english: Wisdom is like fire (in the hearth) : if you have none (if it has gone out), you fetch a "lyanda" from your neighbour.
entries.meaning: "Counsel is never out of date". "Two heads are better than one". Dhop. "Ryeko iomo pa wat".

entries.luganda: Amagezi nsejjere : buli efuluma emmula bwayo.
entries.english: Wisdom is like termite hills : each one puts out new earth in its own way.
entries.meaning: Men have their own ways, their own ideas and purposes.

entries.english: Wisdom is like a flying ant : it grows first and then flies away.
entries.meaning: It develops slowly and then flies away. Gaining experience.

entries.luganda: Amaggwa g'otega abayise : gafumita ggwe nnyinigo.
entries.english: The thorns you put down for passers-by : pierce yourself, the owner of them.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Wer andern eine Grube grabt, fallt selbst hinein".

entries.english: Insulting is not done by proxy.
entries.meaning: He who is insulted will say: "Let him come himself and insult me".

entries.luganda: Amaka abiri musango : olwanirira agali e Kyaggwe n'ag'e Ssingo baganyaga.
entries.english: (To own) two houses (homesteads) gets you into trouble (with the chiefs) : whilst you are working hard at your home in Kyaggwe, they rob you of your home in Ssingo.
entries.meaning: The chief of Ssingo will ask: "Wa kuno takola mulimo?"

entries.english: "My home is peaceful" : (one saying so) buys millet (for brewing beer).
entries.meaning: When the beer is drunk, peace will be soon upset.

entries.english: To be early does not mean the same for everybody.
entries.meaning: For the "nkwale" (partridges) it is 3 a.m., for the buffaloes 3.30-4 a.m. (kinywa-mbogo), for the cock 4-4.30 (maliiri), etc.

entries.english: The manner of beating varies.
entries.meaning: Beating, flogging, spanking, etc. Cf. Dict. of P. Le Veux p.433 (okukuba).

entries.english: One who aims carelessly when hunting : goes away empty-handed.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Quidquid agis, prudenter agas et respice finem".

entries.luganda: Amala geebikka : asula mpewo, tagenda kuwona ssennyiga.
entries.english: One who covers himself negligently : will feel cold during the night, and won't get rid of his cold (in the head).

entries.luganda: Amalala g'omukyaze : 1) nti banziriza olulimi, siigende; 2) nti nsanze olubende, nnaalyayo obugenyi.
entries.english: (It is) self-conceit (imagination) in a visitor (to say) : 1) they have warned me of a bad omen (and therefore) I shall not go.
entries.meaning: Ironical answer: If they present you (at table) with an intestine, will you stay there for ever and ever? Play of words: "okuddiza" is here taken in two senses; "okuddiza olulimi" (to predict evil on account of a bad omen) and "okuddiza ebiriibwa" (to give part of food). The "lulimi" (tongue) is short and the "kyenda" (intestine) is long; therefore the "ever and ever". (It is) self-conceit in a visitor (to say) : 2) I have met a striped cat (on the way), that means I shall get presents. Ironical answer: "When the king became ruler of Busoga, had he perhaps met a zebra on the road?" Both animals are striped, the lubende is small, the zebra is big; therefore small good luck and big good luck! Both proverbs are ridiculing superstition.

entries.english: One who possesses things : (says proudly) "My courtyard is well-trodden by goats".
When one has fallen : he understands how he should have acted (not to fall).
After the meal (he says) "they are calling for me to go home".
Having food without relish does not make one wish for famine.
entries.meaning: It is better to have essentials only than nothing at all. "Half a loaf is better than no bread".

entries.luganda: Amambulugga gajja kiro : ag'emisana galuma (= ge gatta).
entries.english: Mumps come on at night : those of the day-time are painful (are killing).
entries.meaning: Used as form of refusal: "I don't want to have anything to do with it".

entries.luganda: Amamese amangi tigeesimira bunnya : nga tiwali njangwa.
entries.english: (Too) many mice don't dig holes for themselves : unless there is a cat about.
entries.meaning: Too many people together do not accomplish useful work; unless there is one who drives them on.

entries.luganda: Amampaati aga nnyini nkoko : nti "enkoko zange zibuukira omuyagi"; nti "ente esinga obunene ebuuka emituba".
entries.english: Vanity makes the owner of hens say : "my chickens fly over a muyagi shrub"; (ironical reply) "and the cow that is bigger (than a hen) will fly over a bark-cloth-tree".

entries.luganda: Amampaati ageegoloza omukadde : ng'agenda kukula (or: sso nga takyawanvu-wa).
entries.english: It is pride that makes the old man stretch himself : as if he was going to grow (or: although he cannot get any taller).

entries.luganda: Amaanyi ameemanye : ge gamala ebita e mbuga.
entries.english: Imaginary strength : breaks the beerpots in the chief's place.
entries.meaning: One who imagines himself to be strong and tries to lift the calabashes full with beer, will break them. "Pride will have a fall".

entries.luganda: Amaanyi ga nnabugi : gamukubya akyali muto.
entries.english: The hardness of old mutuba-bark (special kind of ficus) is the reason, why it is beaten, when still young.
entries.meaning: When young, it is still soft and pliable. Children must be trained at an early age.

entries.english: Mere force does not peel the stick (because of the thorns on it).
entries.meaning: Be careful in all your undertakings!

entries.luganda: Amaanyi tegalya bwami : singa eŋŋaaŋa ye kabaka w'ennyonyi.
entries.english: Mere strength does not acquire a chieftainship : otherwise the hornbill would be the king of the birds.

entries.luganda: Amaanyi tigalya : eŋŋaaŋa terya nkoko (= singa eŋŋaaŋa emazeewo enkoko).
entries.english: Mere force brings no success : the hornbill does not eat the chicken.
entries.meaning: "Discretion is the better part of valour". M.70, 1.15. 0444 Amasaŋŋanzira : gatta agazimbako n'omubuuzibwa. (cf. Masaŋŋanzira: 2701) Cross-roads : kill the one who builds on them and the one whom people are looking for. One who builds on cross-roads is in for trouble. Drawbacks of publicity.

entries.english: "Fat is no (valuable) gift" : (thus you console yourself) when a strong fellow has taken it (from you).
Superficially scratching off the weeds : is not cultivating.
entries.meaning: Do things thoroughly! Starting only is not enough. Lat. "Age quod agis".

entries.english: On cooking-stones there falls no dew.
entries.meaning: They are always ready for the visitors (or the hungry).

entries.english: The taking hold of shield (and spear) : can be done by anybody.
entries.meaning: Said of one who brags with his fighting spirit and is coward, when the fighting starts. "Dutch courage".

entries.english: Fearful (timorous) eyes : greet the owner of the house.
entries.meaning: It is customary that the visitor is greeted first by those in the house.

entries.luganda: Amaaso batadde ku gwaka : ne beerabira ogunyooka.
entries.english: They have their eyes on a fire that burns : and forget the one that only smoulders.
entries.meaning: Men are attracted by riches, fame, glory, and have no time for humble things.

entries.english: Eyes that have come to see one person : see many.
entries.meaning: The visitor will see many others. Simple actions often bring complications.

entries.luganda: Amaaso gakuli nga ekiwuugulu ekisibe endege.
entries.english: You have a face like an owl with bells on its legs.

entries.luganda: Amaaso gamwesimbye : ng'ag'enkoko enywa mu lwendo.
entries.english: He stares with his eyes : like a chicken drinking from a ladle (looking skywards for swallowing).
It is the eyes that are afraid.
entries.meaning: The first impression on judging the distance for a journey or the amount of work to be done exaggerates the difficulties and underestimates the energy. Imaginary difficulties.

entries.english: Hungry eyes are directed towards the bananary.
entries.meaning: Reproach for people who, as visitors, look round greedily and inquisitively.

entries.english: Big words : contain no presents.
entries.meaning: Dutch "Ledige vaten klinken het hardst".

entries.english: The manner of walking : is not the same with everybody.
entries.meaning: Walking, running, slinking, crawling, marching etc.

entries.english: Stubborn ears : bring blows on their owner.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Wer nicht horen will, muss filhlen".

entries.english: Have they put ears on (only) to adorn the head?
entries.meaning: Ears are given to hear. "Mina amatu agawulira, awulire" (Luke 8.8).

entries.english: Cold food (left over from the night before) : is eaten by one who asks for it.
entries.meaning: Adults, as a rule, are shy to show themselves so hungry.

entries.english: The grunting of the hyena : is the sign that it moves about.
entries.meaning: P. 0470a Amayumba bisaka : tomanya bibaamu. (cf. Ennyumba kisaka: 1714) Houses are like thickets : you don't know what is inside.

entries.luganda: Amayumba bunyonyi : buli akafuluma kazimba bwako.
entries.english: Houses are like birds : each one builds it in its own way.
entries.meaning: In the different homesteads you find different laws, customs etc.

entries.luganda: Amazeeko nga muwogo : waggulu nva, wakati nku, wansi mmere.
entries.english: He is self-sufficient like the cassava-plant : on top greens, in the middle fire-wood, below food.

entries.luganda: Amazzi amatono : gabooza ente; nti baleete ez'abaana zimale okunywa (= nti leka enzadde zinywe).
entries.english: A little water (scarcity of water) : prevents (the whole herd of) cows (from drinking); (the herdsmen give the order) to bring the mother-cows first to drink.
entries.meaning: Precedence of elders etc. A man with few possessions chooses carefully his heir. Only favourites are given rare things.

entries.luganda: Amazzi bwe gakalira : gadda ku mwala.
entries.english: When the water (in a stream) dries up : it concentrates in the middle (from where it spreads).
entries.meaning: In distress one returns to the original (reliable) sources. Rub.C.232. 0478 Amazzi tigeerabira gye gava : waabo mpewo. (cf. Omwana tiyeerabira waabo: 4445) Water does not forget its origin : its home is the cold. The natural and usual state of the water is cold. Even when it is heated up to boiling point, it will cool down to its original temperature. - Application: One does not forget his own clan and is naturally attracted by his clansmen.

entries.english: He scorned him with a burst of laughter : as the termite scorns the lubaale-grass-temple.
entries.meaning: The termites are not harmed by the lubaale-shrine, although they eat it up. Their "enduulu", when men approach, sounds like laughter, scorning the awe, people have for the shrine.

entries.english: A woman who has no child : will carry a stone on her back.
entries.meaning: She wants to appear like others. Used to criticise imitation of modes and fashions. One does not want to be "singular".

entries.luganda: Anaggula omunaku amatu : "wano waliwo kitaawo ne nnyoko".
entries.english: He who wants to open the ears of a poor man : need only say to him: "Here is your father and your mother".

entries.luganda: Anaakuboolera mu lumbe : nti ggwe wa maanyi.
entries.english: If a man, in case of bereavement, considers you as being outside the clan (being no relation of the dead person) : (he will say to you) you have the strength (to go to Bulemeezi to take the death notice there).
entries.meaning: The relatives of the deceased are supposed to have no strength left in their sadness.

entries.luganda: Anaakuggya ennimi : ageya nnyoko ng'olaba (= nga w'oli).
entries.english: He who speaks ill about your mother in your presence : makes you tell her (what the slanderer has said).
entries.meaning: A man who speaks ill about your relations (friends etc.), causes you to speak evil about him to them.

entries.luganda: Anaakugoba ku nswa : nti tolya omulalu.
entries.english: He who intends to drive you away from the flying ants : (says) don't eat the mulalu (the first flying ant emerging from the kiswa)!
entries.meaning: Used for warning off a person from a thing in order to get it yourself after-wards.

entries.english: One who wishes to take your child away from you : speaks of real relationship.
He who will betray you : embraces you.

entries.luganda: Anaakuliisa akasolo akabi : akalya akabeera (= akawaana).
entries.english: He will make you eat a bad (uneatable) animal : if he eats and praises it.
entries.meaning: Enticing, seducing, making sin attractive. Rub.C.1838. 0495 Anaakumaza emmere : akuwa nguuli omutali sooda. One who wants to stop you eating (= wants to kill you) : gives you "waragi" (distilled beer or spirits) without soda, i.e. "neat". A bottle of such stuff can kill a man.

entries.english: He who wants to urge you on to filter half-fermented beer : (says) it should not be left longer to ferment.
entries.meaning: Used for urging on somebody to rash, precipitate action, when it would be better to wait.

entries.luganda: Anaakussa ekkande : "kasooli wa kuno tayera, awunda".
entries.english: One who wants to place you on barren land : (praises it, saying) "Maize not only grows in abundance here, but it is a pleasure to look at it".

entries.luganda: Anaakusiba olumbe olumbe : nti yaluggya wala; nti we lulema tossa wansi?
entries.english: A man who wants to say of you that you have an incurable disease : says "He got it from afar (i.e.
entries.meaning: that is a long and chronic evil)"; (ironical answer) "If it is so heavy for you (having carried it from so far a place) won't you put it down (and rest a while)?"

entries.english: A concubine who wants to spoil the peace of your home : (says) "work that is too much for me, sleeps outside" (i.e.
entries.meaning: I can do anything, nothing is too much for me). She is jealous of her concubine (fellow-wife) and wants to get her away.

entries.english: He who wants to abuse you with offending words : abuses you in your sick-ness.
entries.meaning: Instead of condoling with you, he accuses you of pretending to be sick.

entries.luganda: Anaakuvumira mu magezi : avuma mwana (= akuvumira mu mwana).
entries.english: One who wants to abuse you in a clever way : abuses your child (= abuses you through your child).
You can tell a man who is going to help to bury (your relation) by his girdle.
entries.meaning: He tugs up his garment and gets ready to dig the grave.

entries.luganda: Anaanyumya takeereza : nnamunyi oluva ku nju ng'ekireka akuba.
entries.english: He who intends to tell a story, does not wait long (with) : the wagtail flying away from the house beats its wings, dancing immediately.
entries.meaning: The wings of the wagtail are compared here with the fringes of banana-leaves (kireka), tied round the hips in dancing (mpina).

entries.luganda: Anaaseera owuwe : 1) nti "leka ab'ebweru balye"; 2) asala akiika (= He who intends to cheat his own child : 1) says "stop, let the guests eat"; 2) cuts slantingly.
entries.english: The slices of meat etc.
entries.meaning: are thinner at the bottom.

entries.english: He who has almost had enough : stirs up the relish (sauce) without consideration for others.
entries.meaning: Applied to a woman who intends to leave her husband. She neglects her work, is annoying and spiteful.

entries.english: One who is in the habit of quarrelling : is soon ready with an angry word.

entries.luganda: Anaatuubya engo : embuzi asiba ku luzibaziba.
entries.english: He who wants to entice the leopard : ties a goat to a luzibaziba-shrub.
entries.meaning: Inviting disaster. Okutuubya = okuluvuwaza (give appetite). Luzibaziba is a liana-like shrub ("alchornea cordifolia").

entries.english: (One who asks) "Who will give (the child) food for me?" : gives it to a child that has no teeth yet.
entries.meaning: It cannot masticate yet and therefore the parent gives small amounts.

entries.english: He is keeping away from me : as the ssemukuto (cricket-like insect that exudes an irritating fluid in defence, causing blisters) keeps away eaters of crickets.
He clings to me : like "bigalanga" (flatulent dyspepsia) to a sick person.
entries.meaning: I can't get rid of him.

entries.english: He keeps aloof from me : as the little toe of the dog does (from the other toes).
He who searches : finds.

entries.luganda: Anziriddemu : nga Muteesa Walugembe bwe yaddira mu b'obugulu obutono; nti mmwenna mwambale empale empanvu.
entries.english: He has pity on me : as (king) Muteesa Walugembe had pity on people with thin legs; (because he said to them) all of you dress in long trousers!
He who asks a weak man (for something) : asks whilst taking it.
entries.meaning: The weak man has no chance to resist. "Might is right".

entries.english: He is mad with joy : like a man who managed to rear a big mushroom in famine time.
He wavers from side to side (is undecided) : like the hip-bone of an emaciated person.
One who is crazy for meat : hunts buffalo.
entries.meaning: He will even risk his life to gratify his lust. The buffalo is the most difficult animal to hunt (cunning, vindictive, cruel).

entries.english: He who commiserates with a poor person (in words only).: makes him cry.
entries.meaning: He reminds him only of his misery, but does not help him.

entries.luganda: Aseka ekimwegeru : engalabi ky'eseka n'emiti mu kamwa.
entries.english: He laughs secretly : as the engalabi-drum laughs with the little pegs round its face (drumming-surface).
entries.meaning: The pegs are compared to the teeth of the mouth. Germ. "Auf den Stock-zahnen lachen".

entries.luganda: Asemberera kabaka ye muwangaazi : ennongo emera mu kiswa enkuyege tegirya.
entries.english: The one who comes near the king is long-lived : the nnongo-tree (Albizzia grandibracteata) that grows on the ant-hill is not eaten by the ants.
entries.meaning: The king does not kill his katikkiro.

entries.luganda: Asenga atuusa : y'anenya banne (= abatannaba kutuusa busenze).
entries.english: One who has acquired a plot (kibanja) : criticises those who have not yet succeeded.

entries.luganda: Asenga ku kiggwa : y'akumira lubaale omuliro.
entries.english: He who gives his service to the shrine (of the gods) : kindles the fire for the lubaale.
entries.meaning: The lubaale-priest works for the lubaale.

entries.english: A new tenant is not lazy.
entries.meaning: Otherwise he will not be a tenant very long.

entries.english: He who leaves his plot (kibanja) : increases the number of places where you can stay.
entries.meaning: Chances of finding lodging, hospitality etc.

entries.luganda: Asiba mu mbuzi omugwa : gwe babanja.
entries.english: He who puts the rope round the goat's neck : is the one whom they make responsible.
entries.meaning: He had it last in his possession.

entries.english: He takes his leave like a hungry fellow : (who says) "good-bye" without end.
entries.meaning: He hopes still to be invited for food.

entries.english: He is left in the same state as "the river at Busami" : (whose name is) "Nnee-magaza" (i.e.
entries.meaning: "I am quite at a loss"). Busami is the name of a place. Play on words!

entries.english: One who prematurely examines a mushroom : breaks off the stalk.
entries.meaning: Those who prematurely pry into other people's plans (or interfere with them), spoil them.

entries.english: (or: Asimba ensogasoga - - ) One who cultivates castor-oil plants : does not drive the pigeons from his courtyard.
entries.meaning: A father who has marriageable daughters, does not prevent suitors from visiting him.

entries.english: The man who digs up potatoes for the dog (feeds him) : is the one the dog will listen to.
entries.meaning: Therefore the owner is responsible for the damage caused by the dog. Parents are responsible for their children.

entries.english: Even one who keeps very quiet : surely does something (is not idle).
One who gets up immediately (on hearing the click of the trap) : sets the trap with banana-fibre only.
entries.meaning: The animal might be able to tear loose. Safeguarding a thing which might be lost, unless one is quick.

entries.english: The one who has already hidden himself (in the bush) : reproaches the others (coming after him) that they make so much noise.
The man who has failed to obtain a chieftainship : does not kill himself.
entries.meaning: One can live without being a chief.

entries.english: "He is at it again (he starts putting makobe fruits aside for himself)" : (so they say watching) the fellow working for food and appropriating food that is not a part of his wages.
He who mixes with trouble : will be killed by it.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Quae nocitura tenes, quamvis sint cara, relinque!" (Ovid). "Qui amat periculum, peribit in illo" (Augustine). Engl. "Opportunity makes a thief". "Playing with fire".

entries.luganda: Asula obubi (= awabi) : omulabira ku nkeera.
entries.english: The man who sleeps badly : you see him early in the morning.
entries.meaning: He is in a hurry to get to a better place.

entries.english: The one who is not likely to rule them (the children) : (says) "Let them fight with each other".
The man who has not carried loads himself : does not know how heavy they are.
A man who has not lost his own (relation) by death : says "lumumenye" ("death has broken him").
entries.meaning: Condolence without much sympathy.

entries.english: One who has never yet lost a bride by death : is inclined to say "She is drowsy" (although she might be seriously ill).
entries.meaning: Experience makes you know the signs of danger.

entries.english: He who is not in love himself : (says) "They are infatuated with love".
A father will not bring his own child up well : (if) he brings up (only) his slave.
entries.meaning: If the slave is told to do all the work, the child will be spoilt and lazy.

entries.english: The one who has not brewed the beer : complains to his friend about it, (saying) "He refused me a drink and did it rudely" (although the real reason was his coming, when the beer was finished).
One who does not remember things of old : is not generous.
entries.meaning: He does not think of past merits of people or their parents, is narrow-minded and inconsiderate.

entries.english: One who is late, is later than the earlier man (who has gone away already) : (that means) going back (without having achieved the purpose of coming).
He who does not (frequently) inspect the place where mushrooms grow : calls it a barren place.
entries.meaning: Other people will come and take the mushroom, before he has a chance.

entries.english: The one who does not eat it : does not know its sweetness.
entries.meaning: Pleasure is understood only by those who have experienced it.

entries.english: The man who has not sent the thing (for sale) himself : calls it valueless.
entries.meaning: Despising other people's efforts.

entries.english: He who does not ask you about the news : makes you keep silent about them.
entries.meaning: You conclude that he is not interested in your experiences on a journey.
