entries.english: From the family of your uncle (brother of your mother) : comes no generation of yours (because you can't marry any near blood-relations).
A goat (or: cow, sheep etc.) that is straying : does not belong to the pen.
entries.meaning: The prospective buyer does not trust it. - Also applied to roaming girls and women!

entries.english: The disputes of the shepherds are settled on the pastures.
entries.meaning: Don't wash dirty linen in public! Family disputes are not for the public.

entries.luganda: Ebya Buganda : bya kulya na kugula.
entries.english: The greatest worries in Buganda are eating and buying.
entries.meaning: Formerly there was no buying and selling for money, but only bartering.

entries.luganda: Ebya gundi bya Mwana wa Mukama.
entries.english: What So and so says, are the words of the Son of the Lord.
entries.meaning: Used for statements which cannot be relied upon (unclear, indefinite or sarcas- tic).

entries.luganda: Ebyali ebyannyu babikuseera : enkejje amazzi bagigaseerera mu luwombo, nti "ofukamu matono".
entries.english: What might have been your own property, they make expensive for you : the enkejje in the luwombo (in which it is cooked) does not get enough water because the mother says to the girl: "Pour in a little!" Rub .C.588, M.200, 88.69.
Those secrets which are revealed under the seal of secrecy : cause wrongs.

entries.luganda: "Ebyanfudde bingi" : 1) agula mutwe gwa nte; nti singa oguze enjere eya ssava, ne tumanya bwe bikufa; 2) enswa eruma mumwa.
entries.english: "I am losing a lot (of money)" (says the miser) : 1) buying the head of a cow; (answer) if you had bought fat meat without bones, we could understand that you have lost money.
entries.meaning: For that "lot of money" he gets only inferior quality. "I am losing a lot" : 2) (says) the flying ant biting the lips of the eater. Hopeless, but courageous defence.

entries.luganda: Ebyange tebinfa bwe bityo : gwe mpola embuzi, ampa nte.
entries.english: This way my property does not perish : because the one to whom I lend a goat, must give me back a cow.
The word "I beseech you" : breaks the (punishing) arm.
Useless things : such as those which the mouse eats in a deserted house.
Difficult cases with the chief are settled by a father who has a marriageable daughter.
entries.meaning: If the chief has an eye on that daughter, the father is safe.

entries.luganda: Eby'embuulano tibyala (= tibyeyamba) : 1) bw'ofuna nnyoko, kitaawo abula; 2) gy'osiba (= gy'oterekera) embuzi, enkiringi tizidda; 3) omuwuulu bw'afuna enkoko, omunnyu gumubula.
entries.english: The things of an unmarried person (spinster) do not increase : (because) 1) if you have a mother, there is no father (if an unmarried woman has children, they have no legitimate father); 2) if you leave your goat to be looked after, the produce (offspring) won't come back to you (you get only the goat back); 3) if a bachelor gets a chicken, he won't have any salt (for cooking).
Riches are like a hide : everybody pulls (them) his way.
entries.meaning: Comparing the strife for wealth with stretching out a skin on the ground. Lat. "Sacra auri fames".

entries.english: Riches are like perspiration : if you rest, they dry up.

entries.luganda: Eby'Obuganda : byetegerezebwa nga kye bakutuma okireese.
entries.english: The affairs of Buganda : are discussed, when you have brought, what you have been sent for.
entries.meaning: If you did not bring it, you hear only reproaches.

entries.english: Those are private affairs between husband and wife.
entries.meaning: One should not interfere in other people's business. Buvuma proverb.

entries.english: "That is what makes me afraid" : (says the poisoner) when he hears the diviner (employed to find lost things).
entries.meaning: The poisoner is afraid that such a diviner will find his poisons and brings him to ruin.

entries.english: The prospect of getting something : opens the eyes of the one-eyed.
"I have not come for the purpose of eating" : a visitor (who talks like that) offends his host.
entries.meaning: He gives the impression that he is disappointed and that he does not appreciate hospitality.

entries.luganda: Eby'okuwa bifa obusa : Abanaawa basuuza bbaabwe.
entries.english: Beneficence is misspent : the people of Kinaawa (in Busiro) refused their king.
entries.meaning: King Ssuuna II. who had been extremely helpful to the inhabitants of Kinaawa, was refused passage through their country, when they brought his body from Buddu, where he had died.

entries.luganda: Eby'olutabaalo tibidda ka : nga tibannakosa mu bbwa.
entries.english: The wounds received in the war do not break out at home : unless they touch the sores (scars).
entries.meaning: Old grievances flare up, if mentioned again.

entries.luganda: Eby'omugagga bijja (= biyingira) kiro : bw'alaba ekikere (or: ekisolo) ng'agoba.
entries.english: The treasures of a rich man come in at night : (still) when he sees a frog (or a wild animal) coming in, he drives it away.

entries.luganda: Eby'omugagga bijja byokka : omusota tagukkiriza kujja gy'ali.
entries.english: The treasures of a rich man come in by themselves : (so they say) but he does not let a snake come near him.

entries.luganda: "Eby'omugagga bivunda" : bw'alwala ebbwa, ng'anyiga (or: sso ng'ebbwa bwe limukwata ng'anyiga).
entries.english: "The things of a rich man rot (remain where they are)" (so says the rich man who has been asked in vain for help) : but when he suffers from a sore, he presses out the pus (he does not want to keep that).
entries.meaning: Why does he not let his body also rot?

entries.luganda: Eddagala ekka : lye lituuka ku ndwadde.
entries.english: Strong medicine reaches the sickness.
The madness (disobedience, obstreperousness) of a woman makes her despise her husband.
entries.meaning: He will take revenge (bw'anaakulaba, engalo taaziteme?!). "Okukongoola" = to make a scratching gesture towards somebody as a sign of despising him.

entries.english: The skin (hide) is dry : (therefore) the ants can march off.
entries.meaning: Nothing more to get. - When the food is finished the guests depart.

entries.english: The eating place brings people together.
A good (successful) marriage : marries off even the youngest sister.
entries.meaning: Waalaga = muggalanda = the last born. She goes and becomes co-wife of her elder sister, because she sees that she is happy with her husband. Waalaga, according to others, stands for a girl that gets married to the same husband as her aunt on father's side. Taboo! Rub.C.1250. 1244a Eddya eddungi : likuliisa tiweesibye. A good (peaceful) marriage lets you bring having to dress up for it. An exacting husband would quarrel.

entries.luganda: "Eggayana (= eggayano) liggwe ku kyalo" eggayannano: 2584) Rub.C.1726.
entries.english: the food (to your husband) without : ng'owuwe y'ali kungulu.
"To whom shall I give the bone?" : (so he asks, but) he has already seen the man to whom he is going to give it.
Vindictiveness against a neighbour : will soon be returned.
The treasures of the rich man and the treasures of the poor man are the same.
entries.meaning: Both leave their children in distress.

entries.english: A hidden army fights under cover.
entries.meaning: Potatoes grow under the ground unobserved.

entries.luganda: Eggye lya Kabaka : teriggwa nnyuma (= mabega).
entries.english: The army of the king does not come to an end at the rear.
entries.meaning: When the "mujaguzo" (war drum) is beaten, not all warriors turn up at once. There are late-comers constantly. Constant flow of new warriors or workers.

entries.english: "That place (what do you call it) is far" : (says one) if there is nobody he knows (i.e.
entries.meaning: who can give him food or lodging).

entries.luganda: Eka egwana mukazi ne bba : atalina mukazi azimba ekibanja?
entries.english: In a home there should be wife and husband : does a man with no wife put up a plantation?
I am beaten both ways : at home and in the forest.
entries.meaning: According to a legend, this is what the man said who lost two women on the same day, the wife he possessed and the one he wanted to get. He was dissatis-fied with his wife; but one day he found in the forest a beautiful woman sitting on a tree-trunk to whom he said: "Nkwagala". She answered: "Nange nkwagala. But before you can take me, you must bring me one breast, because I have only one". The man agreed, went home, cut off one of his wife's breasts and returned to the forest. But the beautiful woman had disappeared. Sadly the man went home and there he found his own wife dead. - Lat. "Incidis in Scyllam, cupiens vitare Charybdim". Engl. "Out of the frying pan into the fire". Germ. "Zwischen zwei Stahle fallen".

entries.english: (ekibi) A bad point in a good man's character : is experienced later.
entries.meaning: First everything seems to be perfect. - Also used for physical beauty. "A fly in the ointment".

entries.english: What makes the locusts fly, is the warmth of the sun.
entries.meaning: In the cold of the morning they are stiff and cannot move.

entries.english: The banana-rack has fallen and the bananas with it.
To throw one who is unprepared (by trickery) : is not wrestling.
entries.meaning: It is unsportsman-like. Unfair means!

entries.english: Bad news (or warning) does not wait for one to come back from the well.
entries.meaning: It is given at once to those who are present.

entries.luganda: Ekibojjera ku lwazi : kyesiga mumwa mugumu.
entries.english: A bird pecking a rock : relies on the hardness of its beak.
entries.meaning: A man buying expensive things must have a well-filled purse.

entries.english: A town makes a cow kneel.
entries.meaning: The mighty impressions of town-life and activity fill country-people with awe.

entries.english: What is not ripe yet : is not taken.
entries.meaning: It escapes the fate of mature things.

entries.english: What a poor man has not got : kills him.
entries.meaning: He often uses the word: Ssebo sirina kino, "nfudde".

entries.english: What makes one change the banana-peeling place : is too much rain.
entries.meaning: The refuse starts rotting there. - Every happening has its reasons.

entries.english: For things concerning the lake : you must ask the fisherman.
entries.meaning: Drum-beat of the mutima-clan. - Lat. "Non omnia possumus omnes" (Horace). "Ne sutor super crepidam (judicet)" (Pliny). French "De medecine parlez au medecin". Engl. "Let not the cobbler go beyond his last". Germ. "Schuster, bleib bei deinem Leisten".

entries.english: Resemblance : kills the louse.
entries.meaning: As soon as you see a louse, you kill it, although it might not be the one which has bitten you. One must be the scapegoat.

entries.english: Resemblance : is not kinship.
entries.meaning: Not all who look alike are relations. Used for: Look sharper! You may be mistaken.

entries.luganda: Ekigaluza ow'eŋŋombe : ng'owa ky'obinda akuli bubi.
entries.english: What makes a man brandish his horn : is the fact that one who has got a spear is oppressing you.
entries.meaning: You have nothing else to defend yourself but your horn.

entries.luganda: Ekigambo ekirungi : kisuza mpisi ku lugo.
entries.english: A good word : makes the hyena spend the night near the cattle pen.
entries.meaning: The young animal in the cattle pen, crying without end is threatened by its mother, saying: "If you don't keep quiet, I will throw you out of the kraal". The hyena hears that and waits for a good feed.

entries.english: What is spoken in day time (openly) : does not come to an end everywhere in the same way.
entries.meaning: Everybody who has heard it, will pass it on in his own way.

entries.luganda: "Ekigambo si mutwalo" : nga gye bakutumye oyagalayo.
entries.english: "A message is no load" : (so you say) if you like the place you are being sent to.

entries.luganda: Ekigambo tekitomera mpagi : singa eby'omu luuma bitomera emiti.
entries.english: A word (conversation) does not rebound on the poles (of the house) (i.e.
entries.meaning: one can carry on a conversation from inside with a person outside) : otherwise a telephone message would get stuck on the telephone poles.

entries.luganda: Ekigaanira omuddu : liba bbwa lya mu mutwe.
entries.english: What exonerates the slave (from carrying the load) : is the sore on his head.
entries.meaning: A lawful excuse frees from an obligation.

entries.luganda: Ekigere kikyali ku ttaka : tikyewala nfuufu.
entries.english: As long as the foot is still on the ground (on earth) : it cannot keep away from dust (earthly things).
The foot of the peasant (poor man) is a present of beer.
entries.meaning: The beer is brought to the chief by his peasants (subjects); the poor man has to go himself to get beer.

entries.english: In a bad (dirty) river (without flowing water) : one does not catch nsonzi (small fish).
entries.meaning: Choose the right place for your purposes!

entries.english: What brings out ill-feeling : is (often) a small thing.
The pillow of the king : is his bent arm.
entries.meaning: Although he might have a precious pillow, he uses also his arm to sleep upon like other mortals.

entries.english: What falls (into the dust, on the ground) : you don't pick up.
entries.meaning: Said about food falling on the ground.

entries.english: One fall does not prevent children from singing.
entries.meaning: One failure does not mean final defeat. Do not lose courage too soon!

entries.luganda: Ekijja omanyi : kikunyaga bitono; ekiddukano tekinyaga byenda.
entries.english: What befalls you when you knew (it was coming) : robs you of little; diarrhoea does not rob (you of) your bowels.
entries.meaning: "Forewarned is forearmed". "Kijjomanyi" is the name of a village in Busiro.

entries.english: "The clan is becoming extinct" : (one who says so) has to take the barkcloth (for the burial of his relatives) himself under his arm.
entries.meaning: If he had had children, they would have carried it for him.

entries.english: What makes the thief (or: bushbuck) in the hiding place cough : is being forced.
entries.meaning: He cannot hold back the cough any longer.

entries.english: What makes a farmer thin : makes him fat again.
entries.meaning: Working for the food makes him thin; but eating it makes him fat again. The farmer lives from the soil he tills.

entries.luganda: Ekikulejje : ekikubira engalo emabega ne kimala kuyimba bulungi.
entries.english: A marvellous thing : it clasps hands on the back and bursts out singing lustily (i.e.
entries.meaning: the cock: first it clasps the wings and then starts crowing).

entries.english: That which makes you deal with the spirits : throws you into the fire.
entries.meaning: The basamize jump over fire.

entries.luganda: Ekikwanguyira naawe okyanguyira : 1) ekikajjo olya kibisi; bw'olya ekyokye, ng'oli mulwadde ; 2) empogola we yeeyasiza w'ogisusira; 3) eryenvu olya bbisi.
entries.english: What comes to you easily, you should take easily (without unnecessary trou-ble) : 1) the sugar-cane you eat raw; if you eat it cooked, it is a sign that you are sick; 2) where the banana (boiled in the skin) bursts, there you start peeling it (instead of trying where it is still tight); 3) you eat the ripe lyenvu (eating banana) raw (without taking the trouble to cook it).

entries.luganda: Ekikyo kikyo : n'ekya munno kya munno.
entries.english: What is yours is yours : and what is your friend's is his.
entries.meaning: Respect for other people's property.

entries.english: Silence finishes the argument.
entries.meaning: If one party does not answer any longer, the discussion is at an end. - "Kimala-mpaka" is the name of a large-flowered shrub with highly poisonous seeds, which were used in sorcery (also called "bigingiri-bitya").

entries.luganda: Ekimala omugole ensonyi : byeyazike nga babizzaayo.
entries.english: What puts the bride to shame : is when they carry back the borrowed things.
entries.meaning: At first she thought they were the husband's. If she is wise, she grabs a water-pot and goes to the well meanwhile. Duta 342. 1314a Ekimanye muntu omu : kikussa makunga. What is known by one person only : makes you utter exclamations of astonish-ment.

entries.luganda: Ekimanyire bwe kiba : emmese tetomera buziizi.
entries.english: So it is with a thing you are acquainted with : the rat does not knock its head against the darkest corner in the house.

entries.luganda: Ekinaakulya kijja olaba : ekiwalaata mu masega.
entries.english: What is going to eat you, comes whilst you see it : like baldness cutting in on either side of your forehead.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Weisheitswinkel". You see it coming, but you cannot prevent it.

entries.english: What wants to eat you : you drive away and it comes again (like a furious dog or a sickness) (the more you defend yourself, the more aggressive it becomes).

entries.luganda: Ekinaakutta tekiva wala : nnaganga w'endiga ava buziizi.
entries.english: What is going to kill you, does not come from far : the sickness of the sheep comes from the darkest (and dirtiest) corner of the house.
entries.meaning: Goats and sheep used to be kept in the dwelling house.

entries.luganda: Ekinatta amaka (= nnyini maka) : tekyeramba luggya.
entries.english: What will ruin the home (or: the owner of a home) does not come straight over the court-yard (but sneaks in from the back, e.g.
Why do you let a glowing piece of iron (kyuma) burn you?
entries.meaning: If you know that it will cool down? - Said of passionate love that ends in sepa- ration. Kwata mpola!

entries.luganda: Ekinene kigenda na kusingirwa : enseenene zigenda na vvu.
entries.english: Something big goes (is achieved) with a pledge (a gift, a bribe) : the enseenene (edible grass-hoppers) go with ashes.
entries.meaning: To make the nseenene eatable, their wings and legs must be removed. For that purpose the fingers are dipped in ashes, because the roasted grass hoppers are greasy and slippery.

entries.luganda: Ekinene kye kimira ekitono : emmamba emira enkejje.
entries.english: A big thing swallows a small thing : the lungfish swallows the sprat.
entries.meaning: "The right of the stronger". The survival of the fittest.

entries.luganda: Ekinene tikyetwala : kabaka ayingira ewa Kibaale.
entries.english: Even a big thing does not rule itself : the king is in the power of the Kibaale.
entries.meaning: "Kibaale" is the title of the man to whom the bakungu (Katikkiro, Omulamuzi etc.) can bring their complaints against the king and who sits in judgement over the king. Dutch "Niemand zoo groot of hij heeft zijn meester".

entries.luganda: Ekinogezi ekibeera mu ttimpa : kye kikukombya (kikongobya) engalo.
entries.english: The relish (mixed vegetables) that is in the ttimpa (leaves of the arumlily) makes you lick your fingers.
entries.meaning: By itself the ttimpa is not tasty; but mixed with other vegetables (enva entabule) it is a delicacy.

entries.english: The thing that tires me out : will also tire you out.
A good thing : brings theft upon you.
entries.meaning: It causes desires and finally theft.

entries.english: Just a lick : does not finish the salt.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Parum pro nihilo putatur".

entries.english: A little offence (disappointment) : does not tear the barkcloth (or: the throat).
What is looked for by many : will have a finder.
A bad (uneatable) bird is butchered (is plucked) when many are present.
entries.meaning: But if somebody kills a guinea-fowl, he sneaks home, not to be seen by any- body, lest he might have to share the meat with others.

entries.english: He who ties up a bundle of thorns : will know how to carry it.
entries.meaning: Leave the fellow alone with his (difficult) job; he will manage it.

entries.english: A big leaf from the forest : does not cover the (soil in the) bananary.
entries.meaning: For keeping the ground moist in the bananary, banana-leaves are spread over the surface. But big leaves growing in the forest (like kataddabusa) are only used for rolling head pads (nkata) or for wrapping up mushrooms, etc. (Bw'oki- raba waka, nga kireese ekisiki oba butiko -) Rub.C.1501. 1339 Ekirembwe ekitaakule : kizimba mu lumuli. (cf. Ssekirembwe: 4926; cf. Eki- taakule: 1379) The ant that will not live (long) : builds its nest in a dry elephantgrass-stalk. They will soon collect it as firewood. Lack of foresight. "Building one's house on sand!"

entries.luganda: Ekiriggwa jjo : 1) tekikuggyako munno; 2) tekikutunuza ng'alira.
entries.english: What will be forgotten to-morrow : 1) should not separate the friend from you; 2) should not make you look at his (her) tears.
entries.meaning: Trifles should not upset friendly relations.

entries.english: A (harmless) thing with a harmful force (a sorcerer) behind it (will cause trou- ble) : even nnamukago-matooke can choke (if it goes down the wrong passage).
(A man might swear allegiance till death and say) "What will kill you, I shall kill" : (but he won't be able to keep that oath) in the case of his friend being killed by the lake or by fire.

entries.luganda: Ekiri mu mannyo : sikiganya lulimi kwebaka.
entries.english: What is between the teeth : does not let the tongue come to rest.
What is in the little parcel : is known to its owner.
entries.meaning: Each one has his own little secret which he does not give away. - "The heart knoweth its own bitterness".

entries.english: (A woman who talks about her marriage to outsiders saying) "What is wrong at my home, is that and that - -" : spoils the marriage for you and her.

entries.luganda: Ekiri waggulu bwe kiribwatuka : omwana aliyita nnyina.
entries.english: When the power from above thunders : the child will call its mother (in fear).
entries.meaning: Of christian origin, probably from Matth.24.27.

entries.english: (He who asks) "What lies has the night told you (what were you dreaming about)?" : gets you into the gossip of men.
entries.meaning: He will divulge next morning what you have told him in confidence.

entries.english: (You treat) a cherished thing like teeth : you show them when you laugh and cover them immediately after.
What is in a parcel (load, box) for a long time : gets spoiled (mouldy).

entries.luganda: Ekirya atabaala : kye kirya n'asigadde eka (= n'asigadde eka kimulya).
entries.english: What consumes the warrior : consumes also the one left at home.
entries.meaning: Death, accident, snakes, etc. 1) If the soldier is a coward and does not defend his country, the latter will perish. 2) Death is destined for all. "It is appointed unto all men to die" (Hebr.9.27).

entries.english: The reason why hens eat grass : is the day coming to a close.
entries.meaning: No other food is left. Excuse of a poor man who is caught committing theft. Germ. "In der Not frisst der Teufel Fliegen".

entries.english: The gourd-plant that is going to save you : starts with the "bugujju" (young fruits of the cucurbita pepo - gourd plant - which are cut into very thin slices, dried and cooked in fat).
entries.meaning: If you want to get better, start with those.

entries.english: Kindness which cannot refuse : breeds lies.
entries.meaning: Overindulgence! A parent who fulfills every wish of the child, spoils its charac-ter.

entries.english: Too great gentleness makes the cricket bite you.
entries.meaning: Dangerous things must be handled resolutely and firmly. Dutch "Al to goed is buurmen's gek".

entries.english: Over-indulgence : destroys the chieftainship (authority).
Kindness kills : and malice kills.
entries.meaning: You can overdo both. Lat. "In medio stat virtus". Prudence must find the golden mean between extremes.

entries.english: Pity comes to a barren woman : when the food is nearly finished.
entries.meaning: She eats her fill and only then remembers others.

entries.english: Pity comes to a mother : when she sees that the food is coming to an end.
entries.meaning: She is worried that the children won't get enough.

entries.english: The anthill that sends out the enkuyege (at the openings) : gives you the sign that you should lay out the banana-leaves (in the nvubo etc.).
entries.meaning: Preparation for the swarming enswa. - Watch for the signs and be prepared!

entries.english: The beer-tube of the talker : is full of spittle.
entries.meaning: He invites everybody to have a sip. Said of a generous person.

entries.english: A gift-parcel (ekitone) which might please a passer-by (seeing a child carrying it) might not please the receiver.
entries.meaning: The passer-by sees only the wrapping; the receiver sees the contents. "Not all is gold that glitters". Germ. "Der Schein trugt".

entries.luganda: Ekisinde kyo n'ekya munno gw'oyita naye : kye kimu.
entries.english: Your company (friends) and that of your friend with whom you go : is of the same kind (value).
entries.meaning: "Birds of a feather flock together". Germ. "Gleich and gleich gesellt sich gern". "Gleiche Briider, gleiche Kappen".

entries.english: One who comes to eat does not know what makes the cook silent.
entries.meaning: Probably the wife had difficulty with her husband.

entries.english: A wild animal does not devour a poor man.
entries.meaning: His poverty makes him walk everywhere and at any time, whilst a child of the rich says: "A wild animal is going to eat me".

entries.english: The gourd vine that branches out : gives you the idea of making a frame-work (to encourage the growth and to reach the desirable shape of the gourd).

entries.luganda: Ekitagaanwa musana : bwe bakugoba mu luggya ogwotera mu nsiko.
entries.english: A thing that cannot be refused (to anybody) is the sunshine : if they drive you away from the courtyard, you can still bask in it out in the wilds.
What is not yours : is comparable to the breast of a small girl.
entries.meaning: It cannot be used by anybody; it serves no purpose yet. - Man cannot dispose of someone else's property. Don't touch it!

entries.english: Where there is no relationship, there is no inheriting : as with the cultivated banana and the wild banana.
entries.meaning: The two plants are of different species; no mutual fertilisation.

entries.english: What is unexpected (frightens) : even a piece of dry meat drives the dog away.
entries.meaning: If it is thrown at him, he thinks it is a stone.

entries.english: Trouble which is not revealed : increases in the mind.
entries.meaning: "Company in distress makes the sorrow less". Germ. "Geteilter Schmerz ist halber Schmerz".

entries.english: What is not there : does not make the little one cry.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Ignoti nulla cupido". Germ. "Aus den Augen, aus dem Sinn". "Out of sight, out of mind". What the eye does not see, the heart does not crave after.

entries.english: An unheard-of thing : a child to eat its friend (companion).

entries.luganda: Ekitaliibwa tikirema kwala : ekikere kyayaza ennyama ku mutwe.
entries.english: What is not eaten (not taken away) will multiply : (therefore) the frog increases the amount of flesh on its head.
(ekiswa) An ant-hill that does not produce "nswa" is found out (is known) by one who has been in the place for some time.
A thing that cannot speak : obeys the one who can.
entries.meaning: Superiority of man over animals.

entries.luganda: Ekiteezadde (= ekiteezaala) tekyala : kasooli agoberera muyini kwekoota.
entries.english: What does not bring forth cannot multiply : the maize follows the example of the hoe-handle in bending itself.
entries.meaning: The ripening maize-cob takes the shape of the bent hoe-handle which has helped in the planting. 50.20, Duta 316. 1399a Ekitooke : kidda walime.

entries.english: The banana-plant makes the house-owners similar to itself.
entries.meaning: Both bring forth: children and ensukusa or ebiwago, often even an equal number.

entries.english: What kills the leopard : is something heavier than it.
entries.meaning: Said of a thing (a job, an office) that is too heavy, too difficult.

entries.english: What finishes tenancy is laziness.
entries.meaning: No chief likes lazy tenants.

entries.english: Interminable waiting (whilst others are cooking) : does away with fire-wood and water.
entries.meaning: Said about an unwanted guest.

entries.luganda: Ekitundu kya gonja : kyamponya enjala ku Mulago.
entries.english: A piece of gonja (sweet plantain) : has saved me from starving at Mulago.
entries.meaning: Formerly the chiefs attending court in the lubiri used to stay on Mulago-hill, where there was scarcity of food. Expression of gratitude.

entries.luganda: Ekitwala omwaka ewala : nkuba kubula (= eba nkuba obutatonnya).
entries.english: What makes the year long : is the missing rain.
entries.meaning: If something is hoped for ardently, time seems to go very slowly.

entries.luganda: Ekiwera mu ttama : kye kikuwa envunyuula (= engaaya).
entries.english: What fits into the mouth : gives you a chance to chew it properly.
entries.meaning: Not too big and not too small. 67.45. 1415 Ekiwero : tekiriraana muliro. A rag : should not be kept near the fire. "The man who flirts with danger will lose his life" (Ecc1.3.26). Concupiscence. M.234. 1416 Ekiwola : bakikwasa ngalo (or: tikikwokya ngalo). What has cooled down : they can get hold of with the hands (or: does not burn your fingers). New things are eyed with suspicion (fashions, laws).

entries.english: What is sweet (pleasant to the senses) : makes (you) forget (your) dignity.
entries.meaning: Overeating, drinking, stealing etc.

entries.english: (or: Ekiwoomerera olutata : eba nkenku.) What is being sweetened constantly : brings forth nkenku (beer spoiled by the lack of muwemba ferment).
entries.meaning: Softness, lack of firmness or solidity etc. "Pleasures pall".

entries.luganda: Ekiwuugulu bwe kikaabira mu luggya Iwo : ng'ennyumba omenyawo.
entries.english: If an owl hoots in your courtyard : you tear your house down.
entries.meaning: Old superstition. If a dangerous person wants to befriend you, you keep aloof.

entries.english: A harmless insect is a cow (= plaything) for the children (harmless pet-cow).
What makes the ngalabi-drum rot : is scarcity of beer.
What flies high in the air : gives the fowl a stiff neck.
entries.meaning: To build castles in the air brings disappointment.

entries.luganda: Ekiyita waggulu : otega wansi; empungu terya bire.
entries.english: What flies in the air : you trap on the ground; the eagle does not live in the clouds.
entries.meaning: It has to come down for food. - Man is earth-bound. Do not aim too high - above your state or capacities!

entries.english: If you do something that vexes your brother : do you complain that the same thing makes your husband angry?
entries.meaning: The husband will be angry more quickly than your brother.

entries.english: What makes the bad man loved : is unknown to the good.
Let the cause of your stealing : be the reason for getting a thrashing with sticks.
entries.meaning: Stealing brought the sticks upon you.

entries.luganda: Ekyakutuma okusamira : kirikwokya omuliro kinaakusuula mu muliro).
entries.english: What made you pretend to be possessed by a spirit : will burn you by fire.
entries.meaning: Such pretenders were tried by ordeal. Real basamize were supposed not to suffer any harm through it.

entries.english: Let the cause of your longevity : be the result of growing grey hair on your head.
entries.meaning: Old age is the cause of your grey hair. - The white flowers of jjobyo (penta- phylla) are the symbol of grey hair, of old age. Engl. "Silverhaired". Germ. "Der Schnee des Alters".

entries.luganda: Ekyalo ddiba lya mbogo : terizingibwa omu.
entries.english: A village is like a buffalo-skin : one man cannot roll it up by himself.
entries.meaning: The chief requires helpers.

entries.english: A village in which there are no young banana-shoots : is doomed to die.
entries.meaning: If there are no children left, the nation dies out.

entries.luganda: Ekyalo ekitatta basenguse : ne bamuzibi b'amaaso basenguse musana.
entries.english: In a village where they don't kill deserters (who leave the service of the chief) : also the blind can leave in day4ight.
entries.meaning: Formerly those who were caught leaving, were robbed of everything, of women, children and live-stock.

entries.english: The village from which an acquaintance (of yours) has departed : you show with pouted lips.
entries.meaning: If he was still there, you would go there.

entries.english: In the village where you suffer from a sore : you complain about flies.
entries.meaning: You forget that you yourself attract them.

entries.english: The village of the old man : is called jjingirizi (abundance, too much).
entries.meaning: Whether it is work or walk or food, he always says: "Too much for me".

entries.english: The young of a sheep : is pretty, when it is still small.
The last blow splits the head.
entries.meaning: Revenge is sweet. Germ. "Wer zuletzt lacht, lacht am besten".

entries.english: The wicked (large) lizard : is the master on the wild aloe.
entries.meaning: Applications: 1) A wicked mulangira is not reproachable for his bad deeds, because he is the son of the king. This proverb was coined by king Kiyimba as a name for his house. 2) If your father is a bad man, you cannot exchange him for a good one. 3) A person might be despised by outsiders, but respected in the home.

entries.luganda: Ekkubo ly'omulimba : liba ku lusebenju (= likala emanju).
entries.english: A liar's path : runs at the back of the house.
entries.meaning: He does not want to be seen, coming or going.

entries.english: Ten (different) people do not have the same bad opinion about the same person.
entries.meaning: There is always one - or more - who will tell that person, what people say about him (or her).

entries.english: At the end of the year (i.e.
entries.meaning: harvest, July) : you also cut lots of banana-fibre. The "mwaka gwa kasambula" brings so much food (mpande, binywebwa, ntungo etc.), that you require considerable banana-fibre to tie all the "mitwalo gy'emmere".

entries.luganda: Ekuba omunaku tekya : esigala ku mutwe.
entries.english: Rain falls on a poor fellow and does not stop : it remains on his head.
entries.meaning: Bad luck is haunting him (death, famine, fire etc.).

entries.luganda: Ekyanika taaba bwe kikubirwa enkuba ebweru : nga nnannyinikyo taliiwo.
entries.english: If the tobacco spread out (for drying) in the open is ruined by rain : (you know that) the owner is not at home.
entries.meaning: Otherwise he would bring it into safety.

entries.english: (If one says) "It made me go disappointed" : (it is a sign that) he got no presents, where he was on a visit.

entries.luganda: Ekyasooka kye kikulu : akakowekowe ke kakulira ekirevu (= enkowekowe zikulira ekirevu).
entries.english: What was first, is important : it is the eye-lash that is older than the beard.

entries.luganda: Ekyasooka kye kikulu : eky'ensuuti ky'enkoko sikyetikka.
entries.english: (ekyoya) What was first, is important : the tail-feather of the hen does not carry.
entries.meaning: It is the head that carries loads, not the tail. The tail grows last.

entries.english: Saying "good-bye" : does not bring the day to a close for you.
entries.meaning: So says the visitor who wants to leave and cannot say "good-bye" to everyone. It is only a formality from which one is dispensed in circumstances.

entries.english: Terror comes even to a courageous man.
entries.meaning: To be terrified does not mean that one is a coward.

entries.luganda: Ekyekulumbaza tikituuka wangulu : singa enjovu etuuka ku bire.
entries.english: What exalts itself, does not reach heaven : otherwise the elephant would reach to the clouds.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Gott lasst die Baume nicht in den Himmel wachsen".

entries.english: What ripens quickly : rots quickly.
entries.meaning: Engl. "Soon ripe, soon rotten". Germ. "Wie gewonnen, so zerronnen".

entries.english: A curtain (in a one-room house) provides more privacy than a blanket (kikunta) on the bed.
entries.meaning: Or: A curtain draws the immediate attention and should therefore be clean (first impressions).

entries.luganda: Ekyonooneka nga mmwenna mulaba : tokinenyeza munno.
entries.english: If a thing gets spoiled, whilst all of you see it : you cannot blame your neigh- bour for it.
Strike the iron before cold air has been blown on it.
entries.meaning: "Strike while the iron is hot!"

entries.luganda: "Embaga enyuma kiro" : bw'atagenda kubba, agenda kulwana.
entries.english: (One who says) "A feast is especially entertaining at night" : (has probably special likings) either he goes stealing or he is out for a fight.
entries.meaning: The night gives him a good chance for both purposes.

entries.english: Even one who has (for vegetables) only ttimpa (arum-lily) : can prepare a quick feast Ttimpa is easily prepared, but is not tasty by itself.
They treat the axe carefully when climbing (the tree, to cut the branches).
entries.meaning: But when the work is done, they throw it down. Germ. "Der Mohr hat seine Schuldigkeit getan, der Mohr kann gehen".

entries.english: A mangy dog bites a healthy one to kill it (out of jealousy).
Mbiro ntono: 2734a) 5.8.1482a Embiro tezimala musango.
entries.meaning: Running away does not end a dispute. It does not clear you of a misdeed.

entries.luganda: Embogo ezaala : n'omutyuma guzaala (or: ne Mucuuma azaala).
entries.english: The buffalo begets children : and the lion begets children (or: and Mucuuma begets children).
entries.meaning: The lion often hunts the buffalo. The buffalo thinks: wait, till my children are grown up; they will avenge me. - "Mucuuma" is the name of a famous hunter.

entries.english: A good story dries up the nose.
entries.meaning: One does not dare blow one's nose, whilst listening to it.

entries.english: Conversation carried on at a distance : only becomes people who quarrel.

entries.luganda: "Emboozi k'egwe amakerenda" : ng'omuyala atuuse we bafumba.
entries.english: "Let the interminable talk come to an end" : (says) the hungry one, when he arrives where they are cooking.
Stories don't grow old : it is the narrator who makes them old (by the way of telling them, or by saying: "That one I have told you before, I will not repeat it").
entries.meaning: This and the foregoing proverb are often used whilst taking leave as a compli- ment for the entertainment.

entries.english: "The conversation was not very interesting" : (so says one) if he arrived when the meal was finished.
What the chief's place has given you : is its own.
entries.meaning: A chief's order may not be disputed.

entries.english: "You cannot say good-bye to a chief' : (so says one) who is not a favourite.
entries.meaning: He might be called back on account of a complaint against him or he has no chance of getting any presents.

entries.english: The chief's place is not a place to be played with.
entries.meaning: Respect of authority. Rub .C.825. 1497 Embugo za muno : zirintwala ekiwaalo. (cf. Kirintwala ekipaalo: 2332) The barkcloths of this place (i.e. not getting any clothing here) : will make me run away soon. The wife intends to leave her husband, because he does not give her her dues.

entries.luganda: Embugo ziwooma ntono : nga yeebikka bbiri, nga yeesiga ezo okumumala.
entries.english: Even a few barkcloths can make one happy : if the one who covers himself with two is content with them.
"The things you have inquired about are vegetables" : if she has cooked them.
entries.meaning: The brother has asked: what have you brought here? It would be bad manners, were he to ask that of his mother or any other cook. But with his sister he can risk it.

entries.luganda: Embuzi bw'eva ku nnyiniyo : era n'omusumba tagisobola.
entries.english: If a goat strays from its owner : even a herdsman can't manage it.
entries.meaning: Children running away from their parents or guardians are unmanageable also for the teachers.

entries.english: A goat is crying without tears.
entries.meaning: Said of a person who has no intention of giving anything, but pretends to have great compassion.

entries.luganda: Embuzi terya ntula : nga yalabira ku nnyina waayo.
entries.english: A goat does not eat ntula (edible fruits of a nightshade-plant) : if it has seen its mother (leaving them alone).
If the dog has nobody to incite it : it will not hunt.
entries.meaning: It needs the encouragement of the hunter (nti kwata! lya!).

entries.luganda: Embwa bw'eggwa amaanyi : nga n'amaddu gawedde.
entries.english: If a dog loses its strength : also its desire (for food etc.) come to an end.
A hunting dog : brings forth one that is useless for hunting.
entries.meaning: "Enkolya" stands for "having no sense, useless". Children often lack the talents of their parents.

entries.english: Many dogs : mislead the edible rat.
entries.meaning: They prevent it from escaping. Germ. "Viele Hunde sind des Hasen Tod".

entries.luganda: Embwa eyiggira gaayo : n'aga mukama we.
entries.english: The dog hunts for its own desire (of meat) : and for that of his master.
entries.meaning: Egoistic and altruistic motives.

entries.english: The dog does not forget the one who reared it (whether he is mukopi or mwa- mi).
entries.meaning: Gratitude to parents and benefactors!

entries.luganda: "Embwa yange tebba" : ng'eyise ku lwa taaba.
entries.english: (olwaniko) "My dog does not steal" : (that may be) if it walks where tobacco is laid out (for drying).
entries.meaning: Tobacco is no attraction for a dog. Dutch "De gelegenheid maakt den did". 34.63, Ssal.p.38. 1514 Embwa ya nnamaaso : bw'etebba n'eyigga. (cf. Abalungi mbwa: 0037) M.250, L.249.

entries.luganda: Embwege ziwa emmere obwami : nti emyuse ey'eggulo; gye banaafumba jjo eriba Ssekiboobo nandiki Mukwenda?
entries.english: Simpletons give chieftainships to the food (matooke) : (because they say) the matooke (of today) "emyuse ey'eggulo" (which might mean) the food is similar to that of yesterday (in its good taste) (or: it is second in command to that of yesterday); (answer) will what they cook tomorrow, be the Ssekiboobo (ssaza- chief of Kyaggwe) or Mukwenda (ssaza-chief of Ssingo)?
Friendships die : (but) a good neighbour does not despise you.
entries.meaning: It is better to have a good neighbour than a friend (far away). The neighbour comes to your assistance, when you raise the alarm.

entries.luganda: Emitawaana emingi : gikukuliza enjala ku ngalo.
entries.english: A lot of work : lets the nails grow on your fingers.
entries.meaning: You don't find time to cut them.

entries.luganda: Emitawaana emingi : gyaziyiza wannyindo okwekolera oluggi.
entries.english: (or: Emitawaana gyalobera wannyindo okweggala.) Much work has prevented the nose from making doors (at the nostrils).

entries.luganda: Emiti emito : gye giggumiza ekibira (= gye kibira).
entries.english: It is the young plants : that strengthen the forest.
entries.meaning: The little children are the hope of the future. Lat. "Spes patriae!" French "Les plus humbles creatures ont leur role ici-bas".

entries.english: From many heads : trouble results.
entries.meaning: Used for: Why do you bring the matter before so many people? - Lat. "Quot homines, tot sententiae".

entries.luganda: Emitwe emingi : mwe muva ekigambo ekituufu.
entries.english: When many put their heads together : they will find the right judgement.
When they have given the mmandwa (person possessed by a lubaale) his fee : he does not stay (or: he goes away).
entries.meaning: Said to people, who have received what was due to them.

entries.luganda: Emmeeme ekutundugga : nga kanyonyi akakwate mu ngalo.
entries.english: Your heart is beating (excitedly) : like (that of) a little bird you hold in your hand.
"The heart drops (in my breast)" : (so you say) when you see somebody giving you (something you really want).

entries.luganda: Emmeeme etujuba (= etefumba) kigambo : ekwogeza munno ky'atalyerabira.
entries.english: A heart that does not consider a word carefully : makes you speak something your neighbour won't forget.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Et semel emissum volat irrevocabile verbum" (Horace).

entries.english: It is better for the heart to grieve (to feel lonely or to experience sorrow) than to die.
Where the heart is : the feet will soon follow.
entries.meaning: What the heart wishes at night : the feet will soon pursue in the morning.

entries.luganda: Emmeeme si bigere : etuuka gy'otootuuke nga olowoozayo.
entries.english: The heart is different from the feet : thought can go where the feet cannot reach.
The heart of an old person : keeps silent about many things.
entries.meaning: Long life makes one prudent and patient.

entries.english: The heart of the wanderer : is worried about returning home.
entries.meaning: He might not find his people or his former happiness again. The prodigal son!

entries.luganda: Emmere embisi tekubya mukazi : kubanga akusaasidde enjala.
entries.english: Half-cooked food does not bring a beating for the wife : because she has shown pity with your hunger.
entries.meaning: The man impatiently calls for food, although it is not ready yet; the wife obe- diently brings it.

entries.luganda: Emmere ennyingi : etta mwana wa boowo.
entries.english: Over-eating kills the child with many relations.
entries.meaning: All of them stuff him (her) full of good things.

entries.english: Tasty food is finished, when you would like to eat more.

entries.luganda: Emmere ey'abatabaazi gye bagenda balya : twayita muno nga tweriisa enkuuli.
entries.english: The food of the warriors which they eat on the march : (is) we passed here "nga tweriisa enkuuli" (i.e.
entries.meaning: whilst we fed ourselves with nkuuli (= amaanyi)). "Okweriisa enkuuli" means "to brag" or "to show strength". A play on the words "emmere" and "kweriisa".

entries.english: Food for one alone : tastes well in famine time.
entries.meaning: If there are more to eat there won't be enough.

entries.english: The midday-food is not measured.
entries.meaning: There is always an allowance for possible guests.

entries.luganda: Emmese ennenyi : tiyeesimira bunnya; esinnana busime.
entries.english: A rat that is a stranger (in the surroundings) : does not dig holes; it finds them dug.
entries.meaning: Visitors do not work; they are made comfortable by others.

entries.english: (He who says - when told to bring dry elephantgrass-stalks for the chief) "How much do the reeds cost?" (i.e.
entries.meaning: nothing) : makes his tenancy lasting. He willingly does the job, saying: that's easy enough. The chief likes to keep such people.

entries.english: Where the gun points : there it kills.
entries.meaning: Or: Wherever the gun reaches it conquers. What can spears do against guns?

entries.luganda: Emmwanyi gye weesiga : tebaamu mulamwa (-= muwula).
entries.english: The coffee-bean you have trusted : contains no kernel.
entries.meaning: Outside sound, inside empty, rotten. - False friends.

entries.english: (I'll put a stop to your) insolence : as syphilis puts a stop to the insolence of the partridges.
entries.meaning: The partridges have legs with white spots like syphilitics with "bikaata". There is no denying that they are not syphilitic.

entries.english: The impossible fellow occupies the front-seat (in the canoe).
entries.meaning: And when they land, he jumps out, thereby pushing the boat back.

entries.english: The mpafu (fruits of the incense tree) that are far out on the branches, are the ones that fall.
A part of the kiwagu (one row on the banana-bunch) - taken off by the seller - cheats the buyer, who cannot cut off his own bunch (who has no bananary of his own).
Unending strife : finally ends in blows for the hated woman (not for the fa- vourite).

entries.luganda: Empale ya lucoolo eba emu : y'ekyala, y'ekola emirimu.
entries.english: The poor man has only one pair of trousers : the same for visiting, .the same for working.
Sheer malice : makes the hen throw away the green grass-hopper.
entries.meaning: Applied to a mulogo who kills, but does not eat his victim.

entries.english: Brandishing weapons does not affect the legs, but the mouth.
entries.meaning: Refers to bragging before the fight and fleeing, when it starts.

entries.english: A bridesmaid does not become the bride herself (although she is dressed up like the bride).

entries.luganda: "Empisi enzitira omwana" : nga bali ku wuwe.
entries.english: "The hyena is killing my child" : (so cries the father) when the stronger wrestlers are on his son.
The voracious hyena : dies through a banana-stump.
entries.meaning: They put up a trap for the hyena by fixing a sharp spear head into a cut-off banana stem over which a piece of meat is suspended. The hyena jumps for the meat and falls into the spear.

entries.english: The lion is the Lord and Master of the animal world.
The market-tax comes from home (i.e.
entries.meaning: must be brought along) : if it is known beforehand.

entries.luganda: Empummumpu mu lusuku : kubanga zikoonola nnyingi.
entries.english: (Men are like) flowersheaths of the plantain : because many curve off from the stem.
entries.meaning: Men go on begetting children. - Also a human foetus up to the third month is called "mpummumpu".

entries.luganda: Emputte baaziwa okulya Masaka (Kyalugo) : ne zirya Kasaka (Bbaale).
entries.english: They gave the simpletons the order to occupy Masaka : and they chose Kasaka instead.
entries.meaning: King Jjunju ordered his chief of newly conquered Buddu - his name was Yigga - to reside at Masaka; but Yigga disobeyed, stayed at Kasaka and lost his post. - A different version is given in Munno 1913 p.41.

entries.english: Urging on the dogs in two different directions (on a hunt) : leads them astray.
entries.meaning: Two masters! "Too many cooks spoil the broth".

entries.english: Emyungu (vegetable marrow of poor nutritive value) which are tightly com- pressed, split the cooking pot.
entries.meaning: They try to make up for the poor quality by adding quantity. "Prudence _is better than force". Germ. "Gewalt wird nicht alt".

entries.luganda: Endege ziba nnyingi : ne ziyoogaana (= ne ziyomba, = ne zivuga).
entries.english: If the ankle-bells (on the children's feet) are numerous : they make a lot of noise.
entries.meaning: If there are many people together, they can do a lot of work. "Many hands make light labour".

entries.luganda: Endiga w'ekootakoota : emanyi nga waggulu nga wala.
entries.english: Where the sheep walks with its head down : it knows that it is far to the top (of the hill).
entries.meaning: Young people do not understand the difficulties of life. But in old age one has gained experience.

entries.english: (One who thinks by himself) "The sickness gets worse at night" : covers the live coal with ashes.
entries.meaning: He can then kindle the fire quickly.

entries.luganda: Endwadde ennene tewonera lumu : embogo bagifumita effumu limu?
entries.english: A grave sickness does not disappear in a day : do they kill a buffalo with one spear?

entries.luganda: Endwadde etewona : 1) ekuggyako erinnya; 2) emala eddagala.
entries.english: A sickness that does not get better : 1) takes away the name (of a person) (finally they give him (her) the name "Nsula bubi", because he (she) always says so); 2) gradually finishes the medicine.
A sick animal (cow, hen, etc.) does not eat with the healthy ones.
entries.meaning: Also applied to sickness and work.

entries.luganda: Endwadde ya kibiribiri : ng'olangira (= nga n'okulangira eddogo)?
entries.english: Should you immediately attribute a body rash to witchcraft?
entries.meaning: Look first for natural causes (food, infection, etc.)!

entries.english: Sickness of friendship : (is caused by) a misdeed.
entries.meaning: Some ill-chosen word or action wounds the feelings of the friend and destroys the friendship.

entries.english: "The sickness of a child is not contagious" : (says the visitor) if the child's mother is a favourite.
entries.meaning: And he tells the mother: give me the child to hold for you.

entries.english: Eating up everything at one sitting : has laid waste to Mulajje.
entries.meaning: The inhabitants of Mulajje (Bulemeezi), after one good harvest, ate up every- thing, even the seed. The next year they could not plant and left their place. Application: Selling one's land to get money, instead of developing it, is short- sightedness.

entries.english: The basket of coffee-beans is empty (has gone round).
entries.meaning: The discussion (argument) is finished; everyone has had his say.

entries.luganda: Endiiro (= endiira) y'okumpi terwa kudda : ejjobyo liddira mu mutwe.
entries.english: The basket of coffee-beans that is passed between a small group of persons soon comes back (from where it has started) : like the (white flowers of the) jjobyo-plant (i.e.
entries.meaning: grey hair) which soon appear on the head in advancing age.

entries.english: "The oracle is finished" : (so says the mulaguzi) if he was talking about (if the message was about) a person who has just arrived.
To receive badly : is better than poverty.
entries.meaning: To receive little is better than to receive nothing. Engl. "Half a loaf is better than no bread".

entries.english: An orphan does not die in childhood.
entries.meaning: It seems to be the fate of orphans to remain alive for a long life of trouble.

entries.english: The bushbuck that does not heed the warning of the hunter's horn will die.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Qui amat periculum, peribit in illo". French "Le destin est sourd". Germ. "Wer nicht horen will, muss fahlen".

entries.english: The bushbuck that keeps away (from the hunter) : makes its meat tough (or: becomes old).
A bushbuck does not get tired (does not lie down) : where there is no forest.
entries.meaning: If you see that it lies down, it will die.

entries.luganda: Engalangasi aginoonyeza mu banne : nti banno balima, tolaba?
entries.english: A lazy fellow looks for his food amongst his friends : (therefore they ask him) your friends work in the field, don't you see (and you do naught)?
A weak leopard : eats clay.
entries.meaning: An old kind chief has no power (authority). A strong, even a cruel master gets more respect.

entries.english: "The drums do not sound for nothing (they always convey a message)" : (so you say) if your warrior-friends have come back unharmed (they bring booty!).

entries.luganda: Epnombe y'ekikaayi (= ey'ekireku) : tekulagaanyisa na munno.
entries.english: A horn made from a gourd : is not fit to announce (to make an arrangement with) your friend.
entries.meaning: Because it might break and then you have no means of sending the message. - Do not trust unreliable things!

entries.luganda: Epnombo ekwata omwami : 1) ebuna ekyalo; 2) tereka muganzi (waka).
entries.english: The way a chief acts (his mannerism, walking, speaking, etc.) : 1) spreads to the whole village; 2) does not pass over the favourite.
Good manners (behaviour) : make you speak well about a dead person.
entries.meaning: Lat. "De mortuis nil nisi bene!"

entries.english: The way of obtruding one's self as a relation : which is called "ensebeezi".
entries.meaning: The person doing so is not really related or only a very distant relation and they don't want to acknowledge him.

entries.english: Hunger is like having no children : you want to send somebody and nobody goes.
entries.meaning: You ask for food and nobody gives you any.

entries.english: Hunger is gnawing pain in the throat.

entries.luganda: Enjala eruma omuwuulu : y'etuumisa nnyinimu erinnya, nti "Byakagambwa", emmere yaffe eyasuze tunaagirya ddi?
entries.english: If hunger hurts a bachelor : it makes him address the master of the house with the name "Byakagambwa", when shall we eat our food that has been put aside?
entries.meaning: "Byakagambwa" is an imaginary name which the wife of the master should not understand.

entries.english: One who is hungry : puts something aside for tomorrow (cold food for to- morrow morning).
entries.meaning: Said of somebody who likes to eat early in the morning. - Looking ahead is wisdom.

entries.english: If many hunters urge on the dog (in different directions) : they put it off the track.
entries.meaning: Contradictory orders by parents, superiors, etc.

entries.luganda: Enjogera embi teyuza bulago (= kamwa) : singa obw'eŋŋaaŋa bujjudde nkindo.
entries.english: Bad talk does not tear the throat (or: the mouth) : otherwise the hornbill's throat would be full of seams (being mended).
entries.meaning: The hornbill has a hideous cry.

entries.english: A gossiping visitor : is sure to hurt his host in his weak point.
A chatterer (incessant talker) : causes the hen to leave eggs unhatched.
entries.meaning: When he arrives, he asks: where does the hen lay my eggs? Hearing that the hen thinks: perhaps there are men's eggs under me, and being disgusted, deserts them.

entries.luganda: Enjuba n'omwezi bwe byalwana : ne bigwa e Bakka, Wanga n'abiwanga.
entries.english: When the sun and the moon were fighting : they fell down at Bakka, and (the lubaale) Wanga put them back (into their places).
entries.meaning: Bakka is a hill in Busiro, the butaka of the ffumbe-clan. Wanga (or Muwanga) is a traditional deity.

entries.luganda: Enju y'omu nnungi : okuba ennoga akalanga.
entries.english: To live alone in a house is pleasant : you knead your morsel of matooke un- disturbed.
entries.meaning: Saying used by women who have no muggya (concubine) to deal with.

entries.english: Staring (at the visitor eating) makes one eat the cooked hen of the visitor.
entries.meaning: The visitor notices it and gives part of the chicken to the hungry looking host. Bad manners!

entries.luganda: Enkanula maaso yagoba olubende mu nju ne lugenda lubeera mu nsiko.
entries.english: The staring (protruding) eyes drove the field-rat out of the house and it went to live in the field.
entries.meaning: It saw the dead house-rat in the trap.

entries.english: The monkey does not settle a dispute concerning the forest.
entries.meaning: A partisan cannot give an unbiased opinion (Kirwan). Dhop. "Oner kithum banja ri lul".

entries.english: Impossible tales (about far-away places) you might tell an old person.
entries.meaning: Because he never will go there to see for himself.

entries.luganda: Enkobe ento eseka ekibira nga kiggya.
entries.english: The little monkey laughs when the forest is on fire.
entries.meaning: It does not understand that it might burn him, too. Foolish joy over what might be a disaster. Childish folly.

entries.luganda: Enkodomali enywera amazzi ku nsuwa : sso nga waliwo olwendo.
entries.english: An impractical (stupid) fellow drinks water out of a water-pot : although there is a ladle at his disposal.
If the hen has no more eggs : it will not bring forth its intestines.
entries.meaning: You can't ask for the impossible. Lat. "Ad impossibile nemo tenetur".

entries.english: A chicken that has eaten his fill : makes its crop dance (is happy).
He who tears off a piece of the banana-leaf (used as a table cloth) to make a kawujjo to ladle out the sauce : does not do it, where he sits.
entries.meaning: He takes it from another man's place.

entries.luganda: Enkuba bw'etonnya : ne bannamunye banaaba mu bitaba.
entries.english: When it rains : even the wagtails splash in the pools.
entries.meaning: When a rich man dies, many profit from his riches.

entries.luganda: "Enkuba eritonnya ddi?" : emutonnya (= ekutonnya) mu kamwa.
entries.english: "When will the rain come?" : (they answer him sarcastically) it will fall into your open mouth (when you lie dead).

entries.luganda: "Enkuba eritonnya ddi?" : ne tulya ku mpwankimpwanki; w'alaba ekkovu asammuza oluti (= olusirinnanyi bw'alaba luyingira, ng'asammulira bweru).
entries.english: "When will the rain come?
entries.meaning: (if it only started raining!)" : then we could eat quickly growing things (nva, butiko, etc.); (so one talks) but when he sees a snail (which comes after the rain), he throws it away with a stick (or: when he sees an earthworm coming into his house, he throws it out).

entries.english: Too much rain : prevents the eagle from spreading its wings.
entries.meaning: Too many restrictions, no elbow-room for enterprise.

entries.luganda: Enkuba ka etonnye : tulabe ensiisira we zenkanya emyoyo.
entries.english: Let the rain come : then we shall see that the temporary grass-huts are like the minds of men.
entries.meaning: If they keep out the rain, they are good. The character of men is shown in trials: courage or cowardice in battle, real friendship in adversity, etc.

entries.luganda: Enku ennyingi : zitta mutyabi; enziku etta mwenzi.
entries.english: Too great a load of firewood : kills the gatherer; gonorrhea kills the fornicator.
entries.meaning: Engl. "The pitcher goes so often to the well that it is broken at last". Germ. "Der Krug geht zum Brunnen, bis er bricht".

entries.luganda: Enkula embi : ekaddiya ekikere nga kito.
entries.english: Deformity : makes the frog look old, whilst it is still young.
A small anthill does not call itself a mountain.
If the hoe has become blunt : they sharpen it again (by hammering it thinner).
entries.meaning: Said of giving or taking advice.

entries.english: The fact that there is no hoe : gives the lazy woman a good excuse (for being idle).
entries.meaning: If the husband does not buy her a hoe, she won't dig with her hands.

entries.english: The hoe does not steal where it has been cultivating.
entries.meaning: Where it has planted potatoes, it also has a right to dig them up. "Omukozi asaanira okuweebwa emmere ye" (Matt.10.10).

entries.english: The lake-Victoria-monster (called enkungu-ntale) : is made harmless with stones.
entries.meaning: The fishermen, who are very much afraid of it, take big stones along with them in their canoe, which they throw overboard in such places where the monster may be lying in wait.

entries.english: The (grey) parrot that has seen you (knows you) : throws a ripe mpafu (Uganda- plum) to you.
The termites attract the flying ants (allure them to fly).
entries.meaning: A salesman puts new and shiny things out to attract buyers.

entries.luganda: Enkwale emu : ng'ebigere ossa mu kisasi.
entries.english: (If you have trapped) one partridge : you put its legs under the porch of the house.
entries.meaning: Old superstitious practice, to have more luck in future.

entries.english: A way of going for something, as the visitor goes for potatoes.
entries.meaning: There might be matooke, balugu, etc. dished up for the visitor; but he goes for potatoes, seeing that they are well cooked. Compared with the choice a suitor makes amongst several daughters of the house.

entries.english: Good days : do not dawn twice.
Misery is like the light of the sun : it does not shine on one person only.
entries.meaning: The earth is a vale of tears.

entries.english: Misfortune is not a thing of the past.
entries.meaning: Even the rich and the happy might fall into trouble.

entries.luganda: Ennaku z'abakyala : buli omu azisinda bubwe.
entries.english: The misfortunes which women have : each single woman grieves over them in her own way.
The misfortunes of men : turn up in every conversation (are constantly talked about).
The misfortune of a dog is : even one who has no dog of his own, makes it howl (beats it).
entries.meaning: People without relations, living with others, have a "dog's life".

entries.english: Need makes you work.
There is misery in the place where they say to one : "Get up (from sleep) and eat So one complains, when they rouse him from sleep.
entries.meaning: He says to himself: "If I were a person of standing, they would let me sleep and set aside the food for me". Sarcasm on a lazy fellow.

entries.luganda: Ennaku ziri mu kufiirwa : eyali mwannyoko, okufuuka kitaawo!
entries.english: There is misery in bereavement : the one who was your brother can become your father.
entries.meaning: That happens when the elder brother becomes heir.

entries.english: Misery approaches (creeps in upon you) like uncultivated land.
entries.meaning: Both encroach slowly, imperceptibly upon your peace.

entries.english: Zeal in hoeing at home (of unmarried women) : won't continue (necessarily) in marriage.
entries.meaning: Possible reasons: sickness, pregnancy, discontentedness, etc.

entries.english: Waiting kills the bananas.
entries.meaning: Bananas must be taken at the right time for brewing. If that is passed, only very little juice can be pressed out. "Procrastination is the thief of time".

entries.luganda: Ennoga ya lumonde : eramira wa mukisa.
entries.english: A morsel of potatoes : is a blessing for one who is blessed with a taste (for it).
entries.meaning: Not all appreciate potatoes. A special taste is required for enjoying them. - Special vocations!

entries.english: A bull : becomes strong through falls.
Where the bull drops : there they cut him up.
entries.meaning: Said of anything heavy. Lat. "Divide et impera!"

entries.english: A bull does not fall on his back.
entries.meaning: A cunning man is not easily made helpless, he is not easily driven into a corner.

entries.english: Syphilitic sores (on the soles of the feet) burnt out with softness : do not heal.
entries.meaning: They press the feet unmercifully on scorching hot stones. Dutch "Een goede vader bespart de roede niet".

entries.luganda: Ennyama enkapa esinga nva : enkalubo ekira amaluma.
entries.english: Lean meat is better than (any other) vegetables : tough meat is better than none at all.
entries.meaning: "Half a loaf is better than no bread".

entries.english: The egret does not fly with the shrike (big vulture).
The lake of a peasant is next to his house.
entries.meaning: He cannot buy any fish; so he has to satisfy himself with the vegetables that grow in his garden. Other explanation: If a visitor asks for him they say "Awungukidde awo - - ". "Okuwunguka" means "to cross over the lake".

entries.luganda: Ennyindo teziva bweru : nga wambwa awulidde ey'amasavu.
entries.english: The nose cannot get away from (smelling something) outside : like Mr.
entries.meaning: Dog that smells fat meat. Said of one who seems to be distracted.

entries.english: Despising superiors : does not stop at despising one only.
entries.meaning: As a tenant behaved towards the predecessor (chief), so he will behave also towards his successor.

entries.english: A gratuity : does not kill the trade.
The bird that does not fly about : spits out uneatable remnants.
entries.meaning: Those who don't take trouble to find food, will go hungry.

entries.english: A dwelling house is like birds : it (each house) discusses its own affairs.
entries.meaning: Each family has its own joys, sorrows, difficulties, etc.

entries.english: If there is no woman (mother) in the house : the children do not get enough to eat.
A house is built through visiting.
entries.meaning: A man sees how others build.

entries.english: A house is like a forest : it is no place in which evil talk about a person should be indulged in.
entries.meaning: The person talked about might turn up unexpectedly.

entries.english: A house is like a thicket.
entries.meaning: As the thicket might conceal a dangerous animal, ready to spring on the unwary passer-by, so also a house might conceal a dangerous person.

entries.english: Things there are insipid : like the pieces of cassava (that are separated from the good fruit and put into the ground again for regrowth).
entries.meaning: Insulting a useless fellow: "Oli nsajjalala ng'eza balugu".

entries.english: The bag of one that has gone away : gets filled with stones.
entries.meaning: Thieves will take the contents and replace them with stones.

entries.luganda: Ensawo ey'omusango ebeera mu vviivi : olugira, nti gunzise mu vvi.
entries.english: The bag (the whole weight) of a dispute is in the knee : (because) they say: the dispute has come down on my knee (I,plead guilty).
The father's pocket : always contains something useful (valuable) for the children.
The louse that has bitten you : came out of the barkcloth.
entries.meaning: Said of one who speaks evil about people of his own household.

entries.luganda: Ensenza ennafu : etikka mukama waayo omugugu.
entries.english: Weak ruling (over tenants) : puts the load on the master's head.
entries.meaning: He has to do the work himself.

entries.english: "The country claims its dead" : (one says so) if they have not killed your own near relation.
entries.meaning: No personal sorrow; otherwise he would say: Twaflirwa nnyo etc.

entries.english: The last part of a debt : is collected by a clever man.
entries.meaning: It is as a rule very difficult to get in such remainders.

entries.english: One cent : makes you refuse ten.
entries.meaning: One who shamelessly asks for more, gets nothing at all.

entries.english: One cent is like a little bird : if you don't trap it, you won't catch it.
entries.meaning: Used as a hint for lazy workmen. Germ. "Wer den Kreuzer nicht ehrt, ist des Guldens nicht wert".

entries.english: Cowry-shells (money) do not bring forth (when buried) in the earth.
entries.meaning: Use your money profitably.

entries.luganda: "Ensimbi ze nfuna zimpita mu ngalo" : tatungiramu maliba, zireme kuyitamu.
entries.english: "The money I possess runs through my fingers (I can't keep any money)" : (one who says so) sews no web between them which would prevent the money from running through.
entries.meaning: A spendthrift needs to employ means of greater economy.

entries.english: A sapling of the mutuba-tree gets its companion.
entries.meaning: Said of the propagation of human beings.

entries.english: If a country gets ruined : it is like the nnakasugga-plant that becomes (is used as) njagi.
entries.meaning: The nnakasugga is used as vegetable, but only the leaves. If there are no njagi (ntula) fruits to be had, they sometimes take the fruits of the nnakasugga, which are not appreciated. Compared with a country that has become poor and unimportant.

entries.luganda: Ensisinkano teba ya lumu : enkejje amazzi egaleka mu nnyanja, egasanga mu luwombo.
entries.english: The possibility of meeting each other is not confined to one day : the enkejje (small fish) leaves the water in the lake and finds it again in the luwombo (being cooked therein).
entries.meaning: One must consider things from more than one point of view.

entries.english: A country does not grow up in one day as the mushroom does.
entries.meaning: "Rome was not built in a day".

entries.english: (If they say) "We are far too many sitting in the country" : they break it (ruin it).
entries.meaning: Compared with a branch of a tree, on which there is too much fruit.

entries.luganda: Ensonzi bw'ekukuba mu ttosi : ogikuba mu vvu.
entries.english: If the "nsonzi" (small fish, caught in the mud by draining off the water of the rivulet) besmears you with mud : you besmear it with ashes (whilst smoking it therein).
The fly that loves you : sits down on your sore.
entries.meaning: Said of persons who visit too often.

entries.english: A fly mad for food : dies on the fly-trap (gets caught).
The "nsugga" (vegetable plant) varies according to the quality of the field.
entries.meaning: Children take after their parents.

entries.english: One flying ant : is worth more than a (fat) ddembwe (uneatable insect).
entries.meaning: "Half a loaf is better than no bread". Dutch "Beter een vogel in de hand dan tien in de lucht".

entries.english: The water-lizard that does not take itself out of the sun (that remains basking in it) : makes itself into a cover for the ngalabi-drum.
entries.meaning: They will kill it and use its skin for the drum. - Carelessness in danger.

entries.english: It is thoughtlessness : that will leave the old man on the hill.
entries.meaning: The young people forget that the old must rest.

entries.luganda: Entakyaluka : wa Muwonge (= wa Kakinda) e Jjalambya (or: bagiroga e Jjala- mbya).
entries.english: A person who stays too long as a visitor : (will be dealt with as the man who stayed) with Muwonge at Jjalambya (or: they taught him a lesson at Jjala- mbya).
entries.meaning: Muwonge and Kakinda were two bataka in Mawokota, the first living at Lubanga, the other at Jjalambya, both neighbouring villages. The visitor was taught a lesson there by being accused of having sinister intentions on a married woman and of "spoiling the kyalo".

entries.english: Not to inspect the trap (put out) : causes the meat to rot.
(ennyonyi or mpafu) One who does not aim carefully : won't hit two birds (or: plums) at the same time.
If the cooking pot bursts with the mashed beans and potatoes : there is nobody to blame you (for breaking it).
entries.meaning: Everybody sees that it was not your fault.

entries.luganda: Entamu ennene : terya ka mufumbi; nti suula empiso mu nnyanja tulabe oba onoogiggyamu.
entries.english: (They say) a big cooking pot does not eat a little morsel of ttooke of the cook (i.e.
entries.meaning: if one hides a little thing in a good spot, he is sure to find it again) : (reply) just try and throw a needle into the lake and we shall see whether you get it out again.

entries.english: A light (thin) cooking pot is much talked about.
entries.meaning: It cooks rapidly and it breaks quickly.

entries.english: The cooking pot listens to the first fire.
entries.meaning: If the matooke are not cooked with a lively fire from the very beginning, they won't be done and a second cooking won't help.

entries.luganda: Entamu gye wali ofumbyemu : togamba, nti "ya nfumba mbi".
entries.english: The cooking pot in which you have cooked formerly : you don't call a bad cooking utensil.
entries.meaning: You do not speak of a former wife of yours in an evil way.

entries.english: Taking the menvu-bananas at the wrong time : spoils them for brewing.
entries.meaning: Or: Arguing about the right time spoils the menvu. - Everything in its time. "Too many cooks spoil the broth".

entries.luganda: Entaanya : ow'amaanyi okulwala omunafu ne yeesekera.
entries.english: If there is an unexpected mishap : for instance a powerful man falling sick, the weakling laughs.
An ungrateful person : has no one to give him anything.

entries.luganda: Entate tezaalwa : amakondeere bagafuyira Sseguku, ng'enkumbi eyagalima bakweka.
entries.english: A fool is not born (in the clan) : they blow the makondeere-horns (made from myungu-gourds) at Sseguku, whilst they hide the hoe that has cultivated them.
entries.meaning: A fool is not recognized by his clan; they feel ashamed of him and ignore him. - Sseguku was the fief of the king's homblowers, a hill along the old road to Entebe. - Germ. "Der Mohr hat seine Schuldigkeit getan, der Mohr kann gehen".

entries.luganda: Ente bwe zifa : amaliba gakyalira omwenge.
entries.english: When the cows die : their skins pay a visit to the beer.
entries.meaning: Explanations: 1. One who has lost his riches (herds) has only the skins left to dress in, when he goes for beer. 2. The skins are used for dressing the beer- drums.

entries.luganda: Ente enkulu evaako ennyuma : n'abaana bakulembera.
entries.english: An old cow remains behind : and the young ones go ahead.
entries.meaning: Old people cannot keep pace with the young ones.

entries.english: The owner of the cow that is kept for somebody : is found out when it dies.
entries.meaning: The ownership of such a cow is often disputed. Usually the mulaalo claims that it is not a cow belonging to him, but one belonging to the man who gave it into his charge. - Dishonesty of the herdsmen.

entries.english: For a cow that is not yours : you do not build a stable.
entries.meaning: The owner might get suspicious that you consider it as yours.

entries.english: (A man says) "My animal is a heifer (literally: jumps like the Baziba in their dance)" : (the other taking the literal meaning answers) "When you received it, you jumped over the lake".
A quagmire that is not likely to swallow you up : does not make you get hold of a thorntree.
entries.meaning: In trouble one does not use more painful means than necessary.

entries.english: A messenger is not killed where he was sent.
entries.meaning: Ambassadors are sacrosanct, immune.

entries.english: Even watery (low-quality) vegetables : save you from eating only matooke.
entries.meaning: "One must be grateful for small mercies".

entries.english: Matooke removed from the ashes (warmed up, cooked twice) : are eaten by a poor fellow.
Giving birth to an ugly child : is better than having no child.
entries.meaning: Such a mother can at least be spared the stigma of being called a barren woman.

entries.english: (A man who is received with the greeting) "Eradde,-eradde" (on a visit) : re- ceives bananas (migogo gy'ettooke).
entries.meaning: There will be a good feed.

entries.luganda: Eriggwa likufumitira ku ttale : ate oddira eriggwa n'oggyaamu erikufumise.
entries.english: A thorn has pierced you in the wilds : and then you take another thorn to get out the one which has pierced you.
entries.meaning: It takes a thief to catch a thief.

entries.english: The voice (teaching, instruction) will fall like grains of salt.

entries.luganda: Eri omugga gye tugenda : nti mala okundaga ku ntumbwe; nti onooziraba nga tusomoka.
entries.english: We go towards the river (and the fellow says) : let me see your calves; (the woman answers) wait, you will see them when we cross the river.
entries.meaning: Used to criticise one who interrupts you, whilst you are still speaking.

entries.english: The eye of the master : sees where it is dark.
entries.meaning: His experience shows him where there is something wrong among his subjects. Lat. "Experientia docet".

entries.english: If hunger pinches the owner of the house (and causes the typical folds on his body) : the visitor calls them wrinkles (of old age).

entries.luganda: Erwanira obuko (= ku buko) : ekuuka ejjembe.
entries.english: (ente) A cow that starts fighting in the place of the parents-in-law : breaks a horn.
entries.meaning: Trying to create an impression and going beyond one's strength.

entries.english: A path that crosses another one : is not a good one.
entries.meaning: If two people first walk together and then separate, each one taking a different direction, one might get into trouble (meeting enemies, snakes, etc.) and find no help. Lat. "Vae soli!"

entries.english: A boat that has no oars : must be helped.
entries.meaning: If somebody is helpless, people must come to his aid.

entries.english: (ente) A cow going to another hill (pasture) does not low (longing for the old place).
entries.meaning: Men soon forget kindness received.

entries.luganda: "Essanyu lye nnina mulalu" : baba bamubajjira envuba, nga ye azina (= babajja envuba eno ng'azina).
entries.english: "The joy I feel is like that of a madman" (so one exclaims) : (and the others answer him) even while they cut the stocks, he dances.
Vomiting once : does not prevent you from eating ntula (vegetables) again.
entries.meaning: One should not despise a man (or a thing) on account of one fault.

entries.english: A barren animal : has no pity (consideration) for others when running (away from danger).
entries.meaning: Lack of consideration for shortcomings of others.

entries.english: A (big) fertile bananary : makes you miss a chieftainship.
entries.meaning: Because the chiefs of the bananary-owner do not like to lose the taxes which the owner has to pay for his land. As chief he would be free.

entries.luganda: Eteekutte : tekwefunguliza mwami; waakalwala ejjute nga weefungula, nti liirino linzita.
entries.english: A sickness that is not likely to kill you : does not make you expose yourself indecently before the chief; if you only suffer from a boil (on your buttocks), do you uncover yourself and say: here it is, it is killing me?
(ensonga or ennyama) What is decided by legitimate authority : is not resented by the subjects.
entries.meaning: Or: People do not complain over meat cut up (distributed) by an elder, by authority.
