entries.english: The chicken that does not obey its master : lays eggs that are not fertilized.
entries.meaning: Obedience brings peace and prosperity. Blessing of the fourth commandment: Otyanga kitaawo ne nnyoko.

entries.english: (A person who says) "The earth eats up (destroys)" : speaks evil of the dead.
entries.meaning: He talks behind their backs, because the dead cannot answer.

entries.english: The banana-bunch you have worked for : is sweeter (than the one you got for nothing).
entries.meaning: Engl. "Why is our food so sweet? Because we earn before we eat". P. 1803 Ettooke oliwanirira (= liwanirirwa) : (nga) likyali ku mugogo. (cf. Amagezi gasalwa: 0405) You support the heavy banana-bunch : when it is still up on the stem. "A stitch in time saves nine".

entries.luganda: Ettufu liba wala : akatale k'emmese mu Busoga.
entries.english: A good thing is far away : the rat-market is in Busoga.
entries.meaning: Sarcasm! Rats were considered titbits in Busoga. - "The best things are hardest to come by".

entries.luganda: Ettutu lifumita likyali tto : bwe likula lisogola mwenge.
entries.english: The tip of ssenke-grass stings you, when it is still young : but when it grows older, it helps you to brew beer.
entries.meaning: A former enemy might become your helper.

entries.english: The red biting ant that leaves the marching column : becomes a kaasa (black insect, similar to nsanafu, but travelling singly).
(A man who says to you) "In my place the cattle eat salt-earth" : brings back to you skins only.
entries.meaning: He is a thief. Such a man wants you to give him your cows to look after by telling you that they will have splendid food; but he will probably kill them, sell the meat, and bring only the skins back.

entries.english: "A man who died yesterday, stinks (expression used by one who has had no-thing to eat since yesterday, equivalent to: I want something to eat)" : (and they answer him sarcastically) does a dead man forcibly request-food for his journey?
(ensi) Our country will not become old.
One who is full of beer : blames the door for being drunk.
entries.meaning: In his drunkenness he is unable to close the door and abuses it, saying: Oluggi lutamidde.

entries.english: He who has just eaten of a tasty thing : has the sweetness thereof in his mind.
entries.meaning: "Mulondo" = vanilla, a sweet aromatic fruit. - "The appetite is concealed under the teeth". Food, drink, possessions.

entries.english: A man who has done evil to you : makes you hate all men.
entries.meaning: The evil done to you by one single person makes you suspicious and distrustful also of others. If one does not pay back money loaned to him, you will not be inclined to loan to others.

entries.english: The man who took pity on you : you won't forget (him) till you die.

entries.luganda: Eyakusegulizanga omuntu : bw'akuseguliza omuggo, bw'oba omugezi totuula.
entries.english: If a man who wants you to make room for somebody : tells you to take your stick away, you won't remain sitting, if you are a wise man.
What is stronger than you (what surpasses you in power) : is the court of Ka- wungu (in Mawokota).
entries.meaning: Kawungu was chief and mmandwa; therefore nobody dared to question his decisions.

entries.luganda: Eyakusinze : ensekere ekwetissa omugina (= ekwambaliza amagi); egabiikira e Buddu, egaalulira e Kyaggwe.
entries.english: What is stronger than you is the louse : it makes you carry its nits; it lays them in Buddu and hatches them in Kyaggwe.

entries.luganda: Eyakusinze : entaana ya kabaka masiro, ey'omwami kiggya, ey'omukopi ma- laalo.
entries.english: What surpasses you (is the king, and the chief, because) : the grave of the king is called "masiro", that of a chief "kiggya" and that of a commoner "malaalo".
One who has grown old (grandfather, grandmother) : does not disown (keep away) the children.
entries.meaning: They are all fond of going to the grandparents, who like to see them coming.

entries.english: "The enkejje (which was to serve at your "name's-giving-ceremony") is burnt to cinders (you are doomed)" : (a man who is told that) escapes by leaving his lubugo in the hands of the attackers.
entries.meaning: One rather sacrifices his garment than his life.

entries.luganda: Eyali afudde, bw'olemala : nti Katonda yankolera.
entries.english: You who nearly died in an accident but got away with a lame leg : you com-plain: God has tried me hard!
entries.meaning: You should thank God; it could have been much worse.

entries.luganda: Eyali akuggulirawo : bw'owulira, nti "weggulirewo"; ebiri ku kyoto ng'akutuza mannyo.
entries.english: If you hear the one who formerly opened the door for you himself, telling you: "Open it yourself!"; then he removes what is hanging above the fireplace (parcel with ants) with his teeth (by biting the dried plantain fibre on which it hangs).
entries.meaning: He does not want to let the visitor see the parcel. Said of a miser.

entries.luganda: Eyali akumanyi bw'avaawo : 1) nga bugenderedde; 2) ng'ekkubo lizibye.
entries.english: If the one who knew you, goes away : 1) friendly relations (obumanyi) are gone; 2) passage through property is barred.

entries.luganda: Eyali munno : lw'akubengukako lw'akubanja n'ensimbi emu.
entries.english: As soon as the man who was your friend has broken off the friendship : he will claim every single cent from you.
He that knew her (the old woman who has lost her husband by death) : rescues her from widowhood.
entries.meaning: By marrying her he saves her from misery.

entries.luganda: Eya mukulu wo ezaala, nti efukumula.
entries.english: If the goat of your elder brother brings forth, you (being envious) say: she simply shakes them out and never stops.
The food of the master of the house : does not split the cooking pot.
entries.meaning: They separate his share and later put it back into the pot and keep it on the cooking stones. The volume is much less than if the whole family's food were in.

entries.luganda: Eyasuze obubi : 1) omulabira makeera; 2) omulabira ku makeera.
entries.english: One who has slept badly : 1) shows it in the morning (bad humour etc.); 2) shows it by his getting up early (he is hungry and wants food).
He who has ruined a thing : looks as silly as it does.
One who inquires about the whereabouts of the leopard : will be eaten by it.
entries.meaning: Look for the leopard and it will come upon you. French "Qui parle du diable voit aussitert ses comes".

entries.english: He who waits patiently for the food left over : can also get his fill.
entries.meaning: Dutch "Tien centen maken een dubbeltje".

entries.english: One who knows himself to be a strong fellow : carries the chief over the river.
entries.meaning: He offers himself to show his strength.

entries.luganda: "Ey'embuzi si ya nte" : ng'aliddeko ekifi (= ng'afunyeko, = nga yakaliddeko).
entries.english: "Goat's meat is not cow's meat" : (says one) if he has already eaten his piece of goat (and sees that the others receive cow's meat).
One who admires his own body : won't take advice; and so loses what he values greatly.

entries.luganda: Eyeeraba ebbiri : talaba munne; abeeyagalanga si bwe bafa?
entries.english: A man who admires his own body : ignores his friend; do not those who are selfish die in this manner?
He who admires his own body : does not want to have his fortune told.
He who struts about and gives himself airs : on growing up will lose many chances.

entries.luganda: Eyeesiga embiro : 1) addukira Mbajja; 2) y'aserera omutala (= emitala).
entries.english: One who relies on his quickness (in escaping) : 1) escapes at Mbajja.
entries.meaning: Mbajja is a village in Kyaggwe, near Kojja, where Makanga, a landowner of Mpuma, was arrested by Kabaka Mawanda, because he had favoured the cause of the king's brother and adversary Kagulu Tebucwereke; he managed to escape. One who relies on his quickness : 2) prowls about at night (dances like a muse- zi) on the neighbouring hill. The basezi are hated and have to run for their lives.

entries.english: A man who is confident (that his wife has cooked for him) : does not eat in the village (away from his home).
He who carefully chews cold food (food kept overnight) : gets his fill.
entries.meaning: Patient and conscientious work leads to success.

entries.english: The wife who seeks to please her husband : makes her marriage last.
One who is cautious : kills the fearless.
entries.meaning: "Discretion is the better part of valour". David and Goliath. French "Plus fait circonspection que vaillance".

entries.english: One who has put aside tasty food for tomorrow : looks forward to the morning.

entries.luganda: Eyeewa ez'omu mba (= matu) : gwe bazikuba.
entries.english: (mpi) One who invites a slap on the cheek (or: ears) : will get it.

entries.luganda: Eza kali-mpaka : banyagira (= bazinyagira, = zinyagirwa) mu ssaazi (or: mu ssaazi mwe ziggweera).
entries.english: The cows of a stubborn fellow : are raided next to his very kraal.
entries.meaning: He does not take a warning about approaching danger; he always knows better.

entries.english: (enti) If the small pieces of firewood lie in the same direction as (parallel to) the big log : they won't burn.
entries.meaning: They are put crosswise under the log. If there is no resistance of parents, teachers etc. to the wrongs of the children, there is no obedience and no order.

entries.english: (ensimbi mu basamizi) Riches that will fall into your hands : they point out to you.
entries.meaning: You have to follow the direction of the mmandwa (lubaale-priest), who shows you the way to plenty. Cf. "Lukomera ne Lulina amattire" (Muloboza 1.17).

entries.english: The flying ants that fall into the hole (dug in front of the ant-hill) : are relish (are safely in your possession).
entries.meaning: "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush". Germ. "Ein Sperling in der Hand ist besser als eine Taube auf dem Dach".

entries.english: Vegetables which will serve as relish to matooke : come to an end, even if you don't dip your nnoga (morsel) into it.
The cowries (cents) for ransoming an unfortunate fellow : God strings them together at night.
entries.meaning: Then nobody sees or expects it. Engl. "When bale is highest, boot is highest". Dutch "Als de nood het hoogst is, is Gods hulp het meest nabij". Germ. "Wenn die Not am hochsten ist, ist Gottes Hilfe am nachsten".

entries.english: The property of a cripple : cannot be robbed.
entries.meaning: He will be killed sooner than allow it to be taken.

entries.english: Hens that have someone to raise the alarm : are not eaten by an animal.
entries.meaning: Children that are guarded well by the parents, do not get spoiled.

entries.luganda: Eziruma munno : tezikulobera kwebaka (= zikuyigiriza amagezi).
entries.english: The belly-ache of your neighbour : does not prevent you from sleeping (or: makes you wiser).
entries.meaning: Self-centred egoism, lack of consideration. Lat. "Experientia docet".

entries.english: A price which is not definite : 1) is not liked.
entries.meaning: Bananaries (ensuku) which have no definite boundary : 2) finish off all the ntula-fruit (njagi) (even the unripe ones are taken by one or the other owner).

entries.english: Money that is ransom for your mother : you don't give reluctantly.
Houses abandoned by their master : are open to everybody.

entries.luganda: "Eziva okumu ze mbiro" : nga gw'ayagala asigadde ennyuma.
entries.english: "The speeds that start at the same time are the legal speeds" : (so says one) whose favourite was left behind.
entries.meaning: He means that the winners started before the signal was given.

entries.english: (ente, entebe) The property ,of a man : is not inherited as long as he is alive.

entries.luganda: "Ffe bamu!" : bw'akwata aka munne, ng'assa mu nsawo.
entries.english: "We belong together" : (says the fellow) when he takes the property of his friend and puts it into his own pocket.

entries.luganda: Ffenna tuli byuma : twasisinkana mu ssasa.
entries.english: We all are tools (of the same master) : we were all once made in the same smithy.
entries.meaning: We are children of one and the same God.

entries.english: Get many (children, subjects, tenants) : and the noise (trouble) will grow ac-cordingly.
Let the matooke make a noise (in chewing, on account of being underdone) : if there is only a good amount of it (quantity more esteemed than quality).
Let the fat remain (without finding a buyer) so that I can eat it : so the dog thinks, when he is sent to hawk fat for sale.

entries.luganda: "Gafuma (= gamala okufuma) : bagabejjereza taaba"; nti nnabangogoma alina emmindi?
entries.english: "If the teeth are getting discoloured : they blame it on the tobacco"; has the grasshopper a pipe?
entries.meaning: The lazy rich man does not take the trouble to clean his teeth and retorts that tobacco cannot be the reason.

entries.english: We are only at the beginning.
entries.meaning: Answer to "weebale", when the work has only just begun.

entries.luganda: Gaali masane : ate ente enzirugavu okuzaala amata ameeru!
entries.english: What a marvellous thing : a black cow giving white milk!

entries.luganda: Gaali masane : omusota okulinnya omuti, nga sigulina magulu!
entries.english: What a marvellous thing : a snake without legs climbing a tree!
The water which is in a luleeba (bath made of banana-leaves in a hole in the ground) : is drunk by one who is courageous (takes risks).
entries.meaning: That kind of water is not drinkable.

entries.english: You are pleased with the shrewdness of a lubaale-priest : when you understand it.
entries.meaning: You don't trust him before, because he is wily.

entries.english: The water (from washing the hands) will dry up on the spearshafts : (so says the husband after eating and washing his hands) and he goes away without thanking his wife who has cooked the matooke.
The bananas that have no inclination to ripen : won't do so even with a big fire.
entries.meaning: You can't make a silk-purse out of a sow's ear.

entries.english: (amata) The milk of the calf : is drunk by one that is to live.
entries.meaning: French "Qui vivra boira". Engl. "Struggle for life". Germ. "Kampf urns Dasein".

entries.english: (or: Agaanya bba - - ) A woman who starts to oppose her husband : has found a place to go to.
entries.meaning: She has made up her mind to go and she knows where to go. Applicable also to a servant who intends to leave; very often he causes trouble deliberately.

entries.english: "The spears have brought us together" : (one who says so) will not kill a revengeful person.
entries.meaning: The meeting was accidental; so it will be possible to intimidate the adversary and to escape him.

entries.luganda: Gayita ku kibi : ne gasekera ekirungi.
entries.english: The teeth often pass over (= forget) a sad event and laugh about a good thing (e.g.

entries.luganda: Genda eri e Mbaale mu Baganda banno.
entries.english: Go to Mbaale to your brethren, the Baganda (their cradleland).
entries.meaning: This saying originated after the defeat of the Baganda by the Banyoro at the time of the Kabaka Nnakibinge.

entries.luganda: Ggambo bbi :,lisangwa ku mwoyo (or: wamwenge alisanga ku mwoyo).
entries.english: An evil thing (word or deed) : beer (intoxicating drink) finds it in the soul.
entries.meaning: An evil intention is often carried out under the influence of drink. What a person says or does, when drunk often reveals his mentality. Lat. "In vino veritas".

entries.english: From a dry bone : there can be no gnawing any longer.
entries.meaning: Said of an absolute pauper. Lat. "Nemo dat quod non habet". Germ. "Wo nichts ist, hat der Kaiser das Recht verloren".

entries.luganda: Ggwe bw'olaba ng'oli agalula effunfugu : nga talissangako?
entries.english: If you see that somebody brandishes a lump of soil : (won't you suspect) that he has killed somebody in that manner before?

entries.luganda: Ggwe oh mulimba nga jjembe : lisula ku kikondo, bwe bukeera enkya, nti "nva Buvuma".
entries.english: You are a liar like a "charm" : during the night it has been hanging on the pole (in the house of the mulaguzi), and in the morning it announces: "I come from Buvuma".

entries.luganda: Ggyawo ekikyo ng'omwana aliko nnyina tannajja.
entries.english: Take away your property which the child is playing with, before its mother has arrived.
entries.meaning: When she comes, she will ask you to give the play thing to the child.

entries.english: Their friendship makes them divide the little beer-fly : in comparison to that the flying ant is big.
entries.meaning: They love each other so much, that they share even the tiniest bit between them.

entries.english: Friendship which does not court favour (with the other party) : won't last.
A noble spirit is generous : my friend, you have been good to me!
"That's enough" (you say) : if the one who has hit you on the nose is a relation.
entries.meaning: Otherwise you would return the blow.

entries.english: Where there is plenty of beer : there it is adorned with banana-fringes (there banana-fringes are worn to the dance).
The case cannot be settled : (as the one said) who could not settle it at Mmengo (i.e.
entries.meaning: Apollo the Katikkiro). Sir Apollo often used the word "gulemye" in difficult cases. Therefore he got the name "Gulemye".

entries.english: A fire that has a stirrer : does not go out.
entries.meaning: Headman (overseer) for the work; driving power for an undertaking; motive for an action.

entries.english: Bad behaviour hurts the one who is guilty of it : gonorrhea does not hurt the navel.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Quo quis peccat, eo punietur".

entries.luganda: "Gunadda ne nnywa" : 1) alinda okutoma; 2) talwa kuwuuba ndeku, nti mugu- mazeemu?; 3) asamba endeku.
entries.english: (One who says) "Oh, there will be more beer coming; I shall drink then" : 1) is waiting to complain (that he got nothing); 2) will soon..
entries.meaning: swing his calabash, asking: have you drunk it all?; 3) kicks the calabash (being annoyed that it remains empty).

entries.english: As soon as so and so has started carrying a load : he begins to stoop (he wants to show that they have given him too heavy a load).

entries.luganda: Gundi oyo takuba : nga b'afuga bamuwulira.
entries.english: That Mr.
entries.meaning: So and so does not beat (people) : if those whose master he is, obey him. But what will he do, if they don't obey him?

entries.english: "I feel happy" : (so one says) when he has killed a lamb with his uncle.
entries.meaning: He is looking forward to a welcome feed; he will get the lamb's head.

entries.english: So and so is running to and from : as a married man (called up for war) who has no shield of his own.
entries.meaning: He runs from house to house in search of a shield. - Every householder was supposed to possess a shield and two spears.

entries.english: So and so has pulled himself out of poverty : (and now) he is rolling in pleasure.
entries.meaning: The "new rich", parvenus!

entries.english: (One who confesses) "The case goes against me" : pays a small fine.
entries.meaning: Confessing the guilt diminishes the punishment. Engl. "Confession of a fault makes half amends".

entries.luganda: Gusula : 1) ne gutakusinga, nga mulungi ; 2) gwe gukuwa empoza.
entries.english: If a judgement is postponed over night : 1) and it did not go against you, it is a good one; 2) it gives you a chance of defence.

entries.luganda: "Gute ngutole" : ng'Omuganda awoza n'Omunyolo (= Omuyima anaawoza n'Omuganda).
entries.english: "Leave off pleading and let me go on" : (so an experienced Muganda judge says) when a Muganda pleads in court against a Munyoro.
entries.meaning: The judge knows the ways of both, even if the Munyoro does not speak Luganda very well.

entries.english: A case (crime) that kills the criminal : is finished.
entries.meaning: The death of the criminal satisfies justice.

entries.english: Even if the hunt kills small game only : it is no failure.
entries.meaning: Engl. "Half a loaf is better than no bread". Dutch "Beter weining dan niets".

entries.english: Our friendship has come to an end : it came to an end between King Ssuuna and the Baziba.

entries.luganda: Guweddeko entontogolo : ennyonyi ziyita e ttale (= kkuutwe).
entries.english: When the (wild) figs are finished (on the tree) : the birds fly past it to the un- filled land.
entries.meaning: When the rich man's possessions are exhausted, his friends leave him.

entries.english: (also: Kasita guwedde - - ) "It got finished without trouble" : (one who says so) is sarcastic to the brewer of the beer.
entries.meaning: He hides his disappointment at having missed his share, by saying: Oh, if it only went without trouble (fighting etc.).

entries.english: "I have got my share (mugabo)" : (says one) who has received the top-row of the banana bunch.
entries.meaning: His share is better than that of all the others.

entries.luganda: Guyimbye embwa n'okugulu : nga gulemye omusigire.
entries.english: The dispute has tied the dog (neck) and foot : (so they say) if the dispute is too complicated for the deputy chief.
entries.meaning: Dogs are tied by the neck only, unless they are mad.

entries.luganda: Gwaka nga musana : kaakiro tabulamu (or: ak'ekiro tabulamu).
entries.english: The moon shines like day-light : yet the nature of the night is not missing entirely.
entries.meaning: There are certain signs of the real night, e.g. dances, excesses etc. - Said of any- thing that reveals traces of something under cover, e.g. of a friend who is not quite open or trustworthy.

entries.english: There is plenty of mubisi (sweet cider) : but not plenty of (fermented) beer.
entries.meaning: As long as it is mubisi, there is not much demand; but when it has become real beer, there is always too little. - Mwenge costs more effort and is always in short supply.

entries.english: It was bark of the second (or third) peeling (i.e.
entries.meaning: good material) : and has become like that of the first peeling. The first peeling of the mutuba-stem furnishes inferior material (kitentegere); the following peeling provides good material (musala), unless it is left too long on the stem. - Said of people who were bad when young, good in middle age and bad again in old age.

entries.luganda: Gwa ngalabi : tegunywebwa atudde wamu; bagunywa na kuleekaana.
entries.english: The beer at the ngalabi-dance is not drunk by one who remains at home; they drink it with great shouting.
entries.meaning: A great work can only be achieved when many come together and encourage each other with singing (shouting).

entries.english: (One who says) "It was too much for me" : does not try.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Frisch gewagt, ist halb gewonnen".

entries.english: (One who confesses) "The case has gone against me" (I am guilty) : is more welcome than tasty food.

entries.luganda: "Gwa ntendewala" : 1) nga w'ayunja wagazi; 2) nga yazimba Bukoba mu ma- tooke amangi.
entries.english: (If they say of somebody) "He is a generous host" (who prepares more food for his visitors than they can manage) : 1) then the place where he can cut down banana-bunches, is big; 2) then he lives in Bukoba (Nnaggalama district), where there is plenty of food.

entries.luganda: Gwe bakwatira mu kituli : nga ye mubbi.
entries.english: The one they catch in the hole (digging into a house) : is the thief (i.e.
entries.meaning: caught red-handed, in the act).

entries.luganda: Gwe batakigambye : 1) gwe kitalumya mutwe ; 2) y'agamba nti atadde ebiga- mbo.
entries.english: One whom they have not talked about (in an evil way) : 1) does not get a headache from it; 2) says: Oh, he only talks nonsense (if they had talked about himself, he would take it seriously).
He whom they did not manage to catch : will not fail to plead "not guilty".

entries.luganda: Gwe battira nnyina, si gwe bamuliyira : Lubya baamuliyira emituba.
entries.english: A man whose mother they have killed, is not the one to whom they pay damages : they cut the forest on the Lubya-river (Busiro) and made up for it by planting mituba-trees.

entries.luganda: Gwe batuma okuwera engalabi : tamala kuzina n'alyoka awera ngalabi.
entries.english: The man they send to prevent (stop) a dance to the ngalabi-drum : should not, first dance (with them) and then stop it.

entries.luganda: Gwe baayogeddeko kambe kaawaase : tekaggwa masanda.
entries.english: One who has been the object of slander is like a knife that has been peeling matooke : the sap (latex) remains on.
entries.meaning: Any subsequent bad talk is readily believed. Germ. "Etwas bleibt immer hangen".

entries.luganda: Gwe kitaliiridde nnyina : nti linda bukye (= nti ka bukye).
entries.english: He whose mother has not been taken by the wild animal : (can say) "Wait till morning (before going after the animal)".
entries.meaning: People often do not sympathise with the misfortune of others.

entries.luganda: Gwe nnywedde : gukwata engo mu mannyo.
entries.english: The beer I have drunk : gets hold of the leopard by its teeth.
entries.meaning: Drunkenness causes recklessness; danger unperceived.

entries.luganda: Gwe wabbanga naye : bw'asula emiryango teweebaka.
entries.english: If the man with whom you have been stealing sleeps in your "ddiiro", you keep awake (you do not trust him).
Is it not work (cooking) you have come here for?
entries.meaning: So says the husband to his wife who refuses to cook in the morning. Compare the two verbs: "kufumba" means "to cook" and "kufumbirwa" means "to marry (of a woman)".

entries.luganda: Gwe watumanga : ng'agenda mbiro; naye bw'olaba yekkaanya, ng'agenda ku- senguka.
entries.english: If you (as master) send somebody on an errand : he will go quickly; but if he hesitates, he is thinking of leaving you.

entries.luganda: Gwe weeyigira : gwe gukussa (= gukukubya); ejjenje lifa bulanzi.
entries.english: The work you have learnt : will kill you; the cricket dies by prophesying.
entries.meaning: The cricket cries at night and attracts children who catch it and eat it. - A victim of one's own work (trade, vocation).

entries.luganda: Gwe zisanga azigumira : ejjanzi terigenda na nzige.
entries.english: He who meets trouble, has to bear it : the cricket does not travel with the locusts.
entries.meaning: Each one has his own cross to carry, which no one can take from him.

entries.english: Do you cheat the one from whose food (matooke) you eat?
entries.meaning: Reproach for one who does not give his dues to the chief; lazy tenants etc.

entries.english: The man you despise : will be your friend one day (when you are in need).
entries.meaning: French "Ne jamais dire: Fontaine, je ne boirai pas de ton eau".

entries.english: A game which you leave (first) to the children : later interests you too (and you play it yourself).
entries.meaning: Or: A game you leave to the children (without interfering) : is enjoyed by them.

entries.english: He whose toe you heal : will make it kick you.
entries.meaning: Dutch "Ondank is s'wereld's loon". Germ. "Undank ist der Welt Lohn".

entries.english: One whom you show through your bananary : will take a piece of it.
entries.meaning: Don't make people covetous with your possessions.

entries.english: The man whose moral welfare you worry about : worries about your headache.
entries.meaning: He does not want to understand your worries.

entries.english: The one whose death you conjecture (predict) : is not the one it kills.
entries.meaning: Somebody else might die long before, who you did not expect would die.

entries.english: The man whose skill in throwing a spear is known : you don't wait till he brandishes it (at you).
entries.meaning: Do not expose yourself to unnecessary danger!

entries.luganda: Gw'omenyera mu nkejje : ewuwe alya luti.
entries.english: He to whom you give half an enkejje (small lake fish) : at home eats a whole twig-full.
entries.meaning: He whom you consider a poor hungry fellow and whom you treat as a beggar, might be an important and well-to-do fellow. Underestimating people! - The enkejje are strung together on a twig and roasted.

entries.english: A fire at which you intend to warm yourself : do not let its coals burn out.
entries.meaning: Use your chances! Grasp your opportunity! "Ekiro kijja omuntu ky'atayinza kukoleramu" (Yo.9 .4).

entries.luganda: Gw'onyoomera mu kkubo : eka we nga mugagga.
entries.english: The one you despise on the road : is a rich man at home (perhaps).
entries.meaning: French "Ne jugeons pas les Bens sur la mine!" Germ. "Schein triigt". "Stille Wasser griInden tier Gram.47, M.340.

entries.english: The one on whom you inflict a heavy fine (for the first time) : will not raise the alarm, if he is a blood-brother.
entries.meaning: Blood brothers are supposed to be merciful and just.

entries.luganda: Gw'oteeresezza mu mboozi, gw'owasa : nga mukyayogera bulungi.
entries.english: The one whom you don't leave out of your conversation is the one you will marry : provided that you talk well about her.
Do not reprimand a child that is not yours.
If you have not yet made your body reach old age : don't call it yours.
entries.meaning: Germ. "Heute rot, morgen tot".

entries.luganda: Gw'otoyise (= otayise) naye : si muzibu kulimba.
entries.english: It is not difficult to tell lies (about something you have seen) to one who has not been with you.

entries.luganda: Gw'otozinanga naye : bw'asituka okuzina nga ggwe otuula.
entries.english: If there is one with whom you never have as yet danced : remain sitting, when he gets up for a dance.
entries.meaning: He might hurt you (step on your toes). - Be careful with people you don't know. Thoughtless familiarity.

entries.luganda: Gw'oyagala : omusalira omusango n'omuweerera ebintu by'okuliwa.
entries.english: If you really love somebody (who has transgressed the law) : you condemn him and you supply him with the where-with-all to pay the fine.
entries.meaning: Justice and mercy! No perverse judgement!

entries.english: He whom you teach to cultivate : does not give you anything of what he grows in abundance.
entries.meaning: French "La reconnaissance n'est pas de ce monde".

entries.english: He to whom you teach the mweso-game : beats you with sixteen (in the "ssa").
entries.meaning: The pupil often beats (becomes greater than) the master.

entries.english: He whom you call in a friendly way : answers you offensively.
Where he comes from, the home is burning : and where he goes to, it is burning.
entries.meaning: No place to go to. Engl. "To fall between two stools". "To fall between the devil and the deep blue sea".

entries.luganda: Gye babutta : gye bweyuna; ettooke eddene mu ggwaatiro.
entries.english: Where they kill the animals : there they go again; like the big banana (that grows) on the peeling place.

entries.luganda: Gye banzaalira mmanyiyo : ng'alina mukadde we amubuulirayo.
entries.english: I know the place where I was born : (says one) who has been told by his mother.
entries.meaning: He could not know, unless he had been told.

entries.english: (eŋŋoma) (also: Gye zireegerwa - - ) The drums are not beaten where they are made.
entries.meaning: Or: The drums do not sound now, as when they were made. Often used in bargaining, to diminish the price.

entries.luganda: Gye biva tibirirema kuddayo : gw'okwata ku nkoona, naye akukwata ku nkoo- na.
entries.english: Where things come from, there they will go again : one whom you try to help (by getting hold of the back of the head - as one does with a slow walking child), will get hold of your head one day.
entries.meaning: The parents become children again. - Mutual help.

entries.english: (or: Bwe bakugoba gye bakuzza.) Where you put a thorn-trap : there they put you, when you are in trouble.
entries.meaning: Engl. "Harm set, harm get". Germ. "Wer andern eine Grube grabt, Mit selbst hinein". Dutch "Wie een kuil graaft voor een ander, valt er self in".

entries.english: Where you do not live (where you have nothing to say) : don't divide the bowls.
entries.meaning: Do not interfere with other people's business.

entries.english: Where (to whom) you give the loan of an axe : do not put your ears.
entries.meaning: If one has entrusted his child to somebody else's care - also in marriage - he should not unduly inquire about the treatment she gets there, otherwise trouble will result from it.

entries.luganda: Jjembe ddulumi : olikwasa omwana n'akuba wansi.
entries.english: (or: Ejjembe eddulumi - - ) Give a haunting charm to a child and it throws it away (to the ground).
entries.meaning: The child has no idea about its hidden powers.

entries.english: The king's power reaches far.
entries.meaning: The power of the old kings was unlimited with regard to life and property.

entries.english: A king is more than relationship.
entries.meaning: He has the power to pardon one who has been brought to him to be killed and can even make him a chief.

entries.luganda: Kabaka akussa owuwo : essanja libabula endagala (sso nga ba luganda).
entries.english: The king makes you kill your own son (and you cannot refuse) : (just as) the dry banana-leaf singes the green one (although they are of the same stock).
entries.meaning: The green banana-leaves are made pliable by singeing them over a quick flame of "ssanja".

entries.luganda: Kabaka muzaawula : nga wa malibu asanze we bafumba emyungu (= we balya ekibumba).
entries.english: The king is a great finder (of lost persons or things) : like a toothless fellow who finds people who are just cooking vegetable marrow (or: who are eating liver) (soft food for his toothless mouth).
entries.meaning: On the occasion of the many wars in olden times the warriors got about and found again long-lost friends and relations. The king who started the war, is given credit for that.

entries.luganda: Kabaka nnamunswa : alya ku nswa ze.
entries.english: The king is like the queen-ant : she lives on her flying ants.
entries.meaning: The ruler has a right to get his requirements from his subjects.

entries.english: The king is like the lake : which also kills one who does not fish.
entries.meaning: Nobody is safe. He gets musolo from rich and poor. Otherwise the musolo would be paid by the rich only.

entries.english: A king is like a lake : unfathomable.
A king is like a hammer (or thunderbolt) : it kills by its very weight.
A new king drives away the old one.
entries.meaning: Old people (things, customs) have to give way to young (new) ones.

entries.luganda: Kabaka tamanyi birungi : singa ekitoogo ky'afuusa olunyago.
entries.english: The king seems not to know what is really good (useful) : otherwise he would use papyrus for making spearshafts.
entries.meaning: It is long, smooth, no branches etc. Sauciness, pertness!

entries.english: The king is not like fire, where you can warm yourself.
entries.meaning: In olden times when anybody could be killed by the king, a mukopi kept aloof from the lubiri.

entries.english: The king does not find you, where he left you.
entries.meaning: In course of time you change (age, position, place etc.).

entries.english: "Spread all over the sky" (proper name) : as (one who has a) thick hairy growth all over his chest.
entries.meaning: Said about a fellow who overpowers others with his loud and monopolizing conversation; or of a quarrelsome person.

entries.english: "An interfering person" (proper name) : does not allow the locusts to settle down.
entries.meaning: He won't catch them. - A hasty man does not let you explain.

entries.english: (He who acts according to the principle) "Let them praise me" : is left with his arteries only.
entries.meaning: He gets thin from poverty. He squanders things.

entries.luganda: Kabbo ka muwala : kajja kajjudde, kaddayo kajjudde (ng'alina essimba).
entries.english: The little basket of a girl : is full, when she comes and is full, when she goes (provided that she is trustworthy).
entries.meaning: Especially applied to a married woman, visiting her parents. She brings presents and receives them.

entries.english: If there had been a trap-hole (outside our doorstep - dug by our enemies) : it would have finished us.
entries.meaning: "A close shave"; we have escaped the danger.

entries.english: An undaunted (courageous) fellow conquers his fellow men.
The little wild pig sets off the trap which catches the old pigs (by roaming about among the potatoes where the trigger is).
entries.meaning: Young reckless people often bring harm to the whole community.

entries.luganda: Kabuga ente : ensimbi a1ina emu (nti ente egwe).
entries.english: He who presses for the cow to be killed : has only one cent (saying: let the cow die, that we can eat, we have plenty of money).
entries.meaning: Although he cannot buy much, he wants the cow to be killed quickly. - Even a weakling can incite a big struggle (war) and keep himself out of it.

entries.english: A tough thing : like the neck of a lazy man.
entries.meaning: He plants no food for himself, but goes to work for food (kusaka). Therefore he has to carry firewood or water etc. and brings potatoes etc. home.

entries.english: One who has no place of refuge : like a slave-woman.
An elusive person (there is no way of catching her) : like an unmarried woman who went out to cut saltgrass.
entries.meaning: They say at home: she went to cut saltgrass; although she might have gone visiting. They don't rely on her coming back.

entries.luganda: Kabula we kalaga : bakatema ngalo (or lunwe).
entries.english: (kasajja) If the little man cannot point to anybody (who is ready to witness his state-ment) : they cut off his finger.
entries.meaning: If the witness, you claim to have, is not there, you lose the case.

entries.luganda: Kaabulindiridde : ng'ekinnya ekiri mu mulyango ; bwe kitayasa nsuwa, kime-nya kugulu.
entries.english: A threatening (unavoidable) evil : like a hole at the entrance; if it does not smash the water pot (in falling), it breaks your leg.

entries.luganda: Kaabulindiridde : ng'enkonge y'oku kkubo; bw'etekukuba magenda, ekukuba amadda.
entries.english: An unavoidable evil : like a stump in the path; if it does not catch your toes when going, it will catch them when coming.

entries.luganda: Kaabulindiridde : ng'omusanvu oguli ku nju; bwe gutakuba nnyinimu, ne gugi-ggala.
entries.english: An unavoidable evil : like branches (of fire wood) lying at the side of the house; if they don't trip the owner of the house, they block the entrance.
A thieving dog : makes its back tough (cultivates a thick skin).
entries.meaning: Because it frequently gets a thrashing. Perseverance and strength.

entries.luganda: Kaafuma : ng'ensawo ey'ekiwero; bw'egwa mu mugga, towonya kantu, byonna bitobera ddala.
entries.english: Spoiled : like a cloth-bag; when it falls into the river, you won't save anything, all will be wet through.
entries.meaning: Formerly they had leather-bags. Ye mukazi aloopa bba. The wife has always something to complain about: Bbaze ankola bw'ati - - .

entries.luganda: Kafumu ka muwunda : kafumitira eruuyi n'eruuyi.
entries.english: A spear with an iron spike on the other end : stabs either way.
entries.meaning: Said of a man who is considered as a friend of the husband and maintains at the same time illicit relations with the wife (of the husband).

entries.english: What goes away still eating : does not see trouble.
entries.meaning: If a man is sent away from his kibanja and is still healthy (strong), he can get another kibanja. - Not all hope lost.

entries.english: That is final : as with the old man who has become a widower (or: has grown thin).
entries.meaning: He cannot marry again (or: get fat again).

entries.english: "The toe has brought me luck" : (so you say) where you find them eating.
entries.meaning: The toe has led me to a welcome meal.

entries.luganda: Kaggwa ensonyi :-1) ng'omwana abba nnyina (= kitaawe); 2) ng'omukazi awoza ne bba; 3) ng'alya ne mulamu we enswa.
entries.english: A shameless individual : 1) a child who steals from his own mother (or father); 2) like a wife who takes her husband to court; 3) like one who eats flying ants with her brother-in-law (his sister-in-law).

entries.luganda: Kaggwa ka ttovu : kasonsomolera ne gye katafumise.
entries.english: The thorn of the tree-thistle affects the body even where it has not actually stung.
entries.meaning: Applications: 1) A calamity befalling a certain part of the population can have adverse effects also on other parts (e.g. famine, strike etc.). 2) Also used for evil effects of sexual excesses.

entries.luganda: Kagubiiru : nga mutwe gw'omusasi (= ng'ensikya y'omunafu); gugenda gwetisse, ate gudda gwetisse (= gugendera mu nku ne guddira mu matooke).
entries.english: Strong and sturdy : like the head of a musasi working for food (or: like the neck of a lazy fellow); going it carries (firewood) and coming it carries (matoo- ke).
A person giving away his dignity : like a woman eating with the slaves.
The food of a (rich) farmer : is like a bone in the throat.
entries.meaning: You have to vomit it up forcibly. The farmers don't like to share their food. They quarrel, whether you eat much or little.

entries.english: The sorrel (plant) smarts on a sore.
entries.meaning: Used, when one encounters resistance or a rebellious spirit.

entries.luganda: Kakande ka nnyoko : kakira olwa kitaawo olubikke.
entries.english: The uncultivated bananary of your mother : is better (for you) than the well covered (with ssanja) of your father.
entries.meaning: You get more out of the former. The mother always helps her married children.

entries.english: The little "nkejje" (fish) is ever present at a feast.
entries.meaning: Said of any important item or happening at a feast (marriage, lumbe etc.).

entries.luganda: Kakowekowe kanda : katemereza ne we kataalye.
entries.english: The eye-lash is a queer (difficult) thing : it blinks where it will not eat.
entries.meaning: Said of somebody who looks upon a petitioner, but does not give.

entries.luganda: Kakoloboto Kabaka yamutuma okuwera ekisiibo : n'ate n'alya.
entries.english: The king sent Kakoloboto to proclaim a fast : yet he ate himself.
entries.meaning: Not observing oneself, what one preaches to others.

entries.english: Your offensive speech (kamwa) has entangled you in a court case (mutango) : as when one quarrels with a woman who suckles her child.
entries.meaning: That is considered equal to bulogo (bewitching).

entries.english: (kalagala) What is still undeveloped (banana-leaf) : let it become a luwombo (banana-leaf made limp over a flame, to have meat etc.
The one who discovers the bees (in a tree etc.) : brings the fire (to rob them of the honey).
entries.meaning: Engl. "First come, first served". Germ. "Wer zuerst kommt, mahlt zuerst".

entries.english: (or: Kalagaane : tikaggya buliika.) A promised thing : does not come by force (extortion).
entries.meaning: One should be faithful to his promises.

entries.luganda: Kalema ka nsinjo : ekyuma kitema kinnaakyo.
entries.english: Kalema is like a cold chisel : one iron cuts the other.
entries.meaning: King Kalema shot his brother Kiweewa dead and burnt his corpse (in 1888).

entries.english: There it went up (into the air, thin and high) : like the thin column of smoke from the camp of the warriors.
entries.meaning: Rub.C.1376. 2098 Kaliba akabiri : 1) ngule emmamba ey'omutwe?; 2) omusibe tayita Jjimbo. (cf. Sserwali lundi: 4977) If that happens a second time : 1) do you think that I shall again buy a lungfish with only a head? (I have been warned by my first experience). It will not happen a second time : 2) that the prisoner passes the road to Jjimbo (in fetters). Used for: "I shall not stand bail for him a second time; I have lost my money the first time".

entries.luganda: "Kaliba kaki akalikugwa ku liiso?" : ng'omunaku ayombye n'omwana wa boo- wo.
entries.english: "What can it be that will fall upon your eye?" : so a poor fellow says when he has quarreled with a noble one.
entries.meaning: He wishes evil only, as he cannot do him harm otherwise.

entries.luganda: Kakulu takulirwa : ekyuma tikikulira jjinja (= ennyondo tekulira jjinja).
entries.english: Age comes first (is not overruled) : the iron is not older than the stone (or: the hammer is not older than the stone).
entries.meaning: The iron was melted from stones. - The child is not more than his father.

entries.luganda: Kalifa aleka kalifa : ekiteme okulekawo ensukusa.
entries.english: What is doomed to die, leaves what will also die : the cut-down banana-stem leaves the banana-shoot.
entries.meaning: The shoot will also be cut down one day. "Mine today and yours tomorrow" (Ecclus.38.22).

entries.luganda: Kalimi ka mwewoze : kaweweera majja (= kajja kawewedde).
entries.english: The tongue of a borrower : is smooth when he comes to borrow (but harsh, when you go to claim your money).

entries.luganda: Kalimi ka mwewozi : kwegonza; kajja ne "sembera, nkubuuze".
entries.english: The tongue of a borrower : is smoothness; it starts with "come nearer, I want to greet you".
The tongue is white (clean, harmless).
entries.meaning: Said of a hypocrite, who has smooth words, but murderous thoughts.

entries.luganda: Kalifa abiri : olonda ejjinja nga kalaba.
entries.english: (akanyonyi) A little bird has two eyes : it sees, when you look for a stone (and flies away).
entries.meaning: A watchful person can escape many a danger.

entries.english: A double-tongued fellow : just like a favourite who accuses and excuses (at the same time).
entries.meaning: He tries to court favour with both, the chief and the culprit.

entries.english: The whole lot : that is what the leper holds up, when he wants to show the (number of) days.
entries.meaning: As his fingers are eaten away, he can only show his stumps.

entries.english: A mix-up (confusion) : like the plot of a.
entries.meaning: poor man. There everything is to be found: beans, maize, monkey-nuts, vegetables etc.

entries.luganda: Kalulwe : 1) nnantaliirwa mu nnyama; 2) tabula ku nnyama; omumyuka tabula ku mwami.
entries.english: The gall-bladder : 1) is not eaten with the meat (harmful things must be elimi- nated); 2) is not missing, when an animal is killed; just as the second in com- mand is not missing, where there is a chief.
entries.meaning: Useful things and superfluous or less useful things are always connected with each other.

entries.english: He eats (drinks) twice : like the belly of a lubaale-priest.
entries.meaning: What the musamize eats, whilst being possessed, he does not seem to remember; because later he asks for food (meat) or drink (beer) again. Other explanation: he eats both, ordinary food and fire. A double personality!

entries.english: A double-dealer (two-faced person) : like the mouth of a mmandwa (possessed by a lubaale).
entries.meaning: He gives the same advice to the man who comes for help to him against an enemy, as he gives to the enemy himself (and gets double pay of course).

entries.luganda: Kalya buguga : ng'ow'obusa atatereka bugenyi; nti baganda bo bwe balijja, oli- bafumbira ki?
entries.english: A person who eats up everything he has : like a bachelor who does not put away anything for visitors; (they tell him) "If your relations come on a visit, what will you cook for them?" Rub.C.925.
The (little) man who eats by himself : praises himself for eating slowly.
entries.meaning: There is nobody who contends with him. He has all the food to himself.

entries.luganda: Ka maanyi - kaliibwa na mbiro (= na ngabo).
entries.english: A difficult thing is achieved by tackling it quickly and courageously.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Audaces fortuna adiuvat" (Virgil). Engl. "Where there's a will, there's a way". - Germ. "Frisch gewagt ist halb gewonnen".

entries.luganda: Kaami katono : okanyoomera (= okagayira) mitala wa mugga.
entries.english: A small chief : you despise him, if he is living (ruling) on the other side of the river.
entries.meaning: But you have to respect him, if he is your chief.

entries.english: A person eating to the bursting point (inflicting evil on himself) : is like money that buys "maduudu".
entries.meaning: Maduudu are the seeds of a poisonous plant (Datura Stramonium), used in ordeals.

entries.luganda: Kamukago : okalya dda, kadda dda; ejjobyo liddira mu mutwe.
entries.english: That little coffee-bean (kamwanyi) of the bloodbrother-pact : you ate it long ago and it has its results in the far future; like the jjobyo-plant (a vegetable "Pentaphylla") which produces its white flowers on the head.
entries.meaning: The white jjobyo-flowers symbolize old age in Luganda speech. - The blood- brother-pact imposes its mutual obligations till death and beyond it (children of the bloodbrothers!).

entries.english: (akati) One little twig with another : makes a bundle.
entries.meaning: Engl. "Many a mickle makes a muckle". "Take care of the pence and the pounds will take care of themselves". "A penny saved is a penny earned". Lat. "Gutta cavat lapidem, non vi, sed saepe cadendo". Germ. "Wer den Kreuzer nicht ehrt, ist des Guldens nicht wert".

entries.luganda: Kaamukuulo : embuzi ennume erya olw'eggulo, ng'eraba enjuba egwa ng'efu- ndikiriza.
entries.english: (Trying to devour) all at the same time : like a he-goat eating in the evening, when he sees the sun going down ending the chances of eating more.
(Disappearing) all at the same time : like a field full of maize.
entries.meaning: As a rule all the maize is rooted out at the same time. - They say: "gundi alya kaamukuulo".

entries.english: "The (small) reed has cut me" (you say) : because you have stripped it of its fibre.
entries.meaning: If you have brought trouble upon yourself, you should not blame others.

entries.english: (also: Nze kamunye, nze nnamukwakkula.) The brown kite (hawk) is a robber (grabber).
entries.meaning: Said as a reproach to children for grabbing the food.

entries.english: The forceful brown kite makes the owner (of fowl etc.) raise the alarm (when it robs him of his hens).

entries.luganda: Kamunye w'agwa : 1) tewabula luyoogaano; 2) we waba olugambo.
entries.english: Where the brown hawk swoops down : 1) there is no lack of noise (raising the alarm); 2) there is a peg (a skin spread out for drying).
One who moves from place to place (an unsteady person) : is like the engalabi drum in the season of plenty.
entries.meaning: The engalabi drum is carried from place to place, hanging on a long string from the shoulder.

entries.luganda: Kamwa kabi : katta Siroganga (= kassa Siroganga).
entries.english: An angry word killed Siroganga.
entries.meaning: A fellow who was unjustly accused of practising witchcraft; in anger he replied: "oba nnamutta ne mmuta". On this he was condemned to death by fire. Dying he exclaimed "siroganga" (= I do not practise witchcraft). - Engl. "Give a dog a bad name and hang him!" - One who talks pessimistically about the fate of others (in sickness, in danger etc.) is later accused of having caused the evil (bulogo).

entries.english: "My mouth made a slip" (= I have said too much) : so says one who quarrels with his neighbour (thereby trying to amend and to make peace again).
(The woman who says) "The razor shaves like a big grass-fire" : makes you shave her head.
entries.meaning: The suspicious and jealous husband comes. home, sees it and gets you into trouble on account of it. - Flattery of women!

entries.luganda: Kamwenyumwenyu : embwa k'eseka mu lumbe lw'ente.
entries.english: A smile : as the dog smiles at the death of a cow.
entries.meaning: Pretence of grief which the heir shows at a rich man's funeral, is compared here with the grin of a dog at the slaughtering of a cow.

entries.english: (or: Akako tikasingika.) (cf.
entries.meaning: Katono ko: 2205) What belongs to you : is unsurpassable. "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush". Germ. "Ein Sperling in der Hand ist besser als eine Taube auf dem Dache".

entries.luganda: Kanaakuloopa : bw'okawa (= olumuwa) omwenge, kafuka ku mpagi.
entries.english: A fellow who wants to denounce you : when you give him beer to drink, pours it out on the pole (in the house) (to have proof against you (from the smell of beer) that you are brewing (selling) beer).
A perplexing situation for you : if one gives you water (to drink) and leaves the gourd in your hands.
entries.meaning: You may not put it down on the ground and you do not know where else to put it.

entries.luganda: Kanaaluzaalu : ng'omuwuulu amulisa ku mmere, y'azuula ekkovu.
entries.english: A trouble-maker : like the young man who examines the food with a torch and finds a snail on it.
entries.meaning: The husband of the cook (wife) will abuse or beat his wife.

entries.english: "Let me go and see the heir" : (so says one, when he goes to the feast of kwa- bya olumbe) when he eats there, his wife will have twins.

entries.luganda: "Ka nduve (= ka nguve) ku ntono" : ng'ow'ekibuga asanze (= ng'omuyala atuuse) we bafumba.
entries.english: (olugendo or omulimu) "Let me stop a while on my journey (or: from my business)" : says the towns- man (or: hungry fellow) arriving where they are cooking.
entries.meaning: He wants to rest (talk), till they invite him for a meal.

entries.english: "Let me eat and finish everything (of my property)" : (one saying so) forgets death (which might come, before he has finished - or might leave him in poverty).

entries.luganda: Ka nnananyi : mubbi tagenda na ndege.
entries.english: Let me keep quiet (sirina googera) : a thief does not walk with anklebells.
entries.meaning: If he did, he would have not much chance to steal.

entries.english: One who can say "that is mine" is better off than one who says "that is ours".
Let me take your thorns out.
entries.meaning: Retort of one who has been accused in court and has been told all his sins by his accuser (who has not mentioned one of his own faults).

entries.luganda: "Ka nkugweko ekiyilfuyiifu" : omugole ky'agwa ku nkyakya.
entries.english: "Let me help you with great fervour" : as a young wife washes the feet of her husband (cracks on the side of the feet).
"Let me turn to you" (let me pay full attention to you) : as the child turns to the one who nurses it.
"Let me crush you" : as one with protruding teeth crushes the maize (cob).
entries.meaning: Angry threat! One with such teeth manages the maize corn more strongly and quickly.

entries.luganda: Ka nkwetegule : ejjanzi lyetegula mukazi muzadde.
entries.english: Let me get away from you : as the grass-hopper gets away from a mother (who wants to get hold of it as a plaything for the child).
Nails (on the fingers) : that is what the Muyima uses to pick his nose.

entries.luganda: Kannantebya : 1) ng'omubbi w'omunju; okumala okubba ate ne yeetaakiriza; 2) ng'omulubaale ow'okumpi; kye yawulidde enkya, ky'alagula eggulo.
entries.english: A deceptive person (a "fraud") : 1) like a thief in one's own household; who steals and then emphatically repudiates any suspicion falling on him; 2) like a lubaale-priest living nearby; what he has heard in the morning, he prophesies (as his supernatural knowledge) in the evening.
"Let me cut the difficult knot" : as the wizard cut it at Bubiro (Kyaggwe).
entries.meaning: The said wizard had been accused of having poisoned the son of the chief at Bubiro, and was ordered to drink poison to prove his innocence (ordeal). Instead of drinking it, he jumped into the lake and was drowned. - Engl. "To cut the Gordian knot".

entries.english: A small case (dispute, offence) is settled privately : you pull out the (spiky seeds of) "kafumita-bagenge" on the spot they have stung you.
entries.meaning: Don't make a mountain out of a mole-hill.

entries.luganda: Kanyinyiggi : omukazi omunafu k'akaaba mu lumbe.
entries.english: Shedding bitter tears without end : just as a lazy woman does in mourning (she prefers that to hoeing in the field).
"Let me get my shoulder out of this (i.e.
entries.meaning: I disappear)" : as Lukoda of the Baluubu said (when he died). Lukoda was an old ssiga-chief at Luubu - Mawokota. Clan of the enjovu.

entries.english: Where there is no cat : the mouse feels itself a guest.
entries.meaning: Engl. "When the cat's away : the mice will play".

entries.english: A "spot of sun" : even one who has nothing to dry, likes to see a little sunshine (during the rainy season).
What the "firewood-gatherer" (insect) collects : burns him.
entries.meaning: When the grass-fire comes, the little bundle on his back catches fire and kills him. Self-inflicted evil.

entries.luganda: Kasobeza nga kutu : tikunywa taaba ne kumala kuleeta ebifeetete.
entries.english: A strange thing, the ear : it does not smoke tobacco, and still produces juice (ear-wax).

entries.luganda: Kasobeza ng'enneebaza y'omwavu : ajja akaaba bw'omuwa, nti "onnanze ki ssebo?" (cf.
entries.english: Omwavu taweeka: 4470) A puzzling thing, like the thanksgiving of a poor man : he comes lamenting, and when you give him something, he says (crying again) "What have you given me, ssebo?" 32.23.
A strange thing like a thief stealing in his own household.

entries.luganda: Kasobeza ng'ow'ekiwalaata : atudde mu mulyango nga balya; ogamba nti "mpozzi atunula eno", kazzi atunula mu nju gye balya.
entries.english: A strange (funny) sight : like one with a bald head, sitting in the doorway, whilst they are eating (inside); you might say: "Perhaps he is looking here (into the open)", perhaps he is looking into the house (where they are eating).
The little eye of a cock : sees also at night.
entries.meaning: He sees the day-break (he crows), when nobody else sees it. - Said of shrewd people.

entries.luganda: Kasookedde obirya (= kasooka mbirya) : leero toobisobole.
entries.english: (For quite a time) you have been taking things (you are cheating me) : but today you shall have no success.
(That cob of) maize will make us quarrel.
entries.meaning: If the woman gives it to a young unmarried man, her suspicious husband might say this or think it.

entries.luganda: Kasooli w'e Ggomba : aliibwa na mbiro.
entries.english: The maize of Ggomba (ssaza) : is eaten in a hurry (by the warriors).
A treacherous thing : like the killing of a one-eyed person.
entries.meaning: He has only one eye to see the tricks of the aggressor.

entries.english: One who does not despise himself (who thinks a lot of himself) : attacks his fellow-men (or: alienates the wives of his fellow-men).
An individual who does.
entries.meaning: not kill his own cow (but wants to eat the meat of other people's cows) : will die claiming (trying to reserve for himself) a piece. Selfishness and its punishment. Duta 517, M.383. 2193 Kateeyamba : ng'abaavu abayita ababiri. A helpless thing : just as when two paupers walk together. Neither can help the other.

entries.english: The animal that does not (try to) free itself (from the trap) : will die.
entries.meaning: Man must try, with his own power, to overcome difficulties. "Struggle for life". Germ. "Kampf ums Dasein".

entries.english: (The animal) that does not bring forth, does not multiply.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Bonum est diffusivum sui".

entries.luganda: Katiko ka mukyala : okakuba nnoga, nako kakukuba nvuba.
entries.english: The mushroom-sauce which a married woman has prepared for you : you dip your matooke-morsel into it, and that sauce will dip you (put you) into the stocks.
entries.meaning: The husband noticing the favour which his wife has given to a visitor, gets suspicious and gets the favourite into court and jail.

entries.english: When the little tree (which you are about to cut down says) "You have found me" : don't cut it with your axe!
entries.meaning: The spirit in the tree says: "Don't cut me down, this is my tree!" - Some trees were supposed to be inhabited by spirits and could not be cut down.

entries.english: "God will have had his special purpose" (in letting a certain person die) : (so you say) if he has not killed your own (father, child etc.).
God gives you flying ants : and you drum them back?
entries.meaning: Not being ready with a covering for the anthill, one tries to keep the ants in by drumming on the anthill. - Seemingly not appreciating God's gifts.

entries.english: A would-be little chief : (is one who), as a peasant, makes an enclosure for him- self.

entries.luganda: Katono keewaza : kakira eddene eddwadde (= erinafu).
entries.english: A small thing that is thriving : is better than a big thing that is ailing.
entries.meaning: Engl. "A healthy ass is worth more than a sick horse".

entries.luganda: Katono ko (= akako) : kakira eddene erya munno.
entries.english: Something small that is yours : is better than something big that belongs to your neighbour.

entries.luganda: Katula keebisse buka : naye mu mwoyo ng'ayogeza ekisa.
entries.english: The little "ntula" (edible fruit) covers itself with bitterness : but inside he speaks with kindness.
entries.meaning: "Katula" is a proper name. Said of people with rough manners and a kind heart. - Ntula are very tasty; but when gathering them, people carefully remove the sepals, as they (with the leaves) cause a choking sensation in the throat. "A sort of diamond in the rough!" Duta 1134, M.390, Gram.353.

entries.english: (ettooke) "Let us listen" : (one who says so) spoils the ttooke which is in your mouth.
entries.meaning: He who tries to make you speak, prevents you from chewing. Also applied to being disturbed in other occupations.

entries.english: The same attraction : like salt that is put on the potatoes.
entries.meaning: Salt is savoury by itself and potatoes are tasty. It is difficult to choose between two good things.

entries.english: The little head of the dog is troublesome (annoying) in the door-ways.
entries.meaning: Said of people who visit overmuch.

entries.luganda: Kawuulu kagezi : kagenda okunywa ogw'obusogozi, nga kamaze okweyalira.
entries.english: A wise little bachelor : goes to drink freshly brewed beer only after having spread his bed properly.
entries.meaning: For a married man this would be done by his wife; but a bachelor has nobody to do it for him, if he comes home drunk.

entries.english: The plague goes away : and you beat the snakes?
entries.meaning: Snakes were supposed to be connected with plague; beating makes them angry and the plague comes back.

entries.english: Swiftly : like one with a shield (a warrior) running through the plantation.
entries.meaning: Said of a man who is rushing to and fro. - 'Engabo enkedi' is a shield without buckle.

entries.english: As soon as you mention the name of a wild cat (you have spotted), it runs away into the bush.
entries.meaning: As soon as some people get a name and promise to be useful, they give up their work. - Also said of a thief who runs away, as soon as he hears: Omubbi wuuyo!

entries.english: The "small butter-bean" has made the ordinary bean tasteless.
entries.meaning: When one finds better food, better comforts, better people etc., one loses inter-est in the old things. Germ. "Das Bessere ist der Feind des Guten".

entries.english: Passing each other : like the spittle and the Adam's-apple.
entries.meaning: The spittle goes down and the Adam's-apple goes up.

entries.english: (also: Kuyita pirya - - ) Hurrying uselessly : like an unmarried woman chasing a wild cat (which carries away a hen).
entries.meaning: If the woman recovers the hen, she cannot eat it herself (taboo), and she can- not give it to the husband (because she is not married). - Kayita-pirya is a name given to a grown-up girl, roaming about too freely.

entries.english: It is the drum-maker who knows the charm that is inside the drum.
entries.meaning: Each one knows the secrets of his own trade (basawo, emmandwa etc.).

entries.english: What you have worked for (planted) yourself : is more praiseworthy than (what you got by) "Give me also a piece" (begging).
entries.meaning: "Poverty is the reward of idleness".

entries.english: The cow licks her own calf only.
entries.meaning: Everyone looks after his own flesh and blood first. "Every man thinks his own geese swans".

entries.luganda: Keezimbira : tikaba kato; bw'ogenda okukwata akasanke, ogenda osooba.
entries.english: A youngster who builds a house for himself : is by no means small; if you are going to catch a kasanke (small bird) you stoop down.
entries.meaning: Such a young man seems to be able to fend for himself, to pay taxes etc. Even small creatures oftentimes develop remarkable qualities.

entries.luganda: Kibaawo kimala : amaaso g'omulungi galoga enjala (= amaaso g'omuganzi gamala enjala).
entries.english: It is selfevident (its very presence is enough) : the face of a beautiful woman (favourite) makes (a man) forget his hunger.

entries.luganda: Kibaawo kimala : ennyindo y'enkoko kye kyenyi.
entries.english: It is self-sufficient : nose and forehead of the chicken are one (and that is enough for the hen).
It is there (fulfilling its purpose) : like an old barkcloth (scarecrow) that guards the beans in the field.

entries.luganda: Kibaaze : 1) ng'eky'omwanisi wa taaba; 2) ensekere ky'eyita mu kiwalaata.
entries.english: A clearing (a glade) : 1) like the place where one puts out his tobacco to dry; 2) the louse passes it, when crawling over a bald head.

entries.luganda: Kibi kyo : kisinga omulungi owa munno.
entries.english: (kyana) An ugly child of your own : is more to you than a beautiful one belonging to your neighbour.
entries.meaning: Such a mother is at least not a "mugumba".

entries.english: (ekkubo) Nobody inquires about it : just as with the path to the well (everybody knows it).
What cannot be sold (on the market) : goes back to its owner.
The banana thrives only on cultivated ground.
entries.meaning: French "Rien sans peine". Engl. "No pains, no gains": "Success means 2 % inspiration and 98 % perspiration".

entries.english: (also: Ekifa - ) A thing of no purpose : as when the rain falls, where the herdsmen live (they don't cultivate there).
(also: Ekifa - - ) What dies in the sun (heat) : revives again in the rain.
entries.meaning: Said about friendship, marriage etc.

entries.english: "My dress will speak for me" : (one thinking so) won't get a chieftainship (or: will be disappointed).
entries.meaning: A dumb suitor won't get his girl. "Faint heart never won fair lady".

entries.english: One who likes his old shield : puts a handle on it.
entries.meaning: Personal attachment to things of long service.

entries.english: (Dried and cooked) bananas : are more helpful than a child.
entries.meaning: If I have a child, I have to feed two; if I have none, only myself. Proverb used in time of famine.

entries.english: The blame fell on the Munyoro : to the satisfaction of the Muga- nda.

entries.luganda: Kigudde mu ndira : ekimonde ekinene mu maaso ga muwuulu.
entries.english: It fell into his hands (claws) : like a big potato in front of a bachelor.
entries.meaning: A welcome feed. Germ. "Ein gefundenes Fressen".

entries.luganda: Kigula engabo kiddawo : ng'eyagigula wa maanyi.
entries.english: What is spent on buying a shield, comes back (pays) : if the buyer is a strong man.
entries.meaning: Otherwise it won't bring much profit.

entries.luganda: Kiguumaaza : ng'ente esula ku kyoto; bw'owulira efuuwa, nti ekuma muliro; obudde okukya osanga vvu jjereere mu kyoto.
entries.english: It is deceiving (a misleading conclusion) : as when the cow lies near the fire place and you hear her blowing, you think she keeps the fire going; but in the morning you find nothing but ashes in the fire place.
entries.meaning: Said of men who pretend to do something, but do nothing.

entries.english: A deceiving thing : like a one-eyed person winking.
entries.meaning: You cannot judge, as only one eye is seeing. Duta 496. 2261a Kigwa mu muliro : ng'embaala (= ng'ekiwojjolo). It falls into the fire : like a flying ant (or: like a butterfly). Said of a silly person, harming himself in his folly.

entries.english: It falls like the mmumbwa (sausage-shaped lump of medicine in clay, hung up in the house) : (they say so of a person) who "knows all about it".
entries.meaning: It escaped him! Germ. "Wes das Herz von ist, des geht der Mund fiber".

entries.english: "In this place gonja should be planted" : (so a man says) if he has been born in Busiro (a country famous for gonja).

entries.luganda: Kigwo kya lwazi : bwe kitakumenya mukono, ne kikwasa omutwe.
entries.english: Wrestling on a rock : if it does not break your arm, it smashes your head.
entries.meaning: You cannot do everything everywhere.

entries.luganda: Kikere : ky'osammuza omuti, oluvannyuma okikwasako ngalo.
entries.english: The frog you drive out (of the house) with a stick : you get hold of finally with the hand (if you dip the nsuwa into the well, and a frog gets in).
entries.meaning: King Mwanga was called "Basammula-ekkere".

entries.english: Better than having no husband : is to be married to a deaf one.

entries.luganda: Kikonyogo : bakikasukira (= bakikanyugira) kulaalira ne kijja n'ekirimba.
entries.english: They throw up the stick even at the risk of its remaining in the tree, and it comes down with a bunch of mpafu.
entries.meaning: Negligible doubts about success and disadvantages should not prevent us from acting. - Also used to minimize a "nobody", when he has won honour abroad.

entries.luganda: Kilcoyo : tekiriisibwa maddu (= bw'okifumbya amaddu tokirya).
entries.english: Dried jjuuni-spinach cannot be eaten voraciously (or: if cooked in a hurry, is unpalatable).
entries.meaning: It creates a choking sensation in the throat.

entries.english: It has put you in a difficult position : as it happened to one single visitor (who could not finish all the food dished up for him).
entries.meaning: Engl. "Too much on one's plate".

entries.english: It is lost to you (no means of remedy) : like the sickness of a hen.
entries.meaning: No medicine was tried, when a hen became sick.

entries.english: An unheard-of thing : as going to the well with a pipe.
entries.meaning: Said of something that "is not done".

entries.english: "How strange (sad)" : (you say) when you see somebody considering it also strange (sad).
What has cooled down : they get hold of with the hands.
entries.meaning: Don't rush things! Kwata mpola!

entries.english: (One who says to the visitor) "The banana-rack will take two (or: four) days to ripen the beer bananas" : is responsible for any offence of the visitor.
entries.meaning: He says to him: "Wait, till the beer is ready".

entries.english: It swallows the soul : as the chicken swallows the red ants.
entries.meaning: To do something at a great risk (at the peril of one's health or life).

entries.luganda: Kimmanje : bwe kita (= okuta), ensuwa nga luggyo.
entries.english: When the kimmanje comes off the water pot, it falls to pieces.
entries.meaning: Kimmanje is a plant, from which they prepare a glue to mend cracked pots. -When the uniting element is missing, human undertakings break down. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered" (Zach.13.7).

entries.luganda: Kimunkumunku : ng'omukira gw'endiga omuliire ku bijanjaalo.
entries.english: An unpalatable combination : like the tail of a sheep, eaten together with beans.

entries.luganda: Kimwa kya mugole : kijja ne "siirye", kimala omuwumbo.
entries.english: That "blessed" mouth of a bride : it comes saying: "I do not eat", and then finishes a whole heap of food.
entries.meaning: The bride leaving the kisenge.

entries.luganda: Kimwa-kitoole : 1) ng'omukazi alya emmamba; 2) ng'omusajja alya ebbumba.
entries.english: An omnivorous person : 1) like a woman who eats lungfish (taboo!); 2) like a man who eats clay.
entries.meaning: Mocking expression to a man whose pregnant wife has a peculiar desire of eating clay (taboo for pregnancy).

entries.english: (The Banyoro said: this time it is not Mannyowenu, who fought us with sticks, but) Kimyanku is the leader (who has spears).
entries.meaning: Now it is serious. Be brave! And they won. - Kimyanku = wood-gatherer; Mannyowenu = strong-jaw.

entries.luganda: Kinaabataya (= kinaabasobeza) : ng'amatooke amatono; bw'ogalya omu, toga-mala; bwe mugalya babiri simukkuta.
entries.english: You will be at a loss what to do : like little matooke; if you eat alone, it is too much for you; if two of you eat, you won't get enough.
A thing that will go wrong : will not enter the head of a fisherman.
entries.meaning: In spite of all the warnings he braves the storm (and goes under).

entries.english: A ferocious animal cannot be fenced in.
entries.meaning: It will break out. - A great evil approaching cannot be prevented.

entries.english: It will burn, when I have swallowed it.
entries.meaning: I shall be sorry for it, when I have done it. - "It is worth a tummy-ache".

entries.luganda: Kinene kya nkukunyi : owanda mu ngalo amalusu n'olyoka okisitula.
entries.english: There seems to be something big about the flea : (because) if you want to lift a big thing, you spit into your hands and then you lift it.
entries.meaning: To catch a flea, people wet their finger with saliva.

entries.english: An old potato plot : still contains some potatoes (if the visitors are welcome; otherwise they won't take the trouble to look for them).

entries.luganda: Kinnya kya mulyango : bw'otokigwamu mafuluma, okigwamu amayingira.
entries.english: A hole in the doorway : if you don't step into it, when coming out (of the house), you step into it, when going in.
entries.meaning: If the kabaka spares one in the morning, he kills him in the evening. - "Kinnya kya mulyango" was the name of kabaka Kayima's house.

entries.english: This is good and that is good.
entries.meaning: A choice is difficult, where the qualities are equal.

entries.english: (kikome) The overcast sky (darkness) has found me with firewood.
entries.meaning: I was prepared for an emergency. - Engl. "A penny for a rainy day".

entries.english: A mess : toothless jaws and fat together.

entries.luganda: Kinyoola mumwa : nga gw'ageya wa kumpi.
entries.english: (kisajja or kikazi) That blessed individual twists the lips : just as when one slanders a person nearby.

entries.luganda: Kirabise ng'Abaseveni bangi bajja kuddayo mu maggye : kubanga amagatto ne kabuuti baabitunda.
entries.english: It is quite an established fact, that many soldiers (7th army) go back (from leave) to the army, because they have sold their army boots and their big coats (and have spent the proceeds on drinks etc.).
He is a stubborn fellow : a mad man does not listen.
entries.meaning: It requires great patience to calm him down.

entries.luganda: Kiraza mwoyo : ng'ebbwa eridda mu nkovu.
entries.english: It creates anxiety : like a sore that breaks out again on a scar.
entries.meaning: An incurable wound! Evil habits of old breaking out again.

entries.luganda: Kirevu ntende : kyalekerera wante ne kikwata wambuzi.
entries.english: A beard is a token of honour : (although) it kept away from the cow and stuck to the goat.
entries.meaning: The rich do not like it, when a poor man gets rich.

entries.luganda: Kireebereebe : 1) ng'empagi ey'omu ddiiro; 2) ng'amazzi g'omukonda gw'essu- nsa.
entries.english: An irresolute character : 1) like the middle post in the eating room; 2) like the water in the stalk of the gourd-leaf.
entries.meaning: Said of persons who show a wavering attitude.

entries.english: "It shall be later" (finally I shall arrive there) : says the mouse seeing food (1u- monde) on the next hill.
"It shall be later" (so says the kitanyi (afterbirth), when they bury it in the lusuku, referring to the child born) : but when he will be stooping (in old age), he will follow me.
entries.meaning: They bury me now; but they will do the same to him, when he gets old. The afterbirth, which is also called "mwana" feels unfairly treated and says "nti nze ski mwana?".

entries.english: A miserable little fellow who reached a chieftainship : forgets what has driven him away from his chief once.
entries.meaning: He does the same to his tenants, which he had to suffer from his chief. - Dutch "Als niet komt tot iet, kent iet zich zelve niet".

entries.luganda: Kiridde obwami : tabula muganda we (= tekibula ppanda zaakyo).
entries.english: Even an insignificant little man who has become chief : has plenty of people, who claim to be related to him.
entries.meaning: Or: People, who have become rich, are suddenly related to many.

entries.luganda: Kiri ewala : mpenduzo (= mpendo) y'ekireeta (= y'ekiggya).
entries.english: A thing which is far away (high up) : a hook will get it.
entries.meaning: Engl. "Difficulties are there to be overcome". Lat. "Per aspera ad astra". "Ne- cessity is the mother of invention". Germ. "Man muss sich zu helfen wissen".

entries.english: What is out on loan : does not ransom the child.
entries.meaning: The debtor might leave the child on your hands and not pay.

entries.luganda: "Kiri mulaala" : 1) teyeekolera luggi; 2) omusigire teyeegulira ngabo.
entries.english: "There is peace in the country" : 1) (says the man who builds a house and) puts no door into it (against thieves or animals); 2) says the deputy-chief and does not buy a shield for himself (to defend himself against his enemies).
A useless (ineffective) thing : like the spears of the Lubuga (queen-sister).
entries.meaning: She has the right to possess spears, but never uses them, because she does not go to war.

entries.luganda: Kirinsanga ewange : emmese efiira mu bunnya.
entries.english: (ekibi) The evil will come upon me at my home : the rat dies in its hole.
entries.meaning: The news will reach me early enough at my home.

entries.luganda: Kiruyi kya muzaana : kiggwera ku mmere.
entries.english: The anger of the slave-woman : comes to an end at the food.
entries.meaning: She has nothing else on which to vent her anger. So she beats the food.

entries.english: It is a bad doorway : that lets bad and good enter.
entries.meaning: Said of a woman-lover of the bad sort.

entries.english: (or: Ekiriibwa - - ) What is eaten by the (marauding) warrior : is not lost in vain.
entries.meaning: The loss of the owner of the food is for the good of the country.

entries.luganda: Kisaala munyazi : nti nnyinikyo eyakifuna anaakaaba musaayi (= okukira ald-funa).
entries.english: If a stolen thing (that is again stolen from the thief) annoys the thief : then the real owner will shed bloody tears (or: how much more will it annoy the owner).
(ekiswa) The ant-hill that is quite ready to emit the nswa : makes you cover it properly.
entries.meaning: If you want results, you must plan carefully.

entries.english: It is a smithy (in a smithy) : even one, who is not going to forge, arranges things (pieces of iron, tools etc.).
The bag of the absent one : gets filled with stones.
entries.meaning: Theft! Cf. the story of the "Mwalabu Ali, asomola munne" (Muloboza III.); cf. also legend of king Kagulu (Munno 1916 p.117).

entries.luganda: "Kisaayire okitte" : akirinda kwa mweya (= kwa kyeya).
entries.english: "Scrape off the grass round the anthill", to get the flying ants : (so one says) but he has to wait during the hot season (till the rains come).
entries.meaning: Success comes after patient waiting and watching.

entries.english: A thing which is laughed about by many.
entries.meaning: Like a katikkiro (Prime Minister), who is criticised by many. - To be in the "public eye".

entries.english: A wide stretch of open grassland (or: a fire-place) : is a place where nobody is forbidden to enter.
entries.meaning: Place for big gatherings, sport, public meetings etc.

entries.english: Dismiss it (from your mind) (it is beyond your reach, you won't get it) : as the snake won't grow feathers.
In the shade : one takes shelter from the sun.
entries.meaning: Expression for: Let us have a little rest here (in the shade).
