entries.english: It can happen that a man is not going to kill (the animal he has met) : as it has happened to the unthinking fellow who found only nine cowryshells (for the sacrifice).
entries.meaning: Nine were not enough; they had to be twice or thrice nine.

entries.english: If you cook a bug with your vegetables : you won't eat them.
entries.meaning: A bad character in good company. - "A fly in the ointment".

entries.luganda: Kiiso kya mbuzi : kirekerera omussi ne kitunuulira omubaazi.
entries.english: The big eye of the goat : leaves off looking at its killer and looks (reproachingly) at the butcher.
entries.meaning: Accusing the wrong person. "Barking up the wrong tree". - Duta explains: The real culprit is the mubaazi, because he ordered the killing.

entries.english: It is an empty egg-shell : they throw it on the road.
entries.meaning: If one loses his (earthly) possessions, they despise him. - Germ. "Die Kuh ist ausgemolken".

entries.luganda: Kisugga kya munafu : kye kitema omulima enkizi.
entries.english: A big thriving ensugga plant (in the overgrown garden) of the lazy woman : breaks the spine of the industrious neighbour (causes reasonable envy).

entries.luganda: Kitagenda : azaala abagenzi (= kizaala abagenyi); ekikonde kisindika effumu.
entries.english: "Kitagenda" : brings forth wanderers; the fist throws the spear.
entries.meaning: "Kitagenda" is a name denoting a man remaining long in his place; but his children are inclined to wander about in the world. Compared with the spear that flies away, whilst the fist remains.

entries.luganda: Kitali kibbe : eggufa osuula mu mulyango.
entries.english: If the animal (kisolo) was not stolen : you throw its bones out of the doorway.
entries.meaning: If it was stolen, you would hide the bones. Destroying evidence.

entries.english: "I see my (dead) father" : (saying so) does not prevent a prisoner from running away.
entries.meaning: "Kitange mmulaba" is an oath which the prisoner utters to make his captors loosen a little the tightly-fettered wrists. Although he swears by his dead father that he will not run away, still he will do so, if he has a chance.

entries.english: The misshaped pot of (a potter who is only) a learner : is rejected by the buyer.
entries.meaning: But he takes it all the same, to encourage the learner. Appreciation of the effort, not of the result.

entries.luganda: Kitasimbwa : kyajja ne mukoka, kimala kibala emyungu emingi (= kibala ebita).
entries.english: What has not been planted : came with the rain-water, and produced many vegetable-marrows (or: pumpkins).
entries.meaning: Many a man whose origin was unknown, came to great honour.

entries.english: What does not kill the Muyima : does not finish off his cattle.
entries.meaning: The Muyima cannot live without cattle. - "Kitatta" is a name adopted by king Mwanga, who clung to his kingdom, although he was driven out repeatedly. He stuck to it, as a Muyima sticks to his cattle. - Dutch "Zoo lang er leven is, is er hoop". - Lat. "Dum spiro, Spero".

entries.english: A useless fellow : like a man who points out the place where he wants his vegetables put.
entries.meaning: But he never buys any.

entries.luganda: Kitentegere : bw'okisubula tokivaako nga tekikusiize masanda.
entries.english: When you peel off the first layer (of the barkcloth-tree), you won't go away without being smeared by its latex.
entries.meaning: Going with bad friends contaminates.

entries.english: The "kiteruzi" is a man who throws some of the eatables (offered to him by the host) to the dog.
entries.meaning: A guest may never offer any food to the members of the household (children etc.). He would offend his host.

entries.luganda: Kiti kya muwogo : gy'okisuula gye kimerera (= bakisuula obutadda ne kirokera).
entries.english: (He is like) a stick of cassava : wherever you throw it, it grows.
entries.meaning: There are people, who survive anywhere. "He is for ever turning up like a bad penny".

entries.english: A fig-tree : is a gathering place for birds.
entries.meaning: One who arranges a dance brings many people together.

entries.english: The tsetse-fly : comes (apparently) with the intention of stinging and perishes thereby.
entries.meaning: It sucks itself full of blood to bursting point and does not see the hand going to kill it. - Passionate action of men leading to disaster for themselves.

entries.luganda: Kiwanga kya musenguse : kiva we bandikiziise, kigwa ku kubbo.
entries.english: The skull of a tenant who has left his master : is removed from the spot where they would have buried it, and falls on the road (i.e.
entries.meaning: perishes in the wilds). "Better the devil you know than the devil you don't know".

entries.english: (kigoma) The tig drum has no strings left.
entries.meaning: Its services are finished. Said of people who once had great influence and lost it all. Germ. "Der Mohr hat seine Schuldigkeit getan, der Mohr kann gehen".

entries.english: What has cooled down : can be got hold of with the hands (e.g.
entries.meaning: the corpse of a lion, of an enemy).

entries.english: Something that tastes well, whilst chewing : you will not vomit up again after swallowing.
entries.meaning: One easily gets accustomed to dangerous pleasures. - Lat. "Principiis obsta, sero medicina paratur" (Ovid). French "C'est le premier pas qui coate".

entries.english: Kibuuka (the chief mmandwa of the king) sees wonderful things.
A vagabond goes with vagabonds.
entries.meaning: Used of loose women. - "Oku-gya" is a lusoga word (archaic Luganda?).

entries.english: The old discarded hoe-handle is remembered, when the digging starts.
entries.meaning: When another one breaks, the old one is found useful again. - One day we might need people whom we have despised. Old friends!

entries.luganda: Kiyiira omunaku : kigwa mu vvu; bazibumbira okufa, ziramira mu kyokero.
entries.english: What makes a poor man thrive : falls into the ashes; they form the cooking pots from clay at the risk of their breaking, but they get hard (strong) in the kiln.
entries.meaning: The poor man gets what has fallen into the dust (what the rich man does not want any longer).

entries.luganda: Kiyirikiti kirinnyibwa buwaze : embwa bagikirinnyisa efudde.
entries.english: The "kiyirikiti" tree (Erythrina tomentosa) is climbed only with great effort (on account of the thorns) : they make the dog climb it, when it is dead.
entries.meaning: In okten times they threw dead dogs on such trees.

entries.english: The arum plant (ejjuuni) which is eaten by the elder : is sure to taste well.
entries.meaning: All food reserved for grown-ups excites the envy of children.

entries.english: The "kizeezengere" (an ugly cricket-like winged insect) kills one who does not take the warning.
entries.meaning: This insect makes a noise at night, if there is any person or animal about. So the traveller is warned, if there is any danger about. If he does not heed the warning, he might be killed.

entries.english: A spoilt (unsightly) thing : like a gonja (banana) that is fried with musasa- wood.
entries.meaning: Fire from musasa-wood discolours it and makes it unsightly. Said of a job that is done unsatisfactorily.

entries.english: If one says kizzeeyo (really: put it back) : he means weebale nnyo or nsiimye.
entries.meaning: He expresses gratitude for a gift, or a congratulation, especially used for com- plimenting one who has bought a nice cooking pot. The answer to it is mw'asii- mira = awo!

entries.english: That is the end : like the path to the well (or: as the road to Bubebbere).
entries.meaning: The road to Bubebbere - Buwaya - is the private road for the king's traditional worship place. - No outlet, a blind alley, cul-de-sac, impasse.

entries.luganda: Kkomekkome omuzaalisa ku lubugo : bw'olaba ng'atutte olubugo, ng'omwana omu; bw'olaba ng'atutte embuzi, nga balongo.
entries.english: That is the end of the work of the midwife : you can judge by the barkcloth; if you see her carrying a barkcloth, there was one child; if you see her taking a goat, there were twins.
The road makes one thin.
entries.meaning: Greek "Tes d'aretes hidrota theoi proparoithen ethekan" (Hesiod). Lat. "Per laborem ad honorem". "Ad augusta per angusta". "Per aspera ad astra" (Seneca).

entries.luganda: Kkumi lya mpisi : n'obuto nga bugenda.
entries.english: Where there are ten (= plenty of) hyenas, there also go the young ones.
entries.meaning: All are equally voracious.

entries.english: (= Akamwa akoogera - - ) A mouth that speaks evil : does not remain there.
entries.meaning: Evil talk becomes a habit, i.e. it will speak evil anywhere. And others take up the evil talk.

entries.english: "My uncle knows me" (said the frog, when the Creator - Mugereka - distributed tails, and did not hurry to go there) : and the frog went away without a tail.
entries.meaning: Therefore he has none to-day.

entries.english: Cancer is the husband of sores.
entries.meaning: A cancer-sore is the most fearful of sores. - Said also of bad moral habits: obwe- nzi, obutamiivu etc. Mina kookolo w'obwenzi - - Duta 1157.

entries.english: Work like a slave : and you will eat like a chief.
What you eat in the morning : you have with you, when trouble arises.
entries.meaning: It is better to be prepared than to trust to good luck. - It is better to eat before going to work.

entries.luganda: K'onooweeka : tokalinda kusaabaana ttosi (= kusaaba ttaka).
entries.english: If you are about to carry your child (on your back) : do not linger, till it has soiled itself with mud.
entries.meaning: If something has to be done, do it resolutely. "Go, whilst the going is good". "Nothing venture, nothing win".

entries.english: The mushroom you dig up yourself : you eat.
entries.meaning: No work, no food. "No pains, no gains".

entries.english: (akamweso) The razor-blade you have not shaved with yet : you praise for its sharp edge.
entries.meaning: "The proof of the pudding is in the eating".

entries.luganda: "Kozo mpola, tumalirize" : nga munda yanyiize dda.
entries.english: (One who says to his companion) "Go slow with the gravy, that we may finish together" : has resented (his companion's behaviour) long ago.
entries.meaning: He is afraid that - with the other man using the sauce so lavishly - it will be finished before the mmere is finished.

entries.luganda: Kufuuyira mbuzi mulere : sso nga teezine.
entries.english: (You can) play the flute to the goat : but she won't dance.
entries.meaning: "You can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear".

entries.english: (This is like) seeing a baby-vulture.
entries.meaning: Expression used for seeing a quite unusual (impossible) thing; because all the vultures, old and young, have bald heads. Therefore you cannot call any "young".

entries.english: (okulega = okulengera) One who says to you "Go in front" (through water or dew) : wishes to see your calves (legs) (and does not want to show his own).
entries.meaning: He has some selfish motive for giving the other person precedence.

entries.english: Praise for (the work in the field during) the cold of the morning.
entries.meaning: Expression of gratitude for a present of field-produce (e.g. a basket of maize- cobs etc.).

entries.english: A shameless scoffer : like a male louse.
entries.meaning: He is an incomprehensible character. - You cannot see the difference between a male and a female louse.

entries.english: To eat vegetable marrow : does not mean to pick and choose (because it is so soft, it presents no difficulties).

entries.luganda: "Ku mbuga ndivaako bwereere" : ennyama anyaga ya vviivi embi; nti nno singa anyaze ennungi.
entries.english: "I shall come from the chief's place with empty hands" : (he who said so) grabs a bad knee-piece (of meat); if only he had grabbed a decent piece!
To eat one's soul (to take a great risk) : like the chicken that swallows red (safari) ants.
entries.meaning: - To eat or to do something out of passion, will do harm to oneself. Reckless behaviour! "It is worth a tummy-ache".

entries.english: The road goes past the mouth.
entries.meaning: So one says who has been handed food to pass it on to somebody else - and takes a bite.

entries.luganda: "Kunaaba kumirungusa" : ng'ow'amalibu asanze bafumba emyungu n'ettooke.
entries.english: "That will be just a matter of gobbling it up" : (says) the toothless fellow, when he finds them cooking vegetable marrow and bananas (i.e.
entries.meaning: it will be easy work for me to eat that).

entries.english: (It is like) washing the back of a clean man (i.e.
entries.meaning: easy work, because he is clean already).

entries.english: To make everything smaller (less) : like a thief belonging to the household (he knows where everything is).
To make the head come off (to screw it loose - the neck -) : as when the one- eyed man greets two persons (at the same time) (he has to turn from one to the other).
"Hereabouts is our home" (says he) : but he does not tell you, where he lives.
entries.meaning: He does not trust you.

entries.english: On the feast of the birth of twins : all the unsightly (badly dressed, cripples etc.) are there.
entries.meaning: A dance where all take part.

entries.english: (That is like) sliding down the path that goes to the river (to the well) (i.e.
entries.meaning: it is as easy as sliding - -, it goes by itself).

entries.luganda: Kusigalawo kuzirinda : ng'omwana w'omufu asaba ow'omulamu olubugo.
entries.english: To be left over means to wait for trouble : as when an orphan comes to the surviving relation, for a barkcloth (for the burial).
entries.meaning: The survivor is the goal for petitioners.

entries.english: (That is like) dragging a water-lizard over a rock (i.e.
entries.meaning: a difficult task, because the water-lizard holds itself on the rock with its claws).

entries.english: (The man who dares) to pass through your gourd plants, wants a fight with you.

entries.luganda: "Kuzaala kulimu ki?" : nga gwe waza?la takuwulira.
entries.english: "What good is there in bringing forth children?" : (so you say) if your child does not obey you.
"To have children is a good thing" : (so you say) if your child obeys you.
(The fellow who said) "Oh, it will be moonlight (we need not go yet)" : they have left at Mbaale (Mawokota).
entries.meaning: The others left for home, when it was still daylight. He remained and lost the way. Misplaced confidence!

entries.english: Be friend to many : trust few!
That's what the eyes are looking at (and nothing else) : as the barren woman looks at her husband.
entries.meaning: Because there are no children to look at.

entries.luganda: Kwe kuwampanya : ng'abulidde embiro; nti aligoba wa mmindi.
entries.english: It is a mere subterfuge (trick) of one who is out of breath (to say) : the one who follows us is a pipe-man (a mulogo) (i.e.

"That is also my opinion" : (one who always says so, is just) like the middle finger (which goes along with the other fingers: if you count - and show - "2", the middle finger is there; if you count "3", it comes along; if you count "4" or "5", it is there).
entries.meaning: Applied to people who have no opinion of their own. Yes-men! Nnampawe- ngwa!

entries.english: That is what I put the stick on (i.e.
entries.meaning: that is what I like to eat). Old expression for a favourite dish. "Kye ndiira ddala".

entries.english: Useless trouble-making : as of one who hates the person he has to deal with.
To nurse a poisonous snake in its hole.
entries.meaning: "To court disaster". Germ. "Eine Schlange am eigenen Busen aufziehen".

entries.english: An animal (kisolo) that belongs to both of us : remains untouched, if it dies (till both owners unanimously decide upon it).
Kyagaba (name of a big land-owner in Bulemeezi) does not joke : he is a child (native) of Kasagga (village in Bulemeezi).

entries.luganda: Kyajja na mazzi : ne kibala eŋŋunda.
entries.english: It came with the (rain) water : and produced a calabash.

entries.luganda: Kya kagambwa : ng'omuwuulu anaatuuma nnyinimu erinnya.
entries.english: The way (of speaking) of a forward (pert) person : as when an unmarried fellow addresses the owner of the household by his name.
entries.meaning: Or, when he inquires boldly: amawolu gaffe tunaagalya ddi?

entries.english: What has just arrived (= what is new) : does not lack charm.
entries.meaning: French "La nouveaute a ses charmes". "Tout nouveau, tout beau".

entries.english: He who is only learning how to beat the engalabi (long drum) : does not sing (when he beats).
entries.meaning: He is too occupied with the drumming.

entries.english: Underdone food : does not heed fire.
entries.meaning: What has not been cooked well and gets cold, does not become tasty in the second cooking. Lukewarmness is difficult to remedy.

entries.english: "That may well be" (says the co-wife, hearing something which discredits her fellow-wife) : she does not defend her.
(ggala = muligo) It grew up knowing nothing : like a mouse that lives in the house of a poor man.
entries.meaning: It does not even know how to climb up, because there was never anything eatable in the house.

entries.english: What has attacked you : cannot be pushed back.
entries.meaning: Death is unescapable. - This proverb was the name of king Kimbugwe's umbili-cal cord.

entries.english: The business of dressing has brought great trouble.
entries.meaning: So one says who has nothing to put on.

entries.english: The good advice (ekibuuliriro) has taken no effect : as when the child fails to listen to the advice of the mother.
What he will tell me : I shall do.
A good village (ekyalo) : can become a bad one (circumstances can change).
entries.meaning: Or: A good affair (ekigambo) can develop into a bad one.

entries.english: Great difficulties are overcome with the shield.
entries.meaning: Well prepared for the battle. Lat. "Per aspera ad astra". "Onoolyanga emmere yo ng'omaze kugituyanira" (Gen.3.17). French "Aux grands maux les grands remedes". Germ. "Segen ist der Millie Preis".

entries.luganda: Ky'amukubye : Kawuta akikuba ente mu lubiri.
entries.english: The throw he has given him (in wrestling) : is like the one the head-slaughterer (head cook) gives to the cattle in the king's enclosure.
What somebody has refused to give to you : you will obtain through your child.
"(Formerly this banana plant - kitooke -) was extremely fertile (bearing a big enkota, driving new shoots)" : (one saying so) belittles the shoots (offspring).
entries.meaning: Applied to men and their children or successors.

entries.english: If something happens that one never saw before : he fails to understand.
What God gives to man : is always fresh.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Tu das escam illorum in tempore opportuno" (Ps.145.15). 3.43, Mulo-boza II.p.54.

entries.english: "That is what they want me to do" (says the dutiful warrior) and goes to battle and does not come back.
entries.meaning: He dies in battle. Selfless sense of duty.

entries.english: An extraordinary (impossible) thing : as when a fellow who has got dropsy also grows a hump (how will he sleep?).
What is appreciated very much : will soon be lost.
entries.meaning: "Whom the gods love, die young".

entries.english: One who has seen his folly : like one who has formerly befriended a fellow with protruding jaw-bones.
entries.meaning: Whenever she sees a large lizard, she thinks: that is a twin-brother of my former friend.

entries.english: Terror does not know a courageous man (or vice versa).
I do not eat, whatever is big : the "effa-mpewo" (= ekyengabo = the biggest banana-row on the nkota) I give to the master of the house.
entries.meaning: The best food (part of anything) is served to the master.

entries.english: A way of showing-off : as when a "beauty" calls herself "Nnabiweke" (one with natural small tufts of hair - enviiri za kaweke).

entries.luganda: Kye ndikuwa olikwasaako ebbiri : akuwa lumonde wa bikuta.
entries.english: What I shall give you, you will have to get hold of with both hands : (one saying so) gives you a hot potato in the "jacket".

entries.luganda: "Kye nkola bannange : saagala bakinkole"; ng'omubbi bamubbye (or: ng'omu-sezi bamuseze).
entries.english: "The evil I do to my neighbours : I don't want done to me"; so says the thief, when they have stolen from him (or: so says the night-sorcerer, when they have bewitched him).
entries.meaning: Engl. "Do as you would be done by". Lat. "Quod tibi fieri non vis, alteri ne feceris". "Do not do to anyone what you yourself would hate" (Tob.4.14). "Kyonna kyonna kye mwagala abantu babakolere, nammwe mukibakoleranga" (Matth.7.12).

entries.luganda: "Kinkubidde mu nnimiro" : 1) n'okubunga ng'obunga; 2) ng'ezzimu eggumba.
entries.english: It (the kizimu) came down upon me in the garden : 1) (so you say) when dizziness (kantolooze) gets hold of you; 2) like a barren whirlwind.

entries.luganda: "Kye nkulekera olyanga" : bwe yeerabira ensawo, akoma mu luggya ng'agiddira.
entries.english: (He says) "What I leave over, you may eat" : but if he has forgotten his bag, he turns back in the courtyard and fetches it.
The measure of love with which I love you : is hidden in a stone.
entries.meaning: You cannot fathom how I love you. If it was a piece of wood, you could break the wood and see.

entries.luganda: Kye nnalaba ewattu : sikitenda mu ddya.
entries.english: What I have seen at home : I do not talk about, where I am married.
entries.meaning: It is considered bad manners for a woman to reveal scandals of her family to her husband. "Eby'omu nju tebittottolwa".

entries.luganda: Kyenyi kibi : tekirukirwa nkundulu; omala nga bambalikawo.
entries.english: For an evil (misformed) forehead : no hat is woven; you have to force it on.
entries.meaning: Not all evils (growths, misshapes etc.) can be hidden (disguised).

entries.english: The forehead (face) of an ugly person : asks for water and the beautiful one gets it.
entries.meaning: A pretty face is a good recommendation. - Also applied to the distribution of other things: prices, bibanja etc.

entries.english: The offending remark (kigambo) is soon forgotten by the one who has made it : but the one who has been offended (gwe bakigamba) does not forget it.
A good thing is given up (foregone in favour of others) : and you give it to your friend.
It comes without being called : like the peeler of menvu.
entries.meaning: When menvu are peeled for mubisi, as a rule, no outside help is called - "the uninvited guest".

entries.english: A thing (kitereke) that gives itself away : like a parcel of peanuts.
entries.meaning: The rattle indicates what is in the parcel. Rub.C.1141. 2527 Kye sirabanga, sikyogera : enkuba tejjuza kamoome. What I have never seen, I do not talk about (even if you tell me to) : rain does not fill the holes in an anthill (special kind, small). One cannot convince a man, who does not want to understand.

entries.luganda: Kye sirya, mbuusa : omuyaayu ndaba ddiba.
entries.english: What I don't eat, will hardly do me good : of a wild cat I look only for its skin (I don't want its meat).
entries.meaning: Expression for: I doubt it - I have not seen it myself.

entries.luganda: Kye siirye kukkuta : ndekera abaana ne balya; nnasswi takwata ku nkejje.
entries.english: What won't be enough food for me : I leave for the children and they eat it; the little finger does not get hold of the sprats (small fish).
entries.meaning: The little finger which, as a rule, does not get hold of small articles, is considered just as important (therefore it is grammatically in the mu-ba class).

entries.luganda: Kyetta ng'eya zigoto : amayembe ezza mu kyenyi.
entries.english: Something (kisolo) that kills itself, like a cow with horns turned inward : it turns the horns towards its own forehead.
entries.meaning: Said of a person who ruins his (her) own existence, who runs with open eyes to his doom.

entries.english: Putting oneself into danger : like a one-eyed person digging under the walls of a house (to break in).
entries.meaning: If the falling earth blinds his one eye, he won't be able to escape.

entries.english: What you have seen (discovered, received) is yours.
entries.meaning: More than what you don't possess yet. Lat. "Melior est conditio possidentis".

entries.english: What you were accustomed to eat : you give up, when privation comes.
entries.meaning: You can do without many things. Germ. "Sich nach der Decke strecken".

entries.english: Whatever you have brought forth : is not bad.
entries.meaning: It is your child. - Engl. "Every man thinks his own geese swans".

entries.english: What you agreed (to give the musawo) when you were sick : you refuse to give when you are better.
entries.meaning: To make a promise is easier than to keep it.

entries.luganda: Ky'ofa togabye : Walumbe y'agaba (= akigaba, = akikugabira).
entries.english: What you have not yet given away, when you die : Death will give away.

entries.luganda: Ky'ofuna oyagala : bwe kikudibirira (= bwe kikutamirira) oyita Katonda, nti Ayi Katonda, singa okinzigyeko!
entries.english: You are pleased with a thing, when you get it : but when you get tired of it, you cry to God: Oh God, if you only would take it from me!
entries.meaning: Fickleness of man! Rain, sunshine etc.

entries.english: What has been talked about : is sure to be there.
entries.meaning: "Where there's smoke, there's fire".

entries.english: You have hardly started to take (the first morsel of) matooke (with the kabezo) : and you reach at once the watery part (of it).
entries.meaning: You are too hasty; you judge too quickly; you act too rashly.

entries.english: What you keep hidden at your home : the lubaale-priest reveals (saying: such a thing has brought trouble upon you).

: nti "Endiga yazaala bumeka?" You ask what you see with your own eyes : namely "How many lambs has the sheep brought forth?" You ask the obvious, as the little lambs are always with the mother, not like little goats.
What you see (experience) when you are alone : makes you exaggerate the facts (e.g.
entries.meaning: the snake was so long).

entries.english: What you have experienced : the gonja (banana) experiences in famine-time.
entries.meaning: It is boiled, fried; even the root-stock is dug out and eaten. Said to people who have gone through many trials.

entries.english: What you hide in your statement : makes you lose the case.
entries.meaning: Or: What you leave behind - in the place of crime - causes your conviction. Corpus delicti. - Applicable to hiding sins in confession.

entries.luganda: Ky'olimba obuko : kye kibutta; ndikuttira enswa, ng'ekiswa kikotera.
entries.english: Cheating your relations by marriage : is destroying your relations with them; (it is like saying) "I shall catch flying ants for you", when the anthill is empty.
entries.meaning: Lying people cannot be trusted.

entries.luganda: Ky'olyako omuddu : kye kikuseenyeza enviiri ku mutwe.
entries.english: The food you refuse to give to your servant : makes your hair red on your head.
entries.meaning: The servant, in order to take revenge, pulls your hair, cuts you in shaving your head etc. So you are afraid of his services and you let your hair grow long and discoloured.

entries.english: The food (or any useful thing) you refuse to give to your nephew : makes him indignant.
entries.meaning: Bukodo (stinginess) is very much despised among Africans.

entries.luganda: Ky'omanyiira bwe kiba : amaaso g'omunya tegafa munyale.
entries.english: What you are familiar with (causes no difficulties) : the eyes of the lizard don't become blinded by the sooty cobwebs.

entries.luganda: Ky'onkoze, enkoko ekikola bwana bwayo : ky'ejje ebuzaale, ng'ebufuula ente- be yaayo.
entries.english: What you have done to me, a hen does to her chickens : when she has hardly hatched them, she makes them into a chair for herself.
From the plantain which you raise without effort, you eat the banana.
entries.meaning: The result will be according to the effort. - "No pains, no gains".

entries.english: What you put aside (meat etc.) for your favourite wife : is eaten by the neglected one.

entries.luganda: Ky'otobuulirako munno : 1) enseko zikiyitako; 2) emmese ekibba.
entries.english: What you don't tell your friend : 1) is passed over with laughter (it cannot be appreciated); 2) the rat will steal it (where you have hidden it).
entries.meaning: Do not withhold anything from a good friend. - Germ. "Geteilte Freude ist doppelte Freude, geteilter Schmerz ist halber Schmerz".

entries.english: What you don't eat yourself : don't drive the dog away from it.
entries.meaning: Said to a father who wants to refuse his daughter to a certain suitor.

entries.luganda: Ky'otomanyi bwe kiba : amazina ag'ekirevu olabira ku mmere.
entries.english: What you don't understand directly, (you can judge by circumstances) : you see the dancing of the beard during the eating.
What you don't know : is like kneaded matooke; you don't know how many bananas are in it.
What you have not yet got in your possession : do not consider as yours; they took back the bananas, you had stolen, at night.
entries.meaning: French "Ne vendez pas la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tire".

entries.english: What you never have eaten yet : do not open your mouth for it.
entries.meaning: "Do not count your chickens, before they are hatched".

entries.english: What you don't intend to give to an adult : don't lie about.
You might give a loan whilst sitting : but to get it back, you have to get up.
entries.meaning: It is easier to give a loan than to get it back (looking for the debtor, court-dealings etc.).

entries.english: What you love : you make last long.
entries.meaning: You take great care of it.

entries.luganda: Ky'oyagala tekijja gy'oli : Nnabuzaana akwata Banyolo.
entries.english: What you desire, does not come to you : (the goddess) Nnabuzaana gets hold of Banyoro-women.
entries.meaning: The Baganda women desired to become wives of kings and chiefs, and therefore they sacrificed to Nnabuzaana. But Nnabuzaana used to favour Banyoro women, bringing them into lubiri and the chief's places.

entries.luganda: Ky'oyagala tekikwagala : gy'okuba olubuto, entumbwe ekubayo mabega.
entries.english: What you like, does not like you : the calf (of your leg) turns its back to the side your stomach is turned to.

entries.luganda: Ky'oyagala tekikwagala : omwana wa mwannyoko akula nga nsujju.
entries.english: What you like, does not like you : the child of your sister grows quickly like vegetable marrow.
entries.meaning: The uncle loses his niece (when she gets married) and she is no longer useful to him.

entries.luganda: Ky'oyagala tekikwagala : singa emmere esula mu ttama.
entries.english: What you like, does not like you : otherwise the food would remain in your mouth.
entries.meaning: Love is often one-sided, unrequited.

entries.english: (One who says) "Stop, let the guests eat" : does not let his own child eat enough.
(Although the woman, who is being beaten by her husband, whilst others want to take her part, says) "Let them beat me" : still she will soon be crying out all the same.
entries.meaning: She does not say that in all meekness.

entries.english: The path is well-trodden : like the one that leads to the kitchen.
entries.meaning: That is so, as long as the wife is there. If she is dead, or has run away, the presence of cobwebs shows it.

entries.english: "(The generous helping of ttooke) has given me a chance to satisfy my ravenous appetite" : (so you say) when you eat from a big helping.
(eggumba) (The insolent child says) "Give me the bone, let me break it" (to suck out the marrow).
entries.meaning: As if a child could do that better than an adult! The child wants the rest of the meat on the bone.

entries.english: "Wait till the pain is over" : (one saying so) prolongs your sickness.
entries.meaning: He prevents you from getting the remedy in time.

entries.english: "Wait till all the miserable lame fellows are there" : that brought the Buvuma- island under domination (of the Baganda).
entries.meaning: The Baganda, under Mulangira Kayemba, attacked Buvuma. Each warrior, stepping out of the boat (canoe), stood on one foot. The Bavuma thought that they were all lame and let them all land. That gave the Baganda a chance to attack in full strength and to beat the Bavuma. - Underestimating the danger is courting disaster. "A stitch in time saves nine". "Prevention is better than cure". "An ounce of prevention is better than a pound of cure".

entries.english: "Wait till it is dark and let us have fun with the girls" : (one who says so) must be a leper!
entries.meaning: A leper has no chance in daytime.

entries.english: "Wait for another time (kiseera) to come" (says the unmarried woman to her suitor, because she does not want to get married yet) : and the girl waits for blows on her head (musango, illegitimate child etc.).
(One who says to you) "Wait a little" : wants you to buy stolen things.
entries.meaning: He wants uncomfortable witnesses first to disappear.

entries.english: The lubaale (or witch doctor) profits either way (he takes his fee, wether the sick person dies or recovers).

entries.luganda: Lubaale maliba : bull afuluma alyambala bubwe.
entries.english: The idea of God (religion) is like skins : each one (every mortal) will adopt his own Each one chooses that religion he considers the right one for him.
entries.meaning: The Supreme Being is honoured in different ways.

entries.english: The sky is not (like) the womb of a woman : when it is pregnant (with rain) it brings forth at once.

entries.luganda: Lubaale w'ekiswa : talagwamu lunwe (= nnantalagwamu lunwe).
entries.english: The spirit of an anthill : is not pointed at with the (stretched-out) fore-finger.
entries.meaning: Otherwise the ants won't fly. The openings of the anthill (amaaso) may be pointed at only with the curved fore-finger or with the thumb.

entries.english: The lubaale of a living person is not overpowered (by another person).
entries.meaning: Each person was supposed to have his (her) own lubaale. One trying to do harm to his neighbour by inciting the respective lubaale against each other, tries in vain.

entries.luganda: Lubwa lukovvu onyoomera mu kyoto : naye bwe lutuuka ku nsiko nga luwera nnemba.
entries.english: You despise a miserable dog, when it lies near the fire : but when it reaches the wilds, it makes a brave show (is tireless in hunting).
entries.meaning: Underestimating apparently insignificant people!

entries.luganda: Luganda lwa mbwa : lulamusa na mannyo.
entries.english: Relationship of dogs : is shown by greeting with the teeth (because they cannot talk).
entries.meaning: Duta: It does not come from the heart.

entries.english: A poor old drum : a man who knows its good qualities, takes the (broken) strings off it and puts new ones on.
entries.meaning: Respectful treatment of old people and things!

entries.luganda: Lugudde ku Munyolo : Abaganda baseke (= beesekere).
entries.english: When trouble has befallen a Munyolo : the Baganda rejoice.
entries.meaning: Old enmity between the two peoples! Malicious joy at the misfortune of others.

entries.english: "(The poor old person) is bearing it patiently (hunger, want)" : (so one com- miserates with a poor man) even when he has eaten something.

entries.luganda: Lukande lwa nnyoko : lukira olwa muka-kitaawo olulime.
entries.english: The uncultivated land of your own mother : is worth more than the cultivated plot of (another) wife of your father.
On going down to the lake : one does not leave behind the fish-basket.
The stem of the lukindu-palm : cannot be bent (even the young stems).
entries.meaning: Obstinacy, stubbornness of people. "Muntu mukakanyavu!"

entries.english: When death strikes the cock : it leaves the hens in confusion.
entries.meaning: "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered" (Zak.13.7).

entries.luganda: Lukuggya we bajjula : ne lukutwala we basaaniika.
entries.english: (lubwa) Misfortune takes you from a place where they dish up the food, and brings you to where they still cover it for cooking.
entries.meaning: "To fall between two stools".

entries.english: (I am) "Death makes you covet".
entries.meaning: Lament of a widow who looks with envy on other women still possessing their husbands.

entries.english: (lute) An old cow that still can be milked is not threatened with the axe.
entries.meaning: They do not think of killing it. - What is still useful, should not be destroyed.

entries.english: Where there is beer at the mourning-rites : a consoler is not lacking.
entries.meaning: A rich man has many "friends".

entries.english: "Death is a passionate killer" : (so one says) if it has killed a relation (brother or sister).
Gnaw the bone and let the broth cool down!
entries.meaning: Stands for "keep quiet and let me explain first!"

entries.luganda: Lumbe lukuba eggu ne luleka omuzima.
entries.english: Death strikes the unripe fruit (of the muwafu tree) and leaves the ripe one alone.
entries.meaning: Death does not spare the young.

entries.english: Potatoes prepare the soil for bananas.
entries.meaning: Before planting a lusuku one plants potatoes on the plot.

entries.english: The big potato made the barkcloth-maker fight (with his wife).
entries.meaning: She gave the biggest potato to her child instead of her husband, who came home from work tired and hungry.

entries.english: Death has taken him : (somebody not much concerned about the person) answers: "Ah well, many people have died (since Adam and Eve)".
(lukazi) The woman who intends to leave you : is sure to complain about something.
entries.meaning: Her complaints are: you give me nothing; my relations get nothing, when they come on a visit etc. - Applied to a person trying to justify a wrong action.

entries.english: The sickness will kill the patient : and I suck it in.
entries.meaning: From me, the mujjanjabi, they expect all the information regarding his death. Other version: - - and I contract it myself (by eating what the sick person left over).

entries.luganda: Lunaayabira emmanga : nga y'ekira oluganda (= nga y'esinga oluganda).
entries.english: The finishing of the mourning-rites will be held in the other village : (so is the decision of the responsible persons), if in that village there is a person who is a closer relation.
The finishing of the mourning-rites will be held on the next hill : (so they may say) if there greater amusement is to be had.
"Let the vegetable-marrow plant be sweet (to me)" : (one saying so) gets the seeds out of the fruit (for planting them in his own garden).
entries.meaning: Let good things multiply themselves.

entries.luganda: Lusala ekyayi : lulekera munyeera okusaasaana (= kutaataagana).
entries.english: When the plantain-fibre is cut away : it leaves the small ants (that have built in the trunk) scattered.
entries.meaning: When the owner of the house dies, his dependents are scattered.

entries.english: Sickness sets (people) at variance.
entries.meaning: It causes suspicion, even among good friends, that somebody has bewitched the sick person.

entries.english: The old hunting net : kills (catches the animal) even where there is no game track.
entries.meaning: Old methods don't lose their usefulness altogether.

entries.luganda: Lutta embwa : mu lw'ente batuula kitebe.
entries.english: When death kills the dog (nobody takes much notice) : but at the killing of a cow they sit up happily.
entries.meaning: Also applied to the attitude of people upon a death notice: rich - poor, stranger - relation etc.

entries.english: When death takes your companion : (you say) I am a protg of the spirit (i.e.
entries.meaning: he won't kill me). But the one who died was also a protg of his spirit. That will not save you.

entries.english: (luyombo) "How did the quarrel come about?" : (one who asks that question) makes the quarrel into a court case.
When the mourners (consolers) have all gone away from the burial : the bereaved ones are left to their sorrow.
A general calamity reduces even a witchdoctor (lubaale-man) to tears.
entries.meaning: A mmandwa is considered as a man without feelings. So, if he weeps, the calamity must be great.

entries.english: The small firewood belonging to a man whom you know (who cut down a tree) : you gather when you find it.
When the poor man kills an animal : he easily finds a friend (but not a disinter- ested one).
"The day came to kill people" : (says) the heir of a rich man.
entries.meaning: An expression to hide his satisfaction.

entries.english: The mourning rites of a good person : are praised a long time.
There is passion in blowing a whistle (horn) : you bow, whilst you are licking.
entries.meaning: You should do both things separately. One job at a time.

entries.english: The longings of a living being never come to an end.

entries.luganda: Madongo asanyuse : nga ku musu kw'alaba.
entries.english: Madongo (name for a dog) is happy : when he spots an edible rat.
entries.meaning: Said of things which are habitually welcome. Germ. "Ein gefundenes Fressen".

entries.luganda: Mafuta ga nte : gava mu nte ne gadda mu ddiba.
entries.english: The fat of the cow : comes from the cow and goes back into the hide of the cow (in tanning).
entries.meaning: Said of the circulation of goods (money) amongst the people.

entries.english: You can speak about spears only with a man who has fought with them.
entries.meaning: Speak with people only about subjects they can understand.

entries.luganda: Magulu ga ntungo : gasigala mu ssibiro.
entries.english: The stalks of semsem : remain in the place, where it was hung up for drying.
entries.meaning: They were treasured, as long as they carried the seed; after threshing they are considered rubbish. - Germ. "Der Mohr hat seine Schuldigkeit getan, der Mohr kann gehen".

entries.english: Even a lazy person burns the rubbish (on the field) during the planting-season.
entries.meaning: Expression used to tease a lazy woman; same as "Olimala ddi?"

entries.english: Just the same : as with the mouse that dwells with the poor man.
entries.meaning: When the man goes out for food, the mouse also goes out; when he comes back with food, the mouse brings grass for the nest. ("Makulane" is of Arabic origin.) Duta 894.

entries.english: A strange thing : like a bedstead on which there is a bowl (with vegetables).
entries.meaning: That is the wrong place to put it.

entries.luganda: "Mala okulya" : ava ku mmindi ya taba.
entries.english: "Eat first" : (one who says so) omits to offer a smoke (to the guest).
entries.meaning: To offer a pipe (before the meal) is taken as a sign of welcome.

entries.english: (If they tell a man) "Eat first" (before you go) : the sun does not wait for him.
entries.meaning: It will be dark before he reaches home.

entries.english: (He who says to you) "Eat first" : does not tell you about the additional dishes (to whet your appetite).

entries.luganda: "Mala okulya" : bw'ovaawo ye agamba, nti "abadde amira ebitole".
entries.english: (One who says to you) "Eat first" : when you leave, he says (to the others) "But that fellow swallows lumps of matooke!" Rub.C.1180.
(One who says to you) "Eat first" : talks about your ravenous appetite.
The sobbing (wailing) of men : is wailing like rumbling talk (not like that of women, who shriek their laments).

entries.luganda: Maluulu ga kyalo : tegakusuuza bbuzi lyo.
entries.english: An alarm raised in the village : does not make you neglect your goat.
entries.meaning: Not all follow the alarm (the blind, the lame, those afraid of their property).

entries.english: Eating "enkolo" (famine-food) does not find understanding (with eating plenty).
entries.meaning: Rich and poor live next to each other. Futility of the communistic "paradise"?

entries.luganda: Maanyi ga tulo : gava ku lukokola; bw'otofunyako tiweebaka.
entries.english: Sound sleep comes from the elbow; if you don't fold it (and put your hand under your head), you won't sleep well.
Keep it to yourself : like the calabash with the long neck.
entries.meaning: You cannot see whether there is beer in it.

entries.english: Crossroads kill the one who greets and the one who is greeted.
entries.meaning: Both might be taken by the executioners of the king or killed by enemies or killed by accident, whilst obstructing the road.

entries.english: Small eyes : are worth more than things that glitter.
entries.meaning: "Not all is gold that glitters". Quality is better than quantity.

entries.luganda: Matankane : ng'empale y'omuseveni; mpanvu si mpanvu, nnyimpi si nnyimpi.
entries.english: Doubtful (uncertain) : as the trousers of a 7th-army-man; they are long, but not long enough, they are short, but not short enough.

entries.luganda: Mateerero : nti enkoko yange ebiika mu kyalo.
entries.english: Rash judgement : (to say) my hen is laying eggs in the village.
entries.meaning: Can you judge that by its breast?

entries.english: Big lumps (of ttooke) will not alienate the child from its mother.
entries.meaning: The natural love of the child towards its mother is not overcome by material attractions.

entries.luganda: Matu ga mubaazi : gawulira kya "mbwa etwala ennyama yo"; omusaba takuwa.
entries.english: The ears of a butcher : hear (if you tell him) "The dog is stealing your meat"; but if you ask him for a piece of meat, he does not give it.
entries.meaning: French "Il n'est pire sourd que qui ne veut entendre". Convenient deafness.

entries.english: The ears don't suffer hunger.
entries.meaning: They are always open. The day does not pass without hearing something.

entries.english: Gray hairs (old people) do not like to kneel without reason.
entries.meaning: One should not easily refuse the request of old people. "Mavi ga mukulu" is the name of a herb.

entries.english: (also: Okikinadde : ng'eryambe ezziba.) Stuck-up-manners : like a (big) Baziba knife.
entries.meaning: The cutting edge of the Baziba knife is curved backwards. - Used for stubborn- ness, conceit.

entries.english: Cold food does not break the cooking pot.
entries.meaning: "Ntamu" stands for "meal". Having cold food does not prevent one from cooking a fresh meal.

entries.luganda: Mayanja assa bigere Lukumbi : ng'omutwe guli Sseguku.
entries.english: The river Mayanja has its feet (at Lukumbi), whilst its head (source) is at Sseguku (Kyaddondo).
entries.meaning: The Mayanja Kato has its source at Sseguku and becomes a rapid river at Luku- mbi. There it is called Mayanja ow'Olusenke.

entries.luganda: Maziga ga mmese : gajja na kamasu.
entries.english: The tears of the rat come, when it is caught in the trap.

entries.luganda: Maziga ga musota : gajja na muggo.
entries.english: The tears of a snake : come with the stick.
entries.meaning: When the snake is beaten. The snake does not hear ("listen"). Belated sorrow! Germ. "Wer nicht horen will, muss fiihlen".

entries.luganda: Maziribano : ng'omubi awonga; nti "ekibi kigwana wala".
entries.english: A complicated mess : as when an ugly man goes to bring an offering to the lubaale; (he says) "may the evil go away from me".
entries.meaning: Reply: but where should the lubaale then throw you (as you are so ugly)?

entries.english: Water obtained by begging : does not quench the thirst.
entries.meaning: Begging does not make one rich, but work and personal effort. Do the work yourself and then you know that it is done.

entries.english: Where the desire to drink beer sends you you can hardly refuse to go.

entries.luganda: "Mbijjukidde" : omuwuulu enswa azimalira ku kiswa (= omuwuulu aziriira ku kiswa).
entries.english: "I remember things" : (namely that a bachelor has nobody at home to prepare the flying ants) therefore he eats them at the anthill.
Let me turn them over (namely the things spread in the sun for drying) : the sun does not go down in the direction of Bulemeezi.
entries.meaning: So say the people South or West of Bulemeezi. - It is still time. Rub.C.790. 2734a Mbiro ntono : zikira okwekweka (= okwekisa). (Running away) slowly : is better than hiding oneself. They will find you.

entries.luganda: "Mboneredde" : 1) ali ku nkoomi; 2) tata muze; 3) y'amala abikola.
entries.english: "I am sorry" : 1) (says the sorcerer) when he is at the stake (to be burnt); 2) (says the evildoer) but he does not give up his evil desires; 3) (says the disobe-dient child) but at once it does it again.
The chief's place, where you are a favourite, is better than all the traps.
entries.meaning: If you are a hunter, you might be able to trap many animals; but a favourite of the chief is better off.

entries.english: The chief's place is no lusuubo (a food parcel suspended on a string in the hut, to protect the food from rats).
The chief's place is not in a backward place.
entries.meaning: It is situated on a prominent spot; therefore they say anywhere: "tugende engulu ew'omwami".

entries.english: The chief's place is not supposed to tell lies.
A clever (marvellous) thing (or person) : like the water in the leafstalk (petiole) of the vegetable-plant.
entries.meaning: There is no opening, where the water could have entered and still the water flows out, when the stalk is broken.

entries.english: Bad barkcloth is not appreciated in the market place.
entries.meaning: In public a man shows his best.

entries.english: A goat crying without tears.
entries.meaning: It shouts (wails) only and gives you nothing, not even tears.

entries.english: A dog is more useful than a cow.
entries.meaning: Because it hunts, watches, announces even the death of his master.

entries.english: The dog kills even the singer.
entries.meaning: Whilst the master sings, his dog roams about and steals food, and the people hold the singer responsible. Referring to the responsibility of parents, masters etc. for the misdeeds of their children.

entries.english: (or: Wambwa ne Wango.) Dogs and leopards.
entries.meaning: Referring to the enmity between dogs and leopards. "Like cats and dogs".

entries.english: A dog that is tied up : bites the one who comes near it.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Qui amat periculum, peribit in illo".

entries.english: The work of the hands is money.
A chatterbox (whose lips have no rest) : talks uncharitably about anybody who comes.

entries.luganda: Mirimu gya mu ttoggo : gikooya buli omu.
entries.english: The work of the rainy season (March-April-May) makes everybody tired.
entries.meaning: Because everyone is in the field.

entries.luganda: Miti gy'amayuuni : basimba bayegeekereza; bwe gikula ne gyesimba.
entries.english: When they put the arum-lily plants into the ground : they have to support them; when they have taken root, they stand erect.
entries.meaning: The high position and honour of men often had humble beginnings.

entries.english: One says, "My things are destroyed" : and then he buys a waterpot (as if that could not be destroyed).
entries.meaning: Said of buying useless things.

entries.english: A bad lubaale-priest (medium) : brings abuse upon himself by the person who comes to consult him.

entries.luganda: Mmanya nnenda : nti abalenzi kaakano bazizza.
entries.english: If I had known that, I should have gone (to war) too (says one who has remained at home) : because now the boys bring them (i.e.
entries.meaning: many cows) back. Belated sorrow!

entries.english: (One who says) "I know all" (Mr.
entries.meaning: Know-all) is like a letter going round in the village.

entries.english: A heart that does not reflect : will speak a thoughtless word.

entries.luganda: Mmeeme ya munno ky'eyagala, naawe ky'oyagala : nga mwagalana.
entries.english: What the heart of your friend desires, you also desire : if you love each other.
Food must be paid for : the tenant has to go to the chief's place to put up the enclosure (and other work), in order to be left in peace on his own kibanja.
entries.meaning: If he does not work for the chief, he will be in trouble.

entries.english: (One who says) "There is plenty of food in the chief's place" : starves the chief.
entries.meaning: The chief tries to satisfy his people and might have nothing left for himself. - The mbuga is not a charitable institution!

entries.english: Food of inferior quality (muwogo, bulo etc.) does not leave you hungry.
entries.meaning: If you have no better, you will get your fill with that. - Also used to express thanks for something small.

entries.luganda: "Mmere yange enfudde ki?" : ye akuyita kaliira.
entries.english: "Why have I to lose my food?" (says the woman about the unwelcome visitor) : she calls you a glutton (who has come only to eat).
entries.meaning: Duta 67. 780 "Mmoneredde" : tata muze. (Even if one says) "I am sorry for it" : he does not alter his inclination.

entries.english: There is nothing that could not be treacherous : the dry banana-leaf singes the green one (although they are of the same mother).
entries.meaning: "How faithless all men are!" (Ps.116.11).

entries.luganda: Mpa magombe gazza : ng'embuzi eruma w'esula.
entries.english: The underworld gives nothing back : as it is with the goat that bites off the halter, where it spends the night.
entries.meaning: If it runs away, it will be eaten by the leopard; if it stays it will be eaten by the owner.

entries.english: One nut : pours out the (contents of the) basket.
entries.meaning: If one nut falls out of the basket on your head and you stoop down to pick it up, you might upset the whole basket. - Don't stand upon trifles, losing sight of big things! Engl. "Penny-wise : pound-foolish". The individual is sometimes the cause for the suffering of the community.

entries.english: Come here, I'll put a handle into you!
entries.meaning: Addressing a hoe which has lost its handle. - "Mpankuwange" is the name of a rocky unfertile place.

entries.luganda: Mpaawo atabukuttira : ne nnyazaala wo abukuttira.
entries.english: (bufumbo) There is nobody who could not destroy your marriage : even your mother-in-law can.
(mukwano) There is nobody who could not kill your friendship : even your mother can.

entries.luganda: Mpaawo kitakya : n'omusulo ku nsiko gukya.
entries.english: There is nothing that does not come to an end : even the dew on uncultivated land dries up.
entries.meaning: Used as general consolation in trouble.

entries.english: A demonstration of prowess does not (necessarily) include the legs : it does not prevent him from running away (when it comes to the proper fight).
A child given to somebody else to be brought up, dies in peace only at home.
entries.meaning: But if it dies at the home of the guardians, there will be trouble (suspicions, accusations).

entries.english: "I am forging a knife for the child" : (that means) it is bad workman-ship.
entries.meaning: It does not matter very much, as the knife is only a toy for the child.

entries.luganda: Mpiima teseera : omwoyo gwe guseera (or: mugabi ye aseera).
entries.english: It is not the knife that is cheating (in cutting the meat) : but the spirit (the divider, the man) is cheating.
"I sacrifice a feather" (i.e.
entries.meaning: that is all that I have). A poor man, who has been told to sacrifice a hen to the lubaale, says so, because he has no hen.

entries.english: I hear what is said : like the drum-beat of Nnyanzi.
entries.meaning: Nnyanzi is the head of the ssiga lya mbogo. Their drum-beat is "mpulira byo- gere". Lat. "Relata refero".

entries.luganda: Mpulukutu za musota : ziwulira na muggo.
entries.english: (= Mputtululu - - ) The ears of a snake : listen to a stick.
entries.meaning: Stubbornness is not overcome with sweet words. Germ. "Wer nicht horen will, muss fiihlen". Dutch "Een goede vader bespaart de roede niet".

entries.english: The eagle is a killer for others (kills for others).
entries.meaning: It lets its prey drop. - Reaping where others have sown.

entries.english: A simpleton : greets closed doors.
entries.meaning: He is visiting too often and is not welcome.

entries.luganda: Mu baana abangi (= mu bwana obungi) : timubula azza pnoma (= kalya ŋŋoma).
entries.english: Amongst many children : there is surely one who will become chief.
A thief pays with his (long) fingers.
entries.meaning: An honest man with his money.

entries.english: Although an ugly person catches the ants : still the beautiful ones eat them.
entries.meaning: He (or she) is good enough for helping (serving); afterwards they don't worry about him any longer.

entries.english: As bad as Nsanja.
entries.meaning: Nsanja was a chief of Buzu in Kyaggwe; he lived in the forest and cheated king Mwanga II. with ivory.

entries.english: In the meal (flour) there are always (unground) lumps.
entries.meaning: In every good thing there are flaws. Lat. "Nil perfecti sub sole".

entries.luganda: Muddo gwa luyiira : n'atalina mbuzi agwegomba.
entries.english: The green grass that grows after the burning : is looked forward to also by one who has no goat.
entries.meaning: Good weather for the farmer is also a benefit for the town's people.

entries.english: A slave is of more use than a wife.
entries.meaning: It was the duty of the slaves to carry the master's goods, when he went to war, and to go with him into battle and into death. A wife does not do that.

entries.english: A slave who is obedient : gives long life to his ears.
entries.meaning: If he disobeys, his ears will be cut off.

entries.luganda: Muddu talwewa : aluwa mukama we, nti omwami enkya anaagenda ku kibuga?
entries.english: (lusa) The slave does not give himself permission for a journey : it is his master who gives it, when the slave asks: Is the master going to town to-morrow?

entries.luganda: Mufumbya-gganda : tabalirira mutyabi (= tabalira basennya, = tasaasira bazaala).
entries.english: One who uses a big bundle of firewood for cooking : has no consideration for one who has to gather the firewood.
entries.meaning: One who does not work himself, does not understand how hard it is. Mufumbya- gganda is one of the many titles of the King, and expresses "hardness" or "cruelty". The king used to kill plenty of people, without considering the parents.

entries.english: A rich man possessing his riches : is told pleasant things.
(or: Muganda w'asula.) Where there is a Muganda there is trouble.
entries.meaning: Self-reproach! We Baganda are bad!

entries.english: A witchdoctor does not treat himself (goes to another o ne).
entries.meaning: Otherwise he might never be sick or die. - Lat. "Medice cura teipsum!" M.531, Duta 386, Kag.99.

entries.english: When the favourite woman commits a fault : you, the despised one, rejoice.
entries.meaning: Malicious joy at another person's misfortune.

entries.luganda: Mugenda mulimbagana : nga muli balungi beereere.
entries.english: You will go on entertaining each other : if all of you are of peaceful mind.
entries.meaning: But if a quarrelsome, evil-minded person is amongst you, you won't.

entries.luganda: Mugenyi amanya lijja : nga wa nsumika mbi.
entries.english: If a visitor knows (only) the way (ekkubo) on which he came : he is badly dressed.
entries.meaning: He does not want to lead, when leaving and says: I don't know the way, because then all those behind him would laugh at him.

entries.english: A scandal-monger does not make you richer (akumalamu ekitiibwa).
An oarsman does not gnaw a bone (because he has to handle the oars).
entries.meaning: One who has a responsible job, should not busy himself with things distracting him from the work.

entries.english: One who is inclined to rob : is he not also inclined to be quick?
A trouble bringer : does not take it away.
entries.meaning: It is easier to cause harm than to make it good again.

entries.english: You make a lot of noise : like people who drive lambs (sheep) across the river.

entries.luganda: Mukadde taseka : nga talabise amunyumiza binyuma (= nga tasanze amunyo- nyogera, = nga wabuze amunyonyogera).
entries.english: An old man does not laugh : if there is nobody to entertain him with interesting (spicy) news (if there is nobody who tickles him).

entries.luganda: "Muka Jita : muka Kasirye" (or: Baka Jita : baka Kasirye).
entries.english: "Descendant(s) of Jita : descendant(s) of Kasirye".
entries.meaning: Used as welcome-greeting between the descendants of Jita and Kasirye, the sons of Gunju, head of the butiko-clan (Mawokota - Busiro).

entries.english: A widow : will not fail to praise her deceased husband (in the presence of her new husband, he has given me so many clothes etc.).
"My daughter-in-law has no respect for me" : (so complains the husband's mother) if her child is a chief.
entries.meaning: As a chief's wife she thinks herself superior.

entries.english: A potter's wife : eats out of a potsherd.
entries.meaning: "Shoemakers are the worst shod".

entries.english: The (imaginary) wife of a bachelor has no ears; (because he often says: "If such and such a woman were mine) wouldn't I cut her ears off (for infidelity)?" 43.11, Ssal.p.33.
(amatu) The (imaginary) wife of a bachelor : has not (only) two ears.
entries.meaning: Because he brags so often about cutting her ears off, that she must have any amount of them.

entries.english: A poor man's wife is not looked for except at his home (poverty does not separate the wife from her husband).
entries.meaning: Or: They do not look for a poor man's wife (to ask anything from her; because she has nothing).

entries.english: A woman gets strength from her hoe.
entries.meaning: So says a sickly woman (but industrious), working in spite of her weakness.

entries.luganda: Mukazi muggya : kabugo kakadde; tekabulamu nsekere.
entries.english: A concubine is like an old barkcloth (blanket) : undoubtedly there will be lice in it.
entries.meaning: There is always jealousy between the concubines.

entries.english: (also: Ssenkukirenkukire - - ) Try to be better, always better : a woman with a "lubuto" is worth more than one with dropsy.
"My brother-in-law (or contestant, friend, opponent) is not getting away from me" : (this statement is true) if both of you are equally quick.
entries.meaning: Used for any competition in sport, commerce etc. Both are equally strong.

entries.luganda: "Mukome wano, tweyanguye" : ng'omugenyi anaakyama (= akwatiddwa bubi).
entries.english: "Now let us hurry, turn back" : says the visitor (who has been accompanied on the road), if he is in a hurry to relieve himself.
As long as the husband is alive : the wife cannot marry (another).
entries.meaning: The husband might claim her. - Stolen or robbed things can never be possessed in peace.

entries.luganda: Muka omutabaazi : bw'aleka ekkata si bw'alisanga.
entries.english: The wife of a warrior (really the warrior himself) : does not find his headpad (enkata = his wife), as he left it.
entries.meaning: During the absence of the husband the wife misbehaves - dances - men - etc.

entries.english: The wife of a fearless husband : can only be taken away, when he is not at home.
If you have been able just to roast the meat (and raiders come upon you), the boiled meat is not eaten by you.
entries.meaning: If you have only just started a thing and you are interrupted, you won't be able to finish.

entries.english: It is the master himself, who destroys his home.
entries.meaning: "Mukulu-atta-maka-ge" was the name of King Mwanga's kibuga at Mmengo. - Bw'akola obubi, atta maka ge; bw'akola obulungi era alongoosa maka ge.

entries.luganda: "Mukulu ndimutuma ki?" : yeerabira ogw'okumufulumya ebweru ekiro.
entries.english: "What could I ask my father to do for me?" : a child (being at a loss like that) forgets to ask to be taken out at night.
entries.meaning: "Ssebo, njagala kugenda bweru".

entries.luganda: "Mukulu ne mukulu munne" : nga kwa njala.
entries.english: "An old man and his old friend" : must help each other in time of famine.
entries.meaning: If one is in need and knows that his friend has something, he goes to him and uses this saying.

entries.luganda: Mukulu talya nkanja : nga kwa kyengera.
entries.english: The master does not eat the dregs (of the beer) (as the women and the children do) : if it happens to be the season of plenty.
(A man who says) "A master does not carry loads" : becomes lazy.

entries.luganda: Mukungubazi bonna bwe badduka ye ng'asigalawo.
entries.english: He is a brave man : that holds out, when all the others run away.
"It is my brother-in-law, whom they talk evil of" : (says the woman) and cooks for him with ash-salt (she ought to use better salt (ogw'ensero) to show her attachment).
As long as one is alive : one can get things again.
entries.meaning: Expression used when one has been robbed of his property.

entries.luganda: Mulekere ddala katta-buteme si wa kuta nsiriba.
entries.english: Stop altogether : the katta-buteme (kind of sedge-grass) does not give up its "nsiriba" (little tubercles at the end of its roots).
entries.meaning: Referring to stubborn self-willed people. Same as: tajja kuta muze!

entries.english: The flute of king Ssuuna : is being played incessantly.
entries.meaning: Said of interminably repeated things, sayings, songs. Never stopping.

entries.english: A liar cannot bring up children (they cannot trust him).

entries.luganda: Mulumbaganyi ng'empalaata y'embuzi : okuleka omutwe ng'ekwata amaviivi.
entries.english: An intruder (taking the wrong place) is like the baldness on a goat : leaving the head alone and settling on the knees.
(Although) a beautiful woman leaves you : hunger does not befall you.
entries.meaning: You can get another one to cook for you.

entries.english: A beautiful person who stays with you a long time : loses her charms.
Even a beautiful person makes you come to help with reluctance (if you are not well, bulwadde bubi, impeded walk etc.).
"A beautiful woman will not defy me" : (bragging like that) will result in skulls on the road.
entries.meaning: One saying so and attempting to get everything he covets (money, clothes, women) will use force and there will be fighting and deaths.

entries.english: A sick person picking at his (her) food : makes the healthy ones fat.
"The sick (child, husband etc.) gave me a lot of worries" : (so you say) if you look upon him (i.e.
entries.meaning: if you managed to nurse him back to life and health). Satisfaction after successful efforts.

entries.english: A man who eats in the dark : sees trouble in the evening.
entries.meaning: If he is busy with other things until evening, he has to start cooking, when it gets dark.

entries.english: In trying to knock down the mpafu (Uganda plum) there is no preference (special treatment) for a prince.

entries.luganda: Mumpi w'akoma w'akwata : ensolosozi eruma atudde.
entries.english: A short man grips as far as he reaches : the ensolosozi (poisonous ant) bites one who is sitting on the ground.
entries.meaning: Honest endeavour deserves appreciation and help. Lat. "Ut desint vires, tamen est laudanda voluntas" (Ovid). French "On fait comme on peut".

entries.english: A lazy woman brings forth dogs : an industrious one princes.
entries.meaning: The industrious tiller says: my "princes" here do not eat menvu; whereupon the lazy one says: give them to me, I'll take them home for my "dogs". The children of the industrious woman have plenty of other food; the children of the lazy one are always hungry as dogs.

entries.luganda: Munafu azaala mumbowa : "ettooke lino walirya n'ani?"; kasajja akukutte envuba.
entries.english: A lazy woman brings forth an executioner : "with whom have you eaten this banana-bunch (which was hanging nearby)?"; your little boy is putting the blame on you.
entries.meaning: The man comes home and sees that a nearby-bunch has disappeared, whilst a far-off-one that should have been taken first, is still hanging. The kasajja (little boy) of the lazy woman has given his mother away (akukutte envuba = akuta- ddeko omusango). "Okukwata envuba" is the work of an executioner (mumbo- wa). Play on words!

entries.english: One in distress is like a rat : it is trapped by a tasty thing.
entries.meaning: You win him by giving him something he likes.

entries.english: A great number causes respect (fear).
entries.meaning: Armies, public opinions etc. There is power in numbers.

entries.english: Out of crooked things develop straight things.
entries.meaning: Do not ridicule the work of beginners! Positive criticism and advice! "April showers bring May flowers". Lat. "Experientia docet".

entries.english: My friend, you finish off the hair on my head.
entries.meaning: Expression of astonishment, surprise (over good or bad things).

entries.luganda: Munno atunda : nti "nze ngula"; nti ekimutunza okimanyi?
entries.english: If your neighbour sells something and you say (quickly) "I shall buy it"; do you know what makes him sell the thing?
entries.meaning: Be careful in buying secondhand-things!

entries.luganda: Munno mu kabi : ye munno ddala.
entries.english: A friend in need : is a friend indeed.

entries.luganda: Munnyu gwa vvu : bw'obulwa amazzi tolya.
entries.english: If you have ash-salt, but no water : you won't eat.
entries.meaning: Without water you cannot wash out the ashes in the lusoggo (funnel). If you have no wood, how can you build? If you have paper, but no pencil, how can you write?

entries.english: In the house there is no road.
entries.meaning: The house is not the same as the road. If somebody comes to your house, you have to treat him as a guest; on the road you can pass him by.

entries.luganda: Mu nnyumba timubula mukadde : enkoko eyingira ekootakoota.
entries.english: There is always an old one in a house : the hen goes in stooping.

entries.luganda: Musajja alumbwa : bw'ogenda okumulumba ogenda weenywezezza.
entries.english: A (fearless) man is attacked : when you are going to attack him, you go pre-pared.
(or: Omusajja - - ) A man is happy, if he has his own home.
A man is like (native) potatoes : he grows up on a rope.
entries.meaning: Whenever a boy or a man has committed a crime (stealing etc.), they tie him up and bring him to the chief. A woman is never bound with a rope.

entries.luganda: Musajja munno lukolokolo : olusika nalwo lukusika.
entries.english: Your man-friend is like a "lukolokolo" (tough thorny creeper) : (you get entangled and) you pull it and it pulls you.

entries.luganda: Musajja tabula : bw'olaba abuze, nga basse mutte.
entries.english: A (courageous) man does not simply disappear if you see that he has disappeared, they have killed him.
As a man grows up : he has to go through many a hardship (warnings, re-proaches, disappointments, punishment etc.).
The fault of the cooking pot is mentioned even before a visitor.
entries.meaning: If the wife has only a cracked cooking pot and she is told by her husband: "Fumbira omugenyi oyo", she will answer: "Ssebo sirina ntamu" or "egaanyi okuyiisa", it is cracked underneath. That is spoken of even in front of a visitor, whilst other family affairs are not easily revealed.

entries.english: A new tenant is not soon reproached.
entries.meaning: He does not know the local customs yet.

entries.luganda: Musira-nnumbu : tabaliriza zigwa mu mazzi (or: tabaliriza zigenda).
entries.english: He who washes (rubs) the nnumbu (= very tasty ingredients for meat etc.) : does not count the pieces which fall back into the water.
entries.meaning: He has plenty. Army leaders sending soldiers into battle. "Nnumbu" is a kind of yam (igname), like "ntanganwuzi" (ginger).

entries.english: An Earthquake is a shaker of the heavens (terrific power).
You have met each other : (namely) one who is afraid to join the army and marries a lazy woman.
entries.meaning: The two fit well together: the man is afraid to go into battle and the woman is afraid of the work in the field.

entries.english: The brewer does not eat the dregs (of mubisi).
entries.meaning: One who is at the source (well), does not drink dirty water. Rub.C.1189. 2945 Mussa mukka nga makondeere : sso tigaagalana. (cf. Abakondeere: 0020) You blow together like trumpets : although they don't like each other. The same work, but different spirit. Rub.C.1789. 2946 Mutabaazi gw'amanyi : gw'akuba engabo. (cf. Omutabaazi gw'amanyi: 4333) M.550.

entries.english: A quick, efficient worker (one who does not linger, especially a smith).
You fall into a trap in the mweso-game : whilst you see it.
entries.meaning: Your opponent puts the "mpiki" (seeds) into the winning field, whilst you see him doing it. Warning against running into disaster with open eyes!

entries.luganda: Muti gwa nnanga : ogukuba amabega, gtunala gwogera obulungi.
entries.english: You turn the (curved) stick of the (native) harp with its back towards the court (chief) : and still it sounds beautiful.
A small child talks with his small friend.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Simile simili gaudet". Germ. "Gleich and gleich gesellt sich gern".

entries.luganda: Mutongole mbuzi : zirundibwa wa kamwa; bw'otomugamba okujja okukola tajja.
entries.english: A free citizen is like a goat : they are herded by one with an authoritative voice; if you don't tell him to come for work, he does not come.

entries.luganda: Mutongole ngabi : ye eyitira ginnaayo ababi.
entries.english: A little chief is like a bushbuck : that - by nervous coughing - calls the enemies (hunters) upon the other ngabi (in hiding).
entries.meaning: The chief - by defending himself - gets others into trouble. People often get their friend into trouble unintentionally.

entries.english: A sub-chief should not give away part of his lusuku.
entries.meaning: If he does so (because the petitioner is an influential person), he will lose his whole lusuku.

entries.english: A second-hand-dealer : does not sell things on credit.
entries.meaning: Old things might perish, before the debt is paid.

entries.english: The head is hoaxing (people) : (one says e.g.) "I have dreamt that my dead father has come back".
entries.meaning: People imagine many things.

entries.english: One who has reserved things for himself without paying for them : has not bought them.
entries.meaning: Therefore they will be sold to one who pays.

entries.english: One who is talkative on the road : at home he does not talk.
entries.meaning: People often show different behaviour at home and outside. "Ngira" is old Luganda.

entries.english: (One who tries to bargain in buying, says) "I have little money", (showing it at the same time) : (also when) you eat beans, you show them (hold them in your open hands).
"Cassava is bitter" : is bitter fol.
entries.meaning: one who has had enough food. One who is hungry, will eat it all the same.

entries.english: A hungry fellow is clamouring for food.
entries.meaning: When he is satisfied, he will stop shouting.

entries.english: A wanderer (vagabond) has no home.
The hunter exaggerates the size of the "bottle bird".
entries.meaning: Tall hunters' stories! Germ. "Jager-Latein". "You should have seen the one that got away!" - "Ettutuma" is the coucal, the size of an ejjibwa.

entries.english: The difficult one brings forth a cock.
entries.meaning: This is the name of Mukaabya Milteesa's house at Kasubi (his and his son Mwa-nga's burial place). - The king is the cock, the subjects are the hens.

entries.english: (= Muzibu okulaba - - ) He is not easily recognized : like one who scratches himself, whilst running away.
entries.meaning: If he would walk ordinarily, his gait would give him away.

entries.english: It was the grandson who killed (Bwakamba) Mukudde.
entries.meaning: Mukudde was an extremely cruel chief of the Banyoro in Buddu, before Jjunju, the Baganda-king, conquered it. - Cruelty alienates everybody, even the nearest relations.

entries.english: One who loves with half a will (only) : as the Muyima loves semsem.
entries.meaning: He likes to eat it, but not to the extent of planting it. He does not acquire land to plant it.

entries.luganda: Mwami akwagala : ye akuzimbya ne ku lwazi.
entries.english: A chief who loves you : makes you build your house on rock (unfertile ground).
entries.meaning: Because that means that you can fetch the food at the chief's place, if you have none. - You consider the favour of the chief more important than the fertility of your kibanja.

entries.english: A chief brings forth banana plants (not men).
entries.meaning: If a tenant does not deliver his dues, he has to leave, and another one is put on the kibanja to supply the chief with the produce thereof.

entries.luganda: "Mwami ndimutuma ki?" : bamukwatira mitala wa mugga (= musango gw'emi-tala), nti bayite omwami, ajje anzirukire.
entries.english: (One asks) "What shall I ask the chief to do for me?" : when they catch him on the other side of the river, committing an offence, he can ask: let them call my chief to come and rescue me.

entries.luganda: "Mwami, olidde kya nsonga" : bw'avaawo akuyita "ssikabindi" (= ssika mild-ndi).
entries.english: (The condemned person says) "Chief, you have inflicted a just fine" : but when he goes away, he calls you a "robber".
"The chief is on my side" (I am his favourite) : (one saying so) will take liberties and finally get into trouble in court.
One who wants to bring up a child : needs medicine.
entries.meaning: Great infant mortality! - Perhaps the expression "okuwona" for child delivery is in connection with this.

entries.luganda: Mwana ggwe, oli kasobeza : ng'omwana awoowooterwa nnyina.
entries.english: Child, you are perplexing (beyond me) : like a (crying) child that the mother tries vainly to appease.
A strong healthy child : is already strong, when carried in the cloth on the back of the mother.
entries.meaning: French "Tel pore, tel fill".

entries.luganda: Mwana muwala mutuba : atagusimba ye asubula.
entries.english: A girl-child is like a mutuba-tree (fig-tree) : the one who did not plant, gets the profit.
entries.meaning: The parents (fathers) often die, before the girl gets married. Others receive the dowry. "Asiga aba mulala, n'akungula aba mulala" (Jo.4.37).

entries.luganda: "Mwana na mwana" : ng'omu tannakuba munne lubale.
entries.english: "They are children" : (so you say) as long as one has not yet wounded the other on the head.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Principiis obsta!" "Sunt pueri pueri; pueri puerilia tractant".

entries.luganda: Mwana omu : 1) ajjula bijogo; 2) alinga ekire ky'enkuba ekimu.
entries.english: The only child : 1) has plenty of ornaments (they heap presents on it); 2) is like a single rain-cloud.
entries.meaning: When the cloud has emptied itself, the weather will be as hot and dry as before. When such a child dies, there is emptiness again in the family.

entries.luganda: Mwana wa munywanyi wange tagenda butalya : bye biwanga ebiri e Kitta-nte.
entries.english: The child of my blood brother shall not go away hungry : (so says one who has no food to offer; he goes and steals therefore bananas) that means skulls at Kitta-nte (the slaughter-place of the king).
entries.meaning: He will be caught and killed in the act.

entries.luganda: Mwana wange, mbagambira abali wansi, abali waggulu bawulira.
entries.english: My child (my dear fellow), I tell them, those who are below and those who are above hear it.
entries.meaning: Two enemies go to the same lubaale-man: each one to get his help against the other. The one who came first, sees the second one coming and hides on the kibanyi (banana-rack). Whilst the second one sits in the hut, the millubaale speaks above mysterious words, referring to both enemies, trying to reconciliate them.

entries.luganda: Mwana wange, nkubuulira : ejugumba n'emala ekona.
entries.english: My child, I am telling you : the food is bubbling and still it remains underdone.
entries.meaning: You are too hasty; what you are saying or doing, requires deliberation.

entries.english: My child, you are putting me on the carpet (where evil-minded people speak against me).
entries.meaning: You are putting me to shame before the people.

entries.english: The young of a cockroach does not die from smoke.
