A great eater won't fail to have somebody else eating with him (i.e.
entries.meaning: the hunger and the head eat with him and emaciate him). Whilst the body gets thinner, the head always retains its size. Duta 229, Duta 1545. 5299 W'ennyimba-mbi - - (cf. Ow'ennyimba mbi: 4667) Duta 307.

entries.english: You are exaggerating like one who eats small (unripe) matooke.
entries.meaning: Saying: we eat "go bisisa", which has two meanings: either "unripe matooke" or "caterpillar". Reply: and we eat "ssekesa" (centipedes).

entries.english: You are flattering yourself (you are an optimist) like the woman bringing forth a fat stumpy child (and saying: when its stomach straightens out, it will be taller).

entries.luganda: Weenyumiriza (= weenyumiikiriza) : ng'olugunju olw'ettulu, nti nnannyini nkoko kata mmuleete!
entries.english: You are bragging : like a one-eyed mongoose, (saying) I nearly brought the owner of the hen also (not only the hen).

entries.luganda: Weetaaganya : ng'omugenge alaga ennaku; nti nnamalawo zino!
entries.english: You take useless trouble : like a leper indicating the number of days (counting and showing his stump of a hand); it is so many days since - -Having no fingers he can't indicate numbers.
You go to useless trouble : like an underdone potato.
entries.meaning: Such a potato has undergone the cooking process and is still hard. As people also eat raw potatoes, it could have saved itself the cooking.

entries.english: You care about something that does not care about yoU : wind does not move the ear.
You act on your own initiative : like an habitually crying child.
entries.meaning: Nobody and notking else is to be blamed.

entries.luganda: We twava emmanju nga kiwedde : musale wa matu.
entries.english: When we came from the back of the house, all was finished : (says the) fellow whose ears were cut off.
entries.meaning: He does not want to say that he had his ears cut off for stealing.

entries.english: (The man who shouts to the enemy) "We are as strong as that", calls the killers upon himself.
entries.meaning: He gives information to the enemy.

entries.luganda: Weetyabidde za kukwokya : kijja-na-nnenge ku kkubo.
entries.english: You have collected firewood with which you will burn yourself, as a "kijja-na-nnenge" (baby born feet first) on the road.
entries.meaning: When such a child was buried, they heaped firewood on its grave and the next grassfire burnt it and the corpse. Duta 1328. 5330 Weewanise : ng'ow'ekiwaama azaalira mu Bayima. You are presumptuous like a (Muganda) woman with withered breasts, who brings forth in the land of the Bahima. When she wants to go home to Buganda, there will be no milk to feed her child.

entries.luganda: Weewanise ng'omuwazi : bw'akakana ng'ali ku za birenge ; bw'aba awala asooka mutwe n'alyoka addira ebirenge.
entries.english: You are acting obstinately in your own way : like a dresser of skins, starting from the ends; a dresser starts from the head of the skin and then works towards the ends.
You are aiming too high (you are daring) : like the little bird that is breeding high up in a nkanaga (thorn-tree).
entries.meaning: The hawk will see it.

entries.luganda: Weewulira nga kassukussuku : kajjira mu kibondo ate keetikka ssanja.
entries.english: You are self-conceited like a kassukussuku (kind of mushroom) : it grows in a sack and carries dry plantain leaves on its head.
entries.meaning: Other mushrooms break the soil in their growth; but the kassukussuku grows above ground and carries dry plantain leaves - to boast of its strength.

entries.luganda: Weewulira nga nkoko : eyagifuna akuba nsindirirwa nga yo ekuba muzinga.
entries.english: You are conceited like a hen : its owner charges (the gun with) powder and the hen fires the gun.
entries.meaning: "Kukuba muzinga" has two meanings: "to fire a gun" and "to grow a rump" (the sickly growth on the extremity of a chicken's backbone - a peculiarity imported into Buganda mu "Mikaabya").

entries.luganda: Weewulira nga nkoko : eyagifuna asula wansi mu nkukunyi, yo ng'ebeera waggulu.
entries.english: You are as overbearing as a hen : its owner sleeps below among the fleas and it sleeps on top (on the laths of the hen-roost).

entries.luganda: Weewulira ng'omubumbi : enju asulamu etonnya, ng'essubi ayokya lukumi.
entries.english: You are as silly as a potter : the house he lives in is leaking and (in his courtyard) he burns grass by the heaps.
entries.meaning: Sarcasm on one who neglects the important things for the sake of trifles.

entries.english: You are doing a risky thing : like one who dances in poor clothing.
entries.meaning: If the clothing tears, he is put to shame.

entries.english: (The importunate petitioner urging you to) "search for what I asked you" will make you steal in your own house.
entries.meaning: Having nothing at hand of your own, you take the "mmwanyi" of a member of the household.

entries.english: You are rolling downhill : like a short stumpy person walking down to Masinga (Busiro?).
entries.meaning: Jumpy gait, popping up and down while walking. Rub.C.1346. 5345 Weeyinudde : nga wa nsimbu atabaala; bwe zfrikukwata mu lutabaalo! (cf. Wee-sigudde ng'omusimbu: 5313) Rub.C.680.

entries.luganda: Weeyinula : ng'omunaku avuma amagufa; nti ggwe bwe banaagakuddiza too-kaabe?
entries.english: (or: nti owuwo waali?) (cf.
entries.meaning: Kye nkola bannange: 2514) You are insulting yourself : like the man who has lost his own mother and abuses others about their own dead mother ("nnyoko!"); if they return the insult, will you not lament? (or: is your mother still alive?) Duta 996, M.938, L.73, Ssal.p.36.

entries.english: You are parading up and down like an executioner after shaving his hair.
entries.meaning: He wants to create a good and friendly expression.

entries.english: You are boasting like a woman who has cooked food without vegetables.

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza : ng'afumbye ekikongo, nti lyako ebibiriridde!
entries.english: You are exaggerating : like a woman who has cooked kikongo (kind of yam) and says: eat it, it is soft (soaked with water.) Reply: Will a stone in the lake ever soften with all the water round it?
You are exaggerating : like a man who wants to frighten you away from the chief's place (by saying: he is raving mad today etc.).

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza nga anaakoola omuddo; nti ka nnende nkoole entungo; kazzi ali ku muddo.
entries.english: You are talking like one about to start weeding, and saying: I am going to weed out the semsem, although he means to weed out the weeds.

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza nga asibiikirira embuzi : nti aliba omulamu alirya wa ku nnyama?
entries.english: You are talking (to yourself), like a man who ties up a goat in the grass (saying) Where should one get meat to eat (with all the misery about)?
entries.meaning: Reply: Is what you tie up there not meat? - Unnecessary worries.

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza ng'ekitaalimye : nti baaba (or mulamu) vaayo nfumbe.
entries.english: You are overbearing like a (lazy) fellow who has not worked in the field and says to his sister-in-law: "move away and let me cook".
entries.meaning: Reply of the woman: Awo weebeerera wano obw'enkya ekyakulobedde oku-fumba kiki? You have been here all morning (doing nothing); why did you not cook then? Duta 231, M.940, Rub.C.895. 5354 Weeyogeza ng'olwanobako : nti ewa bbaze nnali muganzi; nti ekyakuggyako ki? You are talking like a miserable woman, saying: "I was favourite with my husband"; (reply) what then removed you from there?

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza ng'olwanoba luzadde : nti taba mwana wange, sandizze.
entries.english: You are talking like a woman who has run away (from her husband) after having had a child and said: if it had not been for the child, I should not have come.
entries.meaning: Reply: Has your child become your husband now?

entries.luganda: Weeyogeza ng'omukazi agamba, nti olusuku Iwange lundaluseeko.
entries.english: You are talking like a woman, saying: My bananary has made me mad.
entries.meaning: Reply: In that case you will have to put your bitooke into the stocks.

entries.english: You bring forth for yourself what will kill you : as is the case with the young shoot of the banana tree.
entries.meaning: When the young plant is big enough, they cut the old down. - Fate of the aged! Germ. "Die Geister, die ich rief, die werd' ich nicht mehr los".

entries.luganda: W'ofunira ebingi : nga kitaawo ne nnyoko tebakyaliwo (= baafa dda).
entries.english: Where you have plenty : your father and your mother are no longer there.
entries.meaning: You cannot be grateful enough to your parents. 52.59. 5365 W'ogerera ekkubo : si we liba. Where you guess the path to be : it might not be at all. One man's judgement is not reliable.

entries.luganda: W'oligwa nange we ndigwa : bwe bafa tebaziikibwa wamu.
entries.english: "Where you will fall, I, also, shall fall" : (says he, but) when they die, they are not buried together.
entries.meaning: Not all is eaten as hot as it is cooked. - Promises and predictions are not always fulfilled.

entries.luganda: W'olimalira omulimo ogwo : nga eza Nnakakedde luwe.
entries.english: By the time you will have finished that job, the hair of a clean-shaven person will have grown into "Iuwe" (hair of about 5mm) (i.e.
entries.meaning: you are very slow!).

entries.luganda: W'olumira ku ly'ogenda okukoza : ng'ekiri munda kikuli bulungi?
entries.english: Where you bite the ttooke before dipping it into the sauce, (they might ask you) does what is inside you (i.e.
entries.meaning: the hunger) give you no peace? Bad manners at table!

entries.english: (= Ow'omubiri - ) One who does harm to his body : does it to himself.
(= Ow'omugongo - - ) One who shows no energy (has no persistency) : will not get anything from the Mugolooba.
entries.meaning: Or: One who is not a favourite : will not get anything from the Mugolooba. Mugolooba was the name of a chief in Bulemeezi (district Kigolooba), who was a difficult man to obtain favour from.

entries.english: (= Ow'omwana - - ) Every one knows and loves his own child (more than he loves others).
entries.meaning: Also said of one's home and country.

entries.english: "Wherever you meet me, you can settle your business!" : one who speaks like this deprives himself of friends (relations).
entries.meaning: He does not like people to visit him.

entries.luganda: W'osanga enkofu : tosangawo Where you find guinea-fowl : you don't find a stone (to hit them with).
entries.english: Being at a loss in a case of emergency!

entries.luganda: W'osuula engabo : obulwa (= olutabaalo) we bukoma.
entries.english: Where you throw the shield away : there the fighting stops.
entries.meaning: You give up too early! Hold out a little longer and you are victorious with your comrades! Lack of perseverance! Lat. "Finis coronat opus".

entries.english: Where you have never yet called : there (you imagine) they have lunch.
entries.meaning: Good things are always where you happen not to be.

entries.english: (or: W'otoyitidde : we wataggwa mawolu.) Where you did not visit : (you imagine) there will be (plenty of) food laid by.
entries.meaning: The good things are always where we are not.

entries.english: A place you have not left yet (your kibanja) : do not let it fall into disorder (do not soil it)!
entries.meaning: You might decide to stay and would have to restore order.

entries.english: You like to go back to a place, where you had no complaint.
He has come in an envelope (official death notice) like a soldier (who has died in the war).
He stopped at the brink of the abyss (i.e.
entries.meaning: he was in proximate danger of a great evil).

entries.luganda: Yakubbye : ate gw'obuulira, nti mwana wattu, ndabye, ababbi banzibye.
entries.english: (= Eyakubbye - - ) To the man who has been stealing from you, you say: my dear, I have had bad luck; thieves have stolen from me (i.e.
entries.meaning: those who come to express their compas-sion, might be the very thieves).

entries.english: He has taken good care : to steal a hen and bananas (at the same time).
entries.meaning: If he had taken only bananas, he would have had to steal once more to have "mmere" with "enva".

entries.english: He sleeps (lies there) like an overripe fruit : like a lazy man to whom you have given your bed.
He changes colour like a chameleon from Bulemeezi.
He is puffed up with pride : like Nsodo.
entries.meaning: Nsodo was a tall man of Gayaaza who, in his vanity, wound a cloth round his head according to the fashion of the Indians (sheiks), and appeared so in court. King Mwanga ordered his ears to be cut off. (Kyaddondo) 25,185. 5398 Yeekabaggula : ng'omunafu alima awagonda. (= Yeekabattula - - ) He pretends to be working hard : like a lazy person hoeing on soft ground.

entries.english: (okuta = okuziika) She enjoys freedom : like a hated (neglected) woman who comes from the burial of the favourite (woman).

entries.luganda: "Ye muto" : "mukulu we gy'agenze, ba nda emu".
entries.english: "She is still a child" (so the parent laments, whose daughter has gone away from home) : (another consoles him or her, saying) "she has only gone to her elder (married) sister, (don't worry) they are from the same womb".
He stretches himself : like a night dancer eating stolen bananas.
He puts on tendrils : like those of the pumpkin (to climb higher).
entries.meaning: Said of somebody who is too ambitious.

entries.luganda: Ye wa maddu : akujjuza emmere embisi.
entries.english: (also: Ow'amaddu ) His appetite is too impetuous : he makes you serve half-cooked food.
entries.meaning: Said of a man who cannot wait, till his wife has cooked properly.

entries.luganda: Yeewulira nga kigenge : kyakajja ku mubiri nga kikuba embuga.
entries.english: He is very self-assured, like leprosy : it has only just settled on the body and builds up a chief's enclosure (patches on the skin!).

entries.luganda: Yeewulira nga mulwadde : tannava ku ndiri, nti kaakati nneewulira.
entries.english: He trusts himself too much, like a sick man : he has not yet got up from his bed and says: now I feel strong.
He is boasting (he is pretentious) like a miserable woman who has left her hus-band and demands: "Let them bring beer and fetch me".
entries.meaning: Reply: When he first married you, did he bring milk or water?

entries.english: He has burnt his tail (like the dog on the fire place) : (that means) he has nothing to sit upon (i.e.
entries.meaning: he has spoiled his chance, burnt his boats, broken his bridges).

entries.english: Pass through the bananary, like a child of the household.
"Oh, these are boy-fights" (says a man) who has one of his own boys among them.
The woman who says: "misery has befallen me", will (stay and) die in her married state (endurance); if she says: "I cannot bear it", she leaves (her hus-band).
Trouble met us together (he says) : but when he becomes rich, he does not give you anything.
entries.meaning: Lat. "Verba, verba, praeterea nihil". - Engl. "A friend in need is a friend indeed".

entries.english: The endaggu-tubers (kind of yam) cause "rising up in the throat" : (one who says so), uproots them all the same (and eats them).
Real trouble comes upon you, where you cannot escape.

entries.luganda: Zikulaga emirirnu : abajja miyini (or: atunda omugavu).
entries.english: Necessity teaches you to work (says the poor man and) he makes hoe-handles (or: he sells the mugavu-tree).
You have failed : as Ntambi failed at Lubya.
entries.meaning: "Ntambi" (ow'enjovu) was the uncle and confidant of King Kagulu Tibucwereke; but he had to flee and he took refuge on Lubya-island.

entries.english: (One who says in a conciliatory mood) "You have seen trouble" : does not kill his enemy.
(One who tells you) "Build a big house" : does not help you to build it.
entries.meaning: It is easier to give an order or advice than to carry it out.

entries.luganda: Zinaakalira mu kkubo : teyekkaanya agafumbye bw'afaanana.
entries.english: (ngalo) (A man who says: my wet hands) will get dry on the road (having washed them after the meal and leaving quickly) : does not look at the host who has cooked the food for him.
entries.meaning: He leaves quickly hoping to find more food somewhere else.

entries.english: Misery is the lot of the one who is born.
"(The money spent in buying beer-bananas) will come in again in selling beer" : (one calculating like that) forgets (possible) bad beer (which won't sell).
The drums may be cut from the same tree : but their sounds are different.
entries.meaning: Said of people in the same house or of children of the same family.

entries.english: The days you announce to a good man (friend) (that you will visit him) : come soon.
entries.meaning: Looking forward with joy. Pleasant things one expects do not tire one out.

entries.english: The days you fix for a debtor (to pay back the debt) : will come soon (for him).
